subject: AHS
title: Introduction to Art and Psychology
description: Explores the intersection of art and psychology. Examines how artists use techniques to manipulate visual perception and elicit emotional responses. Includes how psychological theories can illuminate the understanding of artistic expression. Cross-listed with PSYC 050.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of freshman, or sophomore; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: World Art: Images, Issues, and Ideas
description: An introduction to artistic achievements of the world’s cultures and ways in which they can be viewed. Considers such issues as the use of artworks as historical documents; connections between “high art” and popular culture; and the relationship between artist, viewer, artistic tradition, and society.

subject: AHS
title: Modern Western Visual Culture
description: Focuses on broadly defined cultural practices in relation to painting, photography, video, architecture, and film. Introduces historical, aesthetic, and theoretical issues in twentieth-century visual culture, emphasizing political and social themes relevant to contemporary life.

subject: AHS
title: Topics in Art History
description: Explores significant themes and topics from the history of art and architecture around the world. Concentrates on particular subtopics to be announced in the Schedule of Classes. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 24 units.

subject: AHS
title: Topics in Art and Architectural History
description: Explores significant themes and topics from the history of art and architecture around the world. Concentrates on particular subtopics to be announced in the Schedule of Classes. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 24 units. Credit is awarded for one of the following AHS 010S or AHS 010.

subject: AHS
title: Arts and Architecture of the Islamic World
description: A survey of the major monuments and themes of the visual arts in the Middle East, North Africa, South Asia, and Spain, from the rise of Islam to present day.

subject: AHS
title: Arts of Asia
description: A survey of the major monuments and themes of the visual arts of India, China, and Japan. Topics include recent archaeological discoveries, Buddhist art, Hindu sculpture and architecture, Zen in art, and the development of Asian pictorial art.

subject: AHS
title: Introduction to the Body in Western Art
description: Introduces questions of the human body and how it was depicted and interpreted in works of art from Roman Antiquity to the present, familiarizing them with a broad range of artworks in their specific historical, cultural, medical, social, religious, political and intellectual contexts. Credit is awarded for only one of AHS 016 or AHS 133/ANTH 161/ DNCE 129/GSST 130/HISE 149.

subject: AHS
title: History of Western Art: Prehistoric to Byzantine
description: A survey of the visual arts of the ancient Near East and Egypt, the Greek world, and the Roman and Byzantine empires. Topics include the growth of urbanism, art as an expression of religious and political beliefs, and cultural contact as a source of artistic change. Credit is awarded for only one of AHS 017A or AHS 17HA.

subject: AHS
title: History of Western Art: Medieval to Renaissance
description: Surveys the visual arts of Europe in the Middle Ages and Renaissance. Includes the religious and political functions of art in the reestablishment of high civilization and the increased status of the individual artist. Credit is awarded for only one of AHS 017B or AHS 17HB.

subject: AHS
title: History of Western Art: Baroque to Modern
description: Surveys the visual arts of Europe and America from 1600 through the present. Includes the religious and political roles of art, the rise of secular imagery, the increased role of women in the arts, the impact of popular culture and photography, and other new media in the visual arts. Credit is awarded for only one of AHS 017C or AHS 17HC.

subject: AHS
title: Modern Art: A Broad View
description: A broad, critical overview of the 20th-century visual art practices that defied and expanded artistic conventions with emphasizing works that have shaped contemporary art. Global themes and movements include early avant-gardes, abstraction, Pop Art, performance, conceptual art, institutional critique, and postcolonial, feminist, and gendered interventions.

subject: AHS
title: Photography and the Body
description: Introduces the history of photography by providing ways of reading, writing, and thinking about photographs through the theme of the body. Focuses on photography’s role in forming notions of selfhood and cultural differences. Emphasizes the close analysis of limited examples and a critical approach.

subject: AHS
title: Introduction to Media Art
description: An introduction to the impact of media technology on the visual arts from photography to the Internet. Addresses mechanical reproduction, perception, gender, sexuality, identity, interactivity, cybernetics, and popular culture. Cross-listed with MCS 023.

subject: AHS
title: Introduction to Architecture and Urbanism
description: An introduction to the built environment including buildings, gardens, and cities, examined in terms of historical, cultural, social, technological, and political factors. Emphasis is on examples from Southern California. Credit is awarded for one of the following AHS 021 or AHS 021W.

subject: AHS
title: Introduction to Architecture and Urbanism
description: An introduction to the built environment, including buildings, gardens, and cities, examined in terms of historical, cultural, social, technological, and political factors. This is a writing-intensive course designed to help students improve critical writing skills while writing within the discipline of architectural history. Fulfills the third-quarter writing requirement for students who earn a grade of “C” or better for courses that the Academic Senate designates, and that the student’s college permits, as alternatives to English 001C. Credit is awarded for one of the following AHS 021W or AHS 021.
prerequisites_text: ENGL 001B with a grade of C or better, ENGL 007, may be taken concurrently; for concurrent enrollment in ENGL 007, review the course titles or topics in the current online Schedule of Classes to find the corresponding ENGL 007 writing workshop

subject: AHS
title: Introduction to American Art
description: Surveys the art and visual culture of North America (primarily in the United States) from the first European contact to the present. Emphasizes visual representation as means for cultural encounter; the construction of race, class and gender; and the relationship between art, nation, and identity.

subject: AHS
title: Art of Mesoamerica
description: Surveys the art and architecture of Mesoamerica from the Olmec to the fall of the Aztec capital in 1521. Focuses on empire and trade, religion and astronomy, writing systems and the history the book, and cross-cultural interaction through emphasizing the close analysis of artworks and historical texts.

subject: AHS
title: Art of Pre-Columbian America
description: A survey course that provides a background to the ancient art of Mexico, Central America, and the Andean region of western South America. Discusses art of pre-Columbian America according to the three broad cultural regions of Mesoamerica, the lower part of central and northwestern South America, and the Andean area. Cross-listed with ANTH 027 and LNST 027.

subject: AHS
title: Art and Architecture of Latin America
description: Introduces Latin American art and architecture from the European conquest to the present. Topics include religious and secular art and architecture; hybridization of indigenous and imported styles; national styles after independence; Mexican murals; women artists; Latin American modernismo; and Chicano and Border art. Cross-listed with LNS T028.

subject: AHS
title: Rome: the Ancient City
description: Traces the development of the city of ancient Rome. Studies the literary and historical evidence alongside the physical remains of the city including its monuments, art, and historical and archaeological remains. Seeks to introduce the Romans and their importance for later ages. Cross-listed with CLA 017, and HIST 027.

subject: AHS
title: Photography Since 1960
description: A critical overview of major historical, social, and political issues in art photography since 1960. Topics include New Documentary, conceptual photography, the Pictures generation, institutional critique, identity politics, the emergence of digital photography, and the cross-categorical expansion of the medium.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Art and Architecture of Tenochtitlan/Mexico City
description: Uses a case study of Mexico City (formerly Tenochtitlan) to introduce Latin America’s urban history. Illustrates through murals, mausoleums, pyramids and park show how the connections between art, architecture, and the natural environment (earthquakes, lakes, smog, volcanoes) underpin life and experience in the megalopolis.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Art of the Aztec Empire
description: An introduction to the art of the Aztec Empire. Studies architecture, sculpture, ceramics, painting, lapidary work, gold work, and feather work. Explores the relationship between art and ritual and art and the imperial state. Cross-listed with ANTH 151 and LNST 112.
prerequisites_text: AHS 027/ANTH 027/LNST 027 or upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Sixteenth-Century Mexico: An Art of Two Worlds
description: Explores the art of the first colonial century in Mexico. Investigates the translation of European art forms to the New World, the fate of indigenous traditions, and artistic change in the context of colonialism and evangelization.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: History of Brazilian Art and Architecture
description: The history of Brazilian art and architecture from the nineteenth century to present. Explores visual culture including painting, sculpture, prints, murals, architecture, urbanism, landscape design, and installation art. Studies artworks and buildings through a social historical framework, taking into consideration topics like colonialism, modernization, underdevelopment, race, nationalism, internationalism, and globalism. Cross-listed with LNST 114.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Modern and Contemporary Art of Latin America
description: A study of Latin American art from circa 1900 to the present. Considers national and regional histories and artistic trajectories beginning with the advent of an artistic avant-garde. Investigates the relationships between European and Latin American developments. Cross-listed with LNST 115.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Architecture and Arts of the Andes
description: An introduction to architecture, urbanism, and related material culture of the Andes from ancient times to the present. Focuses on the diverse and rich architectural heritage of an important building center in the Americas. Addresses architecture’s relationship to artistic and material production such as painting, pottery, sculpture, city planning, and textiles. Cross-listed with LNST 116.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Visual Culture of the Incas
description: An introduction to the art, architecture, and urban form of the Inca civilization. Examines how these elements influenced state formation, conquest, and resistance. Includes studies of urban plans, buildings, paintings, textiles, prints, sculpture, metalwork, and ceramics. Cross-listed with ANTH 157 and LNST 117.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Berlin Metropolis in Literature, Film, Music, and Art
description: An introduction to the metropolis Berlin as a gateway between the East and West. Explores topography of the city through film, art, music, and literary texts. Considers Berlin’s dramatic transformations as a microcosm of Germany and Europe’s troubled history in the twentieth century. Course conducted in English. Cross-listed with CPLT 111, EUR 120, and GER 111.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Conceptual Art in Latin America
description: Considers conceptual art made across Latin America, from 1960s to present. Focuses on subversive strategies artists developed to critique military dictatorships then in power, while circumventing legalized censorship. Considers localized versions of conceptual art in Santiago, Buenos Aires, Rio de Janeiro, Havana, Mexico City, and situate them within international movement. Cross-listed with LNST 124.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Illustrations and Illuminations: the Arts of the Book in the Islamic World
description: Introduction to manuscript production in the Islamic world from simple Qur’ans to opulent manuscripts illustrating Persian literature. Explores the centrality of manuscripts in Islamic artistic culture. Topics include calligraphy, painting styles, patronage, workshop organization, the production of knowledge, conceptions of the artist, and the relationship between word and image.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Sultans and Saints: the Visual and Material Culture of Islam in South Asia
description: Introduction to the art and architecture of Muslim dynasties in South Asia from the eighth to the eighteenth century. Explores the centrality of manuscripts in Islamic artistic culture. Studies the movement and settlement of religious, political, and intellectual elites throughout the Subcontinent and the buildings and objects they commissioned.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Body in Western Art: Antiquity to Present
description: Presents further questions and study of the human body and how it was depicted and interpreted in works of art from Roman Antiquity to the present. Explores a broad range of artworks in their specific historical, cultural, medical, social, religious, political, and intellectual contexts. Cross-listed with ANTH 161, GSST 130, and HISE 149. Credit is awarded for one of the following AHS 133, ANTH 161, GSST 130, HISE 149, or AHS 016.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; Restricted to major(s) Anthropology, Art History, Art History/Admin Studies, Art History/Religious Studies, Gender and Sexuality Studies, History, History/ Administrative Studies, History/Law and Society; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Postmedia Art
description: Covers heterogeneous movements, theories, and practices from the 1960s to the present that have collectively challenged the doctrine of medium specificity. Topics may include dematerialization, conceptual and postconceptual art, performance and body art, earthworks, process art, and experimental sound and radio.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: History of Video Art
description: Traces the evolution of video art from the invention of the Portapak and early video collectives to the current ubiquity of video installation, single-channel, and multimedia art. Emphasizes video art in the United States.
prerequisites_text: AHS 017C; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: History of Experimental Cinema
description: A survey of cinema outside of the economic, institutional, and aesthetic imperatives of mainstream film production. Covers an array of alternative film movements including surrealism and dada, Soviet avant-garde, the Cine 16 Group, French new wave, North American avant-garde, and the artist’s film.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Arts of China
description: A survey of Chinese art and culture from the prehistoric to the contemporary. Cross-listed with AST 138.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Arts of Buddhism
description: Explores the history, concepts, and arts of Buddhism. Emphasizes the transmission and cultural translation of pictorial arts within Asia and to Western worlds. Cross-listed with AST 139.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Arts of the Silk Road
description: An exploration of visual and material cultures across the Silk Road network. Emphasizes the intersection of local and global spanning the Eurasian region from antiquity to the medieval period.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Mongol Empire: the World of Genghis Khan and His Descendants
description: An exploration of artistic and architectural developments in the Mongol Empire (1206-1368), the largest contiguous land empire in world history.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Text and Image in Chinese Painting
description: Examines the art of writing and painting in China, focusing on the close relationship between written language and pictorial image. Reading knowledge of the Chinese language is not necessary. Cross-listed with AST 143.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Arts of Japan
description: Major developments in the arts of Japan from the prehistoric to the contemporary period. Emphasizes the social and cultural contexts of religious art, architecture, and master artists through history, with a brief introduction to contemporary art and pop culture. Cross-listed with AST 144.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Contemporary Asian Art
description: Explores the wide spectrum of contemporary arts from China, Korea, and Japan in terms of modernism, orientalism/occidentalism, identity politics, and globalization. Cross-listed with AST 146.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Japanese House
description: History of the traditional Japanese house from prehistoric times to the nineteenth century. Examples used to place the Japanese house within the general history of Japanese architecture and within its social and cultural context. Cross-listed with AST 147.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Art of Greece
description: Explores the architecture, sculpture, painting, and minor arts of ancient Greece from the earliest Archaic Period through the Hellenistic Age.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Cultures in Conflict: Art at the Fall of the Roman Empire
description: Covers architecture, mosaic, wall painting, manuscript illumination, and sculpture from the origins of Christianity to the final dissolution of the Roman Empire. Stresses the role of art in the co-optation of the Church by the Empire and then in the aftermath of its fall.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Memory of Empire: the Art of Early Medieval Europe
description: Covers manuscript illumination, barbarian jewelry, architecture, and sculpture from the fall of the Roman Empire and through the Carolingian Empire up to the tenth century. Stresses the interplay between indigenous Germanic and foreign classical traditions.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Medieval Pilgrimage and the Art of Romanesque France
description: Covers architecture, sculpture, and illuminated manuscripts of the eleventh and twelfth centuries. Stresses the role of the pilgrimage and of politics during the period of the revival of monumental architecture and of public sculpture of the Middle Ages.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Self-Portraits: Renaissance to Contemporary Art
description: Introduces the history, theory, and practice of self-portraiture in Western art, from its beginnings in Antiquity to contemporary works. Discusses concepts of identity, ‘self-fashioning’, and artistic thinking chronologically. Introduces major works of art and important interpretations/methods of art history.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Renaissance Architecture
description: An introduction to architecture in the period 1400-1600. Explores the major ideas and trends in architecture that took form in this period, including the architects and the ideas that motivated them in their historical context.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Italian Renaissance: Fifteenth-and Sixteenth-Century Florence
description: Surveys the painting, sculpture, architecture, and gardens of this period within their historical and cultural context.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Italian Renaissance: Fifteenth-and Sixteenth-Century Rome
description: Surveys the painting, sculpture, architecture, and gardens of this period within their historical and cultural context.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Renaissance in Venice: West Meets East
description: An introduction to the art and culture of Venice circa 1420-1600. Addresses central issues of artistic, cultural, and intellectual exchange among Venice, the Eastern Mediterranean, and the North. Discusses major artworks in the fields of painting, sculpture, and architecture.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Women Artists in Renaissance Europe, 1400-1600
description: Surveys the lives and work of women artists in Renaissance Europe. Considers circumstances under which it was possible for women to become artists; how they evolved from practicing in the cloistered convent to participating in the competitive public market place; what they painted; and who their patrons were. Cross-listed with HISE 133, and GSST 170.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior

subject: AHS
title: Europe in the Early Modern World: Global Artistic Contact and Exchange, 1492-1750
description: Explores trade, religious conversion, intersecting traditions, and the creation of new traditions. Examines the mechanisms and cultural consequences of change through time.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Baroque Architecture
description: Examines the development of architecture in Europe and the Americas from 1580 to 1750. Explores the concept of buildings and the city as a form of communication; the spread and reformulation of architectural ideas in new contexts; and the rise of the architectural profession.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Church, the Court, and the People: Art in Seventeenth-Century Europe
description: A study of the dominant trends and figures of Italian, French, Spanish, Flemish, and Dutch Baroque art. Includes the works of Caravaggio, Bernini, Velazquez, and Rembrandt. Emphasizes the development of illusionistic ceiling decoration, the theoretical basis of Baroque art, and the sacred and political uses of art.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Baroque Rome
description: An in-depth examination of Roman art in the seventeenth century. Studies painting, sculpture, architecture, and urban planning in their political and religious contexts. Emphasizes the ecclesiastical and private patrons who transformed Rome into one of the world’s most important cities.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Rococo to Revolution: Art in Eighteenth-Century Europe
description: Examines major developments in eighteenth-century painting, sculpture, and interior decoration from the emergence of the Rococo to the dawn of Neoclassicism. Explores the response of art to new forms of patronage, the erotics of eighteenth-century art, and how art functioned as social and political commentary.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Industry and Alienation: Late Nineteenth-Century American Art
description: A study of American art from 1848 to 1900. Focuses on social, political, and artistic issues related to industrialization. Explores themes in visual culture; the construction of an American identity; the role of fine arts in American society; and the tensions of class, gender, race, and ethnicity in American art.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Twentieth-Century Photography 1900-1960
description: A critical overview of photographic practices in Europe and the United States in the first half of the twentieth century. Topics include pictorialism, the interwar avant-gardes, the rise of documentary, photojournalism, and street photography. Examines technological, conceptual, aesthetic, economic, and social issues.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: American Art: Colonial Period to 1900
description: Explores painting and architecture in the United States from the colonial period to 1900.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: The Modern City
description: Examines the modern metropolis from the Industrial Revolution to the present. Explores the history and theory of modern urbanism through case studies of metropolitan areas with a rich urban culture, architecture, and morphologic features. Investigates approaches to the problems of the large urban agglomeration in the context of social Cross-listed with URST 178.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Revolution, Reaction, and Revision: American Art Between the World Wars
description: An in-depth study of American art and visual culture during the early twentieth century, focusing on the period between the two world wars. Traces artistic developments in painting, photography, cinema, and material culture. Explores the issues of race, class, gender, and regional identity as addressed in these media.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Honors History of Western Art: Prehistoric to Byzantine
description: Honors course corresponding to AHS 017A. A survey of the visual arts of the ancient Near East and Egypt, the Greek world, and the Roman and Byzantine empires. Topics include the growth of urbanism, art as an expression of religious and political beliefs, and cultural contact as a source of artistic change. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Credit is awarded for only one of AHS 017A or AHS 17HA.
prerequisites_text: admission to the University Honors Program or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Honors History of Western Art: Medieval to Renaissance
description: Honors course corresponding to AHS 017B. Surveys of the visual arts of Europe in the Middle Ages and Renaissance. Includes the religious and political functions of art in the reestablishment of high civilization and the increased status of the individual artist. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Credit is awarded for only one of AHS 017B or AHS 17HB.
prerequisites_text: admission to the University Honors Program or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Honors History of Western Art: Baroque to Modern
description: Honors course corresponding to AHS 017C. Surveys of the visual arts of Europe and America from 1600 through the present. Includes the religious and political roles of art, the rise of secular imagery, the increased role of women in the arts, the impact of popular culture and photography, and the other new media in the visual arts. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Credit is awarded for only one of AHS 017C or AHS 17HC.
prerequisites_text: admission to University Honors or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Modern European Art I: Nineteenth-Century
description: Surveys painting and sculpture in Europe from the French Revolution to the Franco-Prussian War. Introduces the ideas and concepts of modern European art. Traces artistic developments from Neoclassicism to the emergence of Impressionism in a broad cultural, social, and political context.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior

subject: AHS
title: Modern Art 2: Art in Europe, 1870-1945
description: Traces the history of the modern movement from Impressionism to the end of World War II. Focuses on the arts in their interrelationships to the political events and social conditions of the period. Emphasizes the persecution of modernism in Europe under fascism and communism.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Visual Art and Visual Theory After 1945
description: Examines visual art since 1945 primarily from Europe and the United States. Traces developments in all media within a historical and theoretical context. Focuses on the rise of postmodernism, analyzing work in relation to theories of representation and cultural identity.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Photography On Display
description: Covers various topics related to current exhibitions at the California Museum of Photography. Provides the necessary historical and theoretical background of the specific photographs on display. Addresses the wider museum context of the difference between working photographs, art photographs, and the politics of that designation. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Modern Architecture
description: Explores modern architecture and its sources from 1800 to the present. Cross-listed with URST 184.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Media and Movements: Film, Video, Photography, and the Visual Arts
description: Focuses on key cultural movements or developments as global arts over the past century. Provides a thematic history of the avant-garde and experimental arts including painting, sculpture, photography, video, film, performance, installation, and new media art. Cross-listed with MCS 186.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Nineteenth-Century Photography
description: Examines the development of photography in the nineteenth century. Addresses the technologies, artistic practices, and social uses of this medium. Focuses on European and American materials, as well as traces the histories of portrait, landscape, scientific, and documentary photography.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: (E-Z) Topics in Contemporary Art
description: Addresses selected issues, movements, and artists of importance to international art history since the 1960s. E. Art Since Conceptual Art. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior

subject: AHS
title: Special Studies
description: Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: To be taken with the consent of the chair of the department as a means of meeting special curricular problems

subject: AHS
title: California Modern Art
description: Explores California visual expression from 1900 to 1980. Provides critical attention to the development of a purportedly unique California art and culture. Focuses on Southern California topics in order to take advantage of local and regional museums, collections, lectures, and events.
prerequisites_text: an Art History course or upper division standing or consent of instructor

subject: AHS
title: Junior and Senior Seminar in Art History
description: Critical study of selected topics in the history of art and its methods. Topics vary. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing in Art History or Art History Administrative Studies

subject: AHS
title: Senior Honors Thesis
description: Independent research and preparation of a senior honors thesis completed under the supervision of a faculty member. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: admission to University Honors or consent of the Art History Department

subject: AHS
title: Individual Internship
description: Individual study or apprenticeship in a museum, art library, or slide and photo archive in order to gain practical experience and skills for future professional work. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and upper-division standing

subject: ANTH
title: Cultural Anthropology
description: Explores the basic contributions of anthropology to the understanding of human behavior and culture and the explanation of similarities and differences among human societies. Addresses the relevance of materials drawn from tribal and peasant culture to problems of the modern world. Stresses the application of anthropological methods to research problems. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 001, ANTH 001H, or ANTH 001W.

subject: ANTH
title: Honors Cultural Anthropology
description: Honors course corresponding to ANTH 001. Explores the basic contributions of anthropology to the understanding of human behavior and culture and the explanation of similarities and differences among human societies. Addresses the relevance of materials drawn from tribal and peasant culture to problems of the modern world. Stresses the application of anthropological methods to research problems. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Credit is awarded for only one of ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W.
prerequisites_text: admission to University Honors or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Cultural Anthropology
description: Explores the basic contributions of anthropology to the understanding of human behavior and culture and the explanation of similarities and differences among human societies. Addresses the relevance of materials drawn from tribal and peasant culture to problems of the modern world. Stresses the application of anthropological methods to research problems. Fulfills the third-quarter writing requirement for students who earn a grade of “C” or better for courses that the Academic Senate designates, and that the student’s college permits, as alternatives to WRIT 030. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 001W, ANTH 001, or ANTH 001H.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 040T; WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better

subject: ANTH
title: Biological Anthropology
description: A survey of past and contemporary human variation and evolution. Considers the perspective of the fossil record, inferences from nonhuman primate biology and social behavior, and the forces of evolution.

subject: ANTH
title: World Prehistory
description: Examines the cultural history of humankind, from the beginning of tool-using behavior in the Old World to the rise of complex social and political systems (civilizations) in both the Old and New World.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Archaeology
description: A general introduction to the aims and methods of archaeology, in the field and in the laboratory. Briefly surveys world prehistory as revealed by these methods.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to World Music
description: A survey of people, identity, and music making. Includes listening to music from many cultural contexts. Also covers a variety of scholarly topics in world music. Cross-listed with MUS 006.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: Introduces linguistic anthropological understanding of how language not only reflects but also refracts and shapes our social, political, cultural, and moral realities, values, and interests. Examines linguistic anthropological theories, ethnographies, and methodologies to explore how, to what extent, and why language is unexpectedly cultural, social, and political. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 007 or ANTH 007S.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: Introduces linguistic anthropological understanding of how language not only reflects but also refracts and shapes our social, political, cultural, and moral realities, values, and interests. Examines linguistic anthropological theories, ethnographies, and methodologies to explore how, to what extent, and why language is unexpectedly cultural, social, and political. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 007S or ANTH 007.

subject: ANTH
title: Mysteries of the Ancient Maya
description: An introduction to all aspects of the ancient Maya civilization of southern Mexico and Central America. Explores Maya origins, political organization, agriculture, art, religion, architecture, hieroglyphic writing, and the unexplained collapse of the civilization. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 010 or ANTH 010S.

subject: ANTH
title: Mysteries of the Ancient Maya
description: An introduction to all aspects of the ancient Maya civilization of southern Mexico and Central America. Explores Maya origins, political organization, agriculture, art, religion, architecture, hieroglyphic writing, and the unexplained collapse of the civilization. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 010S or ANTH 010.

subject: ANTH
title: Great Discoveries in Archaeology
description: Introduces the methods and goals of archaeology through examples of “great discoveries” that have altered our understanding about the past. Explores discoveries from around the world, including such well-known examples as King Tut’s tomb, Pompeii, and the lost cities of the ancient Maya. Also covers lesser-known recent finds and the application of modern scientific technologies in archaeology.

subject: ANTH
title: Culture, Health, and Healing
description: Surveys health, disease, curing, and nutrition in a cross-cultural perspective. Covers how different cultural groups consider disease, health maintenance, and healing; how traditional beliefs about health and nutrition arise; and what one can and cannot learn from traditional health-seeking practices. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 020 or ANTH 020S.

subject: ANTH
title: Culture, Health and Healing
description: Surveys health, disease, curing, and nutrition in a cross-cultural perspective. Covers how different cultural groups consider disease, health maintenance, and healing; how traditional beliefs about health and nutrition arise; and what one can and cannot learn from traditional health-seeking practices. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 020S or ANTH 020.

subject: ANTH
title: Art of Pre-Columbian America
description: A survey course that provides a background to the ancient art of Mexico, Central America, and the Andean region of western South America. Discusses art of pre-Columbian America according to the three broad cultural regions of Mesoamerica, the lower part of central and northwestern South America, and the Andean area. Cross-listed with AHS 027 and LNST 027.

subject: ANTH
title: Human Evolution
description: Explores the evolutionary history of humans as biocultural beings adapting to changing environments. Examines fossils, genetics, and archaeological data. Offered online only.

subject: ANTH
title: History of Anthropological Theory
description: A survey of the history of theory in anthropology and the development of the discipline. Focuses on useful ideas from these theories and methods anthropologists have developed to study other societies. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 100 or ANTH 100W.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: History of Anthropological Theory
description: A survey of the history of theory in anthropology and the development of the discipline. Focuses on useful ideas from these theories and methods anthropologists have developed to study other societies. Fulfills the third-quarter writing requirement for students who earn a grade of “C” or better for courses that the Academic Senate designates, and that the student’s college permits as alternatives to WRIT 030. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 100W or ANTH 100.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 040L; ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W; WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better; and consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Contemporary Anthropological Theory
description: Explores the core ideas in modern anthropology about culture and society. Covers basic issues of contemporary theory since the 1980s. Explores the new methodologies and application of theory to ethnography.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 100

subject: ANTH
title: Historical Archaeology
description: Introduces the archaeological study of the historical period (15th century-present). Includes the theories, methods, and data sources used in the discipline. Explores case studies and topics of interest in historical archaeology.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Visual Anthropology
description: An introduction to the field of visual anthropology. Examines the similarities and differences between ethnographic film, critical studies, and written ethnographies. Explores the politics of representing other cultures visually. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 103 or ANTH 103S.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Intro to Visual Anthropology
description: An introduction to the field of visual anthropology. Examines the similarities and differences between ethnographic film, critical studies, and written ethnographies. Explores the politics of representing other cultures visually. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 103S or ANTH 103.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 with a grade of C- or better or ANTH 001H with a grade of B or better or ANTH 001W with a grade of C or better; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Bioarchaeology
description: Introduces the study of bioarchaeology in order to explore human skeletal remains from archaeological settings. Topics include the history and ethics of studying human remains, mortuary archaeology, methodological shifts in skeletal research, and interpretation of human skeletons using various methods.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 002 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Organizations as Cultural Systems
description: Examines the role of culture in the formation and management of complex bureaucratic organizations. Covers types of organizations and organizational cultures, the impact of the cultural environment, and problems posed by rapid cultural change. Offered in summer only. Cross-listed with BUS 158.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Gender and Genocide
description: Examines gendered dimensions of contemporary and historical genocides. Analyzes the ways gender ideologies intersect racialization and ethnic marking. Explores how gender shapes selection, forced labor, torture, and murder. Considers gender ideologies in relation to collective, institutional, and individual responses to genocide and genocidal campaigns. Cross-listed with GSST 125.
prerequisites_text: one of the following courses: GSST 001, GSST 001H, GSST 001S; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Evolution of the Capacity For Culture
description: An examination of the evolution of the biological and social capacities that have made culture the central attribute of the human species. Topics include the evolution of human diet, tool-making, the family and kinship, and language.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or ANTH 002 or ANTH 003 or relevant preparation in psychology or biology or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Global Media
description: Examines the global production, transmission, and consumption of mass media in diverse national and transnational contexts. Includes debates over the power of media; construction of knowledge of others; affective responses to images of violence; practices of self-representation; and the ways in which consumers accept, reject and negotiate media messages.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Prehistoric Agriculture
description: A cross-cultural perspective on prehistoric agriculture as resource management, economic system, and political tool. Archaeological methods and theory of reconstructing agricultural systems and their role in prehistoric societies.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Peopling of the New World
description: Consideration of the archaeological, biological, linguistic, and dating evidence documenting the nature and timing of the earliest occupation of the Western Hemisphere by human populations.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Settlement Patterns and Locational Analysis
description: An archaeological perspective on spatial behavior from architectural design to regional economic systems. Provides an introduction to a broad range of issues and analytical perspectives with an emphasis on theoretical approaches and case studies.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Ancient Households and Communities
description: Explores archaeological perspectives on households and communities. Discusses their composition, function, and meaning. Illustrates with specific cases from diverse cultural contexts. Topics include everyday life in ancient households and communities, social and economic reproduction, and long-term stability and change.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W; ANTH 003 or ANTH 005; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Lithic Technology I
description: Introduction to the technology of core-and-flake stone tools. Addresses principles of fracture, quarrying, reduction, heat treatment, core technology, and production and use of flaked stone tools in core-and-flake lithic assemblages. Includes assemblage formation processes and their interpretation.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Lithic Technology 2
description: Covers the technology of core-and-blade and ground-stone industries. Addresses percussion- and pressure-blade reduction sequences and strategies. Emphasizes quarrying, initial reduction, core and blade production, and production and use of tools from blades. Includes technology and production of ground-stone tools, quarrying of raw material, and assemblage formation processes and their interpretation.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 114A; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Lithic Analysis
description: Covers characterization, analysis, and interpretation of stone tool assemblages with emphasis on debitage.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 114B; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: (E-Z) Archaeological Interpretations
description: Study of the prehistory of different regions of the world. Emphasis is on the method and theory underlying archaeological investigations of the nature of people and culture and the course of human development.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005

subject: ANTH
title: North American Prehistory
description: Interpretation of the archaeological record of North America from initial peopling of the continent to the historic period.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Prehistory of California
description: A survey of prehistoric cultures of California from the earliest settlement to the historic period.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology of Eastern Mesoamerica
description: An introduction to Mayan archaeology intended to provide an overview of ancient Maya cultural history from the Formative period to the time of Spanish contact. During the course, particular Maya sites will be described in detail.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology of Western Mesoamerica
description: An introduction to the archaeology and culture history in the New World nuclear area of Western Mesoamerica from the occupation of this area before 10,000 years ago to the arrival of Spanish Europeans in A.D. 1519.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Prehistory of the Southwest
description: A survey of prehistoric cultures of the American Southwest from earliest settlement to the historic period.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Andean Prehistory
description: A description of Andean culture history, emphasizing Peru, from the earliest documentation of human occupation to the Spanish conquest of the Inca. Topics include origins of food production, early ceremonial architecture, Paracas textiles, the Nasca lines, Moche iconography and ritual, and Inca architecture. Discussion of major sites and their architecture, ceramics, sculpture, and other archaeological remains.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 003 or ANTH 005 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Ancient Oaxaca
description: Explores current understanding about ancient Zapotec, Mixtec, and neighboring cultures in Oaxaca, Mexico, the location of the earliest Mesoamerican state system and one of its earliest cities.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W; ANTH 003 or ANTH 005; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Cities
description: Examines theoretical and methodological debates in the anthropological study of cities and urban life. Uses ethnographic case studies in Asia, Africa, and Latin America to explore cultural practices and representations of urban space, and struggles over rights to the city. Topics include urban inequality, ecology, housing, planning, and redevelopment.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of the instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Origins of Cities
description: Explores new forms of social, economic, and political organization that developed with the advent of cities. Examines case studies of the rise of urbanism in both the Old and New Worlds to investigate how and why cities emerged and consolidated.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or ANTH 003 or ANTH 005 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: The Anthropology of Tourism
description: Surveys the central problems and issues in the anthropological study of tourism. Main topics include the place of tourism in the global economy, the impact of tourism on cultural identity and culture change, environmental issues in tourism development, and tourism as a form of cross- and multicultural communication. Credit is awarded for only one of ANTH 119 or ANTH 280.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Language and Culture
description: Covers the interrelations among language, culture, and habitual behavior; the classification of languages; and anthropological uses of linguistic evidence.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W, LING 020 or ANTH 007 or ANTH 007S; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropological Theories of the Arts
description: Covers anthropological theories of the arts emphasizing folk and traditional forms. Features oral and written literature and discusses theories of musical, visual, and other arts.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Economic Anthropology
description: Examines the social and cultural dimensions of production, exchange, saving, borrowing, and consumption. Topics covered include rationality and economizing, reciprocity, gender and household decision-making, and neoliberalism.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Linguistic Anthropology
description: Course will cover the application of linguistics techniques to studies of other symbolic and social fields, the analysis of semantic systems, and the use of linguistic techniques for prehistory.
prerequisites_text: LING 020, or consent of the instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Ritual and Religion
description: The elements and forms of religious belief and behavior; functions of ritual in society. Cross-cultural comparisons.

subject: ANTH
title: Kinship and Family Organization
description: Introduces the study of kinship, marriage, family, and social organization in contemporary cultural anthropology and the history of approaches to these topics. Examines the interplay and tensions between cultural norms and practices and state legal systems.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W

subject: ANTH
title: Southeast Asian Performance
description: Introduction to the roles and genres of expressive culture in Southeast Asia, including dance, music, theater, film, and digital culture. Performance is discussed as both a time-honored and a contemporary medium for cultural production, from the courts to everyday experience. Cross-listed with AST 123, DNCE 123, MUS 123, and SEAS 123.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Political Anthropology
description: Examines different overt and covert means by which power and social differentiation are produced, perpetuated, and challenged in societies across the world. Studies the politics of culture, ethnicity, nationalism, and gender. Credit is awarded for only one of ANTH 127 or ANTH 127S.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Political Anthropology
description: Examines different overt and covert means by which power and social differentiation are produced, perpetuated, and challenged in societies across the world. Studies the politics of culture, ethnicity, nationalism, and gender. Credit is awarded for only one of ANTH 127 or ANTH 127S.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Performing Arts of Asia
description: A survey of music, dance, theatre, and ritual in four major geocultural regions of Asia: Central, East, South, and Southeast. No Western music training is required. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units. Cross-listed with AST 128, DNCE 128, and TFDP 176.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Maya Hieroglyphs
description: Introduces the Maya hieroglyphs and critically evaluates its political history. Topics include three Maya calendars, a basic grammar (logographs, syllables, verbs, pronouns), three writing methods (transcriptions, transliteration, and translation), dynastic events, gods, supernaturals, and political interactions. Cross-listed with CPAC 129A, and LNST 129A.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or ANTH 005 or ANTH 007 or ANTH 007S; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: The Linguistics of Ancient Maya Writing
description: Analyzes and critically evaluates the linguistics of Ancient Maya Writing. Topics include grammar (transitive, intransitive, positional, active, passive, mediopassive, antipassive, inchoactive verbs, tense, aspect, transitive perfect, noun, pronoun, morphosyllable, phonology); three writing methods (transcriptions, transliteration, and translation); title and rank; scripts and ideologies; and dynastic interactions. Cross-listed with CPAC 129B, and LNST 129B.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 129A; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Ancient Pottery Analysis
description: Prerequisite(s); ANTH 005 or consent of instructor. An extensive review of the techniques used by archaeologists to study ceramic artifacts, one of the most common archaeological remains found at many Holocene sites throughout the world. Critically explores the use of typology, attribute analysis, experimental archaeology, petrography, source analysis, residue analysis, and ceramic ethnoarchaeology.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Anthropology
description: Applies anthropology to current issues such as community development, education, health, public administration, and conflict.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Cultural Ecology
description: Introduces people’s relationships to their total environment. Explores strategies for managing the environment and its resources, the effects of the environment on culture and society, the impact of human management on the ecosystem, and ways in which human groups view their surroundings.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology and International Development
description: Analyzes the concept of development by examining major theories and approaches in the anthropological study of international development. Focuses on the relationship between anthropology and the development industry. Topics include ethical issues in development anthropology, causes of failure and success in development interventions, and transformations in development theory and practice.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: The Will to Adorn Dress and Identity
description: Explores sartorial practices as a means for examining formations of identities and structural inequalities across space and time.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: The Archaeology of African Diaspora History and Culture
description: Covers the thematic and methodological approaches associated with the historical archaeology of Africa and the African diaspora.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropological Perspectives On Gender in Southeast Asia
description: Examines the intersections of gender, power, and sexuality in post-colonial Southeast Asia. Revisits early ethnographic claims of gender equality. Addresses current anthropological literature on the effects of colonialism, capitalism, and globalization on gender roles and relations within national and transnational contexts. Cross-listed with SEAS 136. Credit is awarded for only one of ANTH 136/SEAS 136 or ANTH 136S/SEAS 136S.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or equivalent

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropological Perspectives On Gender in Southeast Asia
description: Examines the intersections of gender, power, and sexuality in post-colonial Southeast Asia. Revisits early ethnographic claims of gender equality. Addresses current anthropological literature on the effects of colonialism, capitalism, and globalization on gender roles and relations within national and transnational contexts. Cross-listed with SEAS 136S. Credit is awarded for only one of ANTH 136/SEAS 136 or ANTH 136S/SEAS 136S.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or equivalent

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology: the American Tradition
description: Introduces the historical development of anthropological thought in the United States as a manifestation of class and state formation. Clarifies various intellectual currents in contemporary anthropology and their relationships to intellectual and social developments in the broader society.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Paleopathology
description: Introduces the study of disease in past populations within a paleoepidemiological framework. Includes the history and development of paleopathology, distinguishing disease from normal human variation, and making differential diagnoses. Addresses the following categories of pathology: congenital disorders, dental disease, trauma, infection, metabolic and hematologic conditions, neoplasms, and arthropathies.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 002 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Change and Development
description: Examines alternative theories of society, change, and development, as well as the assumptions and premises on which they are based. Considers how they are used to explain capitalist development, imperialism, colonial encounters, nationalism, decolonization, socialist revolution, modernization, unequal exchange, uneven development, globalization, and postcolonialism.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or ANTH 003 or ANTH 005; upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: (E-Z) Ethnographic Interpretations
description: Study of peoples and cultures in particular areas of the world. Emphasis is placed on ethnological and theoretical problems as these are revealed in the examination of the history, coherent sociocultural patterns, and ecology of specific aboriginal populations and contemporary groups.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnology of the Greater Southwest
description: An introduction to the many varied native cultures of the Greater Southwest. Major differences as well as similarities in the forms of language, social organization, religion, and material culture occurring in the Greater Southwest will be defined and described. The peoples of the Greater Southwest are considered, not only in terms of the ethnographic present, but also through a diachronic perspective, from the prehistoric past through the Spanish colonial era to the present.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropological Perspectives in Africa
description: Examines a number of African cultures using anthropological perspectives on subsistence patterns, social organization, and religious systems. Addresses the treatment of these cultures following a brief overview of the geography, history, and linguistic patterns of Africa.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: ANTH
title: Cultures of Southeast Asia
description: Anthropological interpretations of culture and society in southeast Asia including Indonesia. Topics include prehistory, ethnic groups, social organization and structure, human ecology, and folk and high culture.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or equivalent

subject: ANTH
title: Cultures of the Pacific
description: Overview of the cultures and contemporary issues facing the people of Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia. Examines the contribution of Oceanic studies to anthropological theories of kinship and exchange, gender, development studies, and indigenous knowledge systems. Emphasizes how Pacific Islanders draw on their cultural heritage in emerging from formal colonialism to establish new island nations.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: The Peoples of Mexico in Historical and Global Perspective
description: Survey of the cultures and societies of Mexico in historical and global perspective. Emphasis on agrarian communities and the contributions of Mesoamerican ethnography to general anthropological theory.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Sociocultural Perspectives On Graduate Education Futures
description: Introduces prominent sociocultural anthropological principles and theories underpinning the disparities between undergraduate and graduate diversity within the U.S education system. Also addresses components of graduate education within the UC system. Topics include impostor syndrome, growth mindset, social and cultural capital, intersectionality, and time poverty. Offered Online Only. Fulfills the third-quarter writing requirement for students who earn a grade of “C” or better for courses that the Academic Senate designates, and that the student?s college permits, as alternatives to English 001C. Credit is awarded for one of the following ANTH 141W or HNPG 110.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 040Y; WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: (E-Z) Black and Black Diaspora Studies
description: Segments offer critical anthropological perspectives on anti-blackness including historical political economic perspectives, colonial legacies, institutional and individual racism, racialized health disparities, and social movements.
prerequisites_text: see individual segments for assigned prerequisites

subject: ANTH
title: Blackness and Mass Incarceration
description: Introduction to the data, policy, political debates, and grassroots initiatives addressing unprecedented current incarceration in the United States. Critically investigates role of race and blackness in incarceration trends, new trends in policy, and alternatives to incarceration.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Black Business Cultures and Identities
description: Examines major debates, methods, and theories in studies of entrepreneurship and the commodification of (ethnic) cultures in transnational and cross-cultural contexts. Critically investigates how identity shapes and is shaped by entrepreneurial success with special attention to the contested and shifting meanings of entrepreneurial success and identity formations.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Caribbean Culture and Society
description: An overview of the Caribbean region from a historical, cultural, and political perspective. Emphasizes contemporary issues affecting the Caribbean and the struggle of its people to maintain their identities. Cross-listed with ETST 148, and LNST 168.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Afro-American Experience in the U.S.
description: Explores the racial politics of African American cultures and identities in juxtaposition with the making of the American nationhood and global capitalism. Critically examines the various anthropological discourses about African Americanness and portrays African Americans as nation-builders.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Political Economy of Southern Africa
description: Examines contemporary societies of southern Africa. Focuses on changes and continuities since the end of apartheid. Topics include transformations in ethnic and racial identity and classification; post-apartheid class formation and neoliberalism; labor migration and immigration; HIV/AIDS; land reform, resettlement, and spatial transformation; tourism; and conservation.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: (E-Z) Medical Anthropology Specialization
description: Courses related to the cross-cultural study of health and healing including health systems, healthcare, the political, economic, sociocultural, and biological factors that shape human health, and personal experiences of illness.
prerequisites_text: see individual segment for assigned prerequisites; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Culture and Medicine
description: Explores the interrelations of health, illness, and culture. Addresses cross-cultural comparisons of health and healing and the effects of cultural systems on health and illness. Examines a diversity of societies and their belief systems and the effects of cultural change (historical and modern) on health and wellbeing.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or ANTH 020 or ANTH 020S; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Gender, Race, and Medicine
description: Explores the relationship between Western medicine and women, racial minorities, and non-Western citizens. Investigates how gender ideology, racial inequity, and colonialism shape the medical representation of bodies, sexuality, and pathology. Examines how patients have renegotiated their relationships with medicine through health movements and alternative healing practices. Cross-listed with GSST 185.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Reproduction: Policies, Politics, and Practices
description: Examines reproductive policies, politics, and practices from a cross-cultural and historical perspective. Discusses political and economic processes and sociocultural dynamics; population control; sex preference; infanticide and neonatal neglect; adoption and foster parenting; abortion; technologically assisted conception; and gestational surrogacy. Cross-listed with GSST 140.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)
description: A cross-cultural examination of the global Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) epidemic from an anthropological perspective. Cross-listed with SEHE 181.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Biological Approaches to Medical Anthropology
description: Introduces medical anthropology from the biological perspective. Explores topics on evolution, health, and medicine; human biological variation in relation to disease; bioarchaeology; and the history of health. Takes the integrative and multidisciplinary approach.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 002; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Drugs and Culture
description: A cross-cultural examination of drug use and its relation to race, class, gender, morality, laws, and health policy. Cross-listed with SEHE 182.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Political Economy of Health
description: Examines critical medical anthropology. Focuses on the linkages between political economy, health, and healthcare systems in modern societies. Considers the effects of poverty, occupation, and environmental transformation in particular social contexts. Reviews four case studies: the political economy of HIV/AIDS, poverty, famine, and nuclear regulation.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Global Health
description: Examines the overlaps, debates, and potential of medical anthropology to address contemporary issues in global health. Focuses on how the historical development, theoretical frameworks, methodological approaches, and ethical debates within medical anthropology can contribute to a just and inclusive version of global health. Cross-listed with SEHE 183.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Bodies
description: Explores various anthropological discourses about the constitution of bodies focusing on how bodies differ across cultures and historical moments.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Sexualities and Culture
description: Examines the field of sexuality studies using a comparative, cross-cultural approach. Emphasizes the relation between culture, history, and political economy in the emergence of sexual practices and sexualized identities. Examines theories of sexuality and identity focusing on violence, human rights, and political agency. Cross-listed with GSST 103.
prerequisites_text: one of the following courses: GSST 001, GSST 001H, GSST 001S; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Gender, Kinship, and Social Change
description: Examines theories of gender and kinship, the formation of gender hierarchies and their uneven development, and the dynamics of family and gender in stratified social formations. Analyzes the relationship between family forms and political and economic processes. Cross-listed with GSST 149.
prerequisites_text: one of the following courses: GSST 001, GSST 001H, GSST 001S

subject: ANTH
title: The Art of the Aztec Empire
description: An introduction to the art of the Aztec Empire. Studies architecture, sculpture, ceramics, painting, lapidary work, gold work, and feather work. Explores the relationship between art and ritual and art and the imperial state. Cross-listed with AHS 112 and LNST 112.
prerequisites_text: AHS 027/ANTH 027/LNST 027 or upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Evolution of the First Hominids
description: Explores human evolution in the first five million years; examines the fossil record and incorporates data from archaeology and genetics. Topics include hominoid evolution in the Miocene, origin models of the human lineage, and the first ancestral humans.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 002 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Evolution of the Genus Homo
description: Explores human evolution in the last two million years; examines the fossil record and incorporates data from archaeology and genetics. Topics include origins of genus Homo, world-wide dispersals, Neanderthals, and origins of modern humans.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 002 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Human Osteology
description: An in-depth study of the human skeleton, including bone biology, functional morphology, fragment identification, reconstruction, forensic methods, and curation techniques. Useful for anthropologists and those intending careers in medicine, physical therapy, and forensics.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 002, upper-division standing; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Visual Culture of the Incas
description: An introduction to the art, architecture, and urban form of the Inca civilization. Examines how these elements influenced state formation, conquest, and resistance. Includes studies of urban plans, buildings, paintings, textiles, prints, sculpture, metalwork, and ceramics. Cross-listed with AHS 117, and LNST 117.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: The Body in Western Art: Antiquity to Present
description: Presents further questions and study of the human body and how it was depicted and interpreted in works of art from Roman Antiquity to the present. Explores a broad range of artworks in their specific historical, cultural, medical, social, religious, political, and intellectual contexts. Cross-listed with ANTH 161, GSST 130, and HISE 149. Credit is awarded for one of the following AHS 133, ANTH 161, GSST 130, HISE 149, or AHS 016.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; Restricted to major(s) Anthropology, Art History, Art History/Admin Studies, Art History/Religious Studies, Gender and Sexuality Studies, History, History/ Administrative Studies, History/Law and Society; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Transnational and Global Communities
description: A critical survey of recent anthropological and related research and theory concerning transnational and global sociocultural processes. Special emphasis on transnational, diasporan, and other unbounded communities; borderlands; and the impact of global media and communication and transnational migration on community and identity.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: Forensic Anthropology
description: Introduces the applied study of forensic anthropology. Topics include basic training in forensic anthropology, its history and theoretical background, medico-legal aspects, case studies, and training in how to identify human skeletal remains and information that can be determined from human bone.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 002 with a grade of C or better; or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
title: (E-Z) Anthropological Methods
description: Surveys methods and techniques utilized in archaeology, biological anthropology, cultural anthropology, and linguistic anthropology. Emphasizes field and laboratory methods.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 005

subject: ANTH
title: Methods in Archaeology
description: Review of methods used by archaeologists in field and laboratory contexts. Critically explores the applications of different techniques to answer social questions.

subject: ANTH
title: Methods in Biological Anthropology
description: Introduces research methods in biological anthropology. Topics include the history of scientific approach in American anthropology, statistics, data resampling, evolution, and variation.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 002 or consent of instructor

subject: ANTH
