description: Engages practical use of research practices, methods, and epistemologies introduced in BLKS 191A. Facilitates design of research questions and projects for senior capstone project as well as further exploration of the role of researcher.† Focuses on research development skills and field-based concentrations. Helps identify relevant theoretical frameworks and bibliographies.
prerequisites_text: BLKS 191A; or consent of instructor

subject: BLKS
title: Black Study Senior Capstone 1
description: Facilitates initiation of a transdisciplinary capstone project drawing on methods and practices learned in the Black Study major. Applies research and critical writing methods, performance and embodied praxis, and knowledge of visual cultures and media. Provides mentorship for research, writing, and revision processes.
prerequisites_text: BLKS 191A with a grade of C- or better or BLKS 191B with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; a transdisciplinary research plan must be approved; and consent of instructor

subject: BLKS
title: Black Study Senior Capstone 2
description: Continues transdisciplinary capstone project drawing on methods and practices learned in Black Study major. Applies research and critical writing methods, performance and embodied praxis, and knowledge of visual cultures and media. Provides mentorship for research, writing, and revision processes. Focuses on research and writing skills, peer reviews, and field-based work.
prerequisites_text: BLKS 193A with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; restricted to class level standing of senior; or consent of instructor

subject: BLKS
title: Black Study Inland Empire Community Initiative
description: Introduces community engagement including prevention of social problems and promotion of well-being in diverse contexts. Critically examines how to define and propose solutions to social and institutional problems. Covers empowerment, resilience, diversity, cultural competence, and social action. Involves service learning through community organizations in Inland Empire communities. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: BLKS 001, BLKS 002, BLKS 003; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: BLKS
title: Directed Research Or Creative Activity in Black Study
description: Concentrated, in-depth study with a faculty member. Enables conduct of interdisciplinary research in one or two of the upper-division track concentrations in the Black Study major. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: BLKS 001, BLKS 002, BLKS 003; or equivalent; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; and consent of instructor

subject: BMSC
title: Freshman Advising Seminar For Medical Scholars Program Students
description: Introduction to UCR for students in the Medical Scholars Program. Focuses on learning the necessary survival skills to succeed in college and prepare for a career in the allied health sciences. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: freshman standing in the Medical Scholars Program

subject: BMSC
title: First-Year Seminar For Medical Scholars Program Students: Topics in Health Careers
description: A discussion of health careers in biomedical sciences and allied health sciences for students in the Medical Scholars Program. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: freshman standing in the Medical Scholars Program or consent of instructor

subject: BMSC
title: Seminar For Medical Scholars Program Students
description: A discussion of special topics in biomedical sciences and allied health sciences as they pertain to students in the Medical Scholars Program. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: lower-division standing in the Medical Scholars Program or consent of instructor

subject: BMSC
title: Independent Reading
description: Independent study under faculty supervision. Possible topics include modern approaches to the pathophysiology of disease, delivery of medical care to the community, or current medical education. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 4 units.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: BMSC
title: Research Tutorial in Biomedical Sciences
description: Laboratory tutorial in research related to biomedical sciences. To provide laboratory experience in the areas of physiology, microbiology, molecular biology, pharmacology, cell biology, immunology, biochemistry for exceptional lower-division students. A written report is required at the end of each quarter. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). May be repeated for up to 6 units.
prerequisites_text: grade point of 3.0 and consent of instructor

subject: BMSC
title: Seminar in Biomedical Sciences
description: Special topics in biomedical sciences, healthcare delivery, cultural competency, biomedical research, and related areas. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 6 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing in the Medical Scholars Program or consent of instructor

subject: BMSC
title: Independent Reading
description: Independent study will be conducted under faculty supervision. A written report to be graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 4 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor and Divisional Dean Independent study involving library projects on topics related to Biomedical Sciences

subject: BMSC
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: An introduction to the methods of research in biomedical sciences. The student will conduct investigation in an area of biomedical sciences under the supervision of a Division of Biomedical Sciences faculty member and submit a written report on his/her work. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing (completion of 90 quarter units) and consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Plants and Human Affairs
description: An introduction for non-science and non-Botany majors to the importance of plants and plant products in the shaping of human affairs and civilization. Covers the origin and practice of agriculture; the utilization of plant products; the latest agricultural advances including genetic engineering; and the current agricultural and social issues.

subject: BPSC
title: California’s Cornucopia: Food From the Field to Your Table
description: Examines California’s diverse agricultural products. Addresses related contemporary issues such as crop improvement by biotechnology, climate change, pollution, resource use, and nutrition. Also examines how the interplay of geography, history, and culture shapes the cuisine of a region.

subject: BPSC
title: Spring Wildflowers
description: Secondary emphasis on the field biology of flowering plants.
prerequisites_text: none General approach to the study of vegetative and floral features of plants as a means of identification and botanical classification of major plant families in Southern California

subject: BPSC
title: The Evidence For Evolution
description: Introduces and explores the extensive evidence supporting evolution as the driver of biological diversity. Designed for non-science majors and/or those with limited prior knowledge about biology. Includes the scientific method, paleontology, natural selection, genetics, speciation, and the importance of sex. Addresses the broader need for scientific literacy in society. Cross-listed with ENTM 050.

subject: BPSC
title: Scicomm: Exploring Effective Communication Methods in the Life Sciences
description: Teaches the process of analyzing and translating scientific research into popular science stories. Introduces the art of science communication through written narratives. Provides resources and guidance on interpretation of scientific literature; interviewing scientists; and pursuing careers in entomology, the broader life sciences, and science writing. Fulfills the third-quarter writing requirement for students who earn a grade of “C” or better for courses that the Academic Senate designates, and that the student’s college permits, as alternatives to WRIT 030. Cross-listed with ENTM 060W.
prerequisites_text: WRIT 040P, may be taken concurrently; WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better; BIOL 005A with a grade of C- or better

subject: BPSC
title: Lower-Division Research
description: Involves special research projects in plant biology performed under faculty supervision. Requires a final written report. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 6 units.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Foundations of Plant Biology
description: A study of the plant world from cells to ecosystems. Examines the structure and function of organisms from the major plant groups and their role in the biosphere. The laboratory explores the unique properties of plants. Cross-listed with BIOL 104.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C

subject: BPSC
title: Epigenetics
description: Introduction to mechanisms that cause a heritable change in phenotype without a change in the genetic code. Covers DNA modifications, histone modifications, and noncoding RNAs that influence the expression, maintenance, and inheritance of traits. Discusses impacts of epigenetics on multicellular life such as learning, memory, disease, and crosstalk with environments. Cross-listed with CBNS 109.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 102; BIOL 107A or BCH 110C

subject: BPSC
title: Systematics
description: Principles and philosophy of classification. Topics include phylogenetic and phenetic methods, species concepts, taxonomic characters, evolution, hierarchy of categories, and nomenclature. Cross-listed with BIOL 112, and ENTM 112.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C or equivalent

subject: BPSC
title: Plant Anatomy
description: Explores the functional and developmental aspects of plant cell, tissue, and organ structure. Covers all aspects of the flowering plant life cycle from germination to pollination and fruit and seed development. Cross-listed with BIOL 132.
prerequisites_text: BPSC 104 or BIOL 104; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Plant Diversity and Evolution
description: Introduces the principles and methods of identifying, naming, and classifying flowering plants. Surveys selected flowering plant families in California and shows their interrelationships.
prerequisites_text: BPSC 104 or BIOL 104; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Soil Conditions and Plant Growth
description: A study of the chemical, physical, and biological properties of soils and their influence on plant growth and development. Topics include soil-plant water relations; fundamentals of plant mineral nutrition; soil nutrient pools and cycles; soil acidity, alkalinity, salinity, and sodicity; root symbioses; and rhizosphere processes. Cross-listed with ENSC 134.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 104/BPSC 104 or ENSC 100; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Plant Molecular and Cell Biology:concepts and Applications
description: Introduces concepts of plant molecular biology and the dynamics of plant cell structures and functions. Explores applications in biotechnology as revealed by modern technologies such as gene editing, microscopy, and live imaging.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Plant Developmental Morphology
description: Introduces the key areas of research in plant morphology and developmental biology. Emphasizes flowering plants (angiosperms). Cross-listed with BIOL 138.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C, PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC, PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100, may be taken concurrently or BCH 100H, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110A, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110HA, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Plant Physiology
description: A survey of the fundamental principles of plant physiology including photosynthesis, respiration, water relations, mineral nutrition, growth, morphogenesis, plant hormones, dormancy, and senescence. Cross-listed with BIOL 143.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C, MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC, PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100, may be taken concurrently or BCH 100H, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110A, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110HA, may be taken concurrently; BPSC 104 or BIOL 104; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Geospatial Analytics For Landscape Ecology
description: Builds on the basic understanding of fundamental concepts of Geographic Information Science (GIScience). Applies spatial data concepts to understand the ecological impacts of human activities across landscapes. Examines the link between landscape patterns and ecological processes at larger spatial scales.
prerequisites_text: PBPL 010; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Plant Ecology
description: A study of the fundamentals of plant ecology. Emphasizes community ecology, environment, life histories, population dynamics, species interactions, succession, ecosystem and landscape ecology, and plant conservation ecology. Cross-listed with BIOL 146.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 104 or BPSC 104 or BIOL 116; STAT 010; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Quantitative Genetics
description: Examines approaches to studying the genetic basis of polygenic metric traits. Includes types of gene action, partitioning of variance, response to selection, and inferring the number and location of quantitative trait loci. Cross-listed with BIOL 148.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC, PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; STAT 011; BCH 100, may be taken concurrently or BCH 100H, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110A, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110HA, may be taken concurrently; BIOL 102

subject: BPSC
title: Nanobiotechnology
description: An Introduction to fundamental concepts of the emergent field of nanobiotechnology and its application to plant and medical sciences. Topics include nanomaterial-mediated genome editing and transformation, targeted and controlled drug delivery, nanosensors for electrical signals and signaling molecules, and cyborg plants and animals with augmented or novel functions.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; BIOL 102; CHEM 008C or CHEM 08HC, CHEM 08LC or CHEM 08HLC; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC, PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC or PHYS 040C or PHYS 040HC; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Genes, Selection, and Populations
description: Considers the conscious manipulation of allelic frequencies in populations as the basis for domestication of crop and animal species. Examines the genetic basis and standard strategies for the improvement of targeted characteristics in populations of plants and animals through selection and introgression of specific genes and gene constructs.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 102 with a grade of “C-” or better, upper-division standing; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Chromosomes
description: An examination of the structure, function, and behavior of eukaryotic chromosomes. Cross-listed with BIOL 155.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C, MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC, PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100, may be taken concurrently or BCH 100H, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110A, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110HA, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Restoration Ecology
description: An examination of the basic ecological principles related to land restoration. Topics include enhanced succession; plant establishment; plant adaptations; ecotype; weed colonization and competition; nutrient cycling; functions and reintroduction of soil microorganisms; restoration for wildlife; and the determination of successful restoration. Includes field trips to restored sites. Cross-listed with BIOL 165.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 104 or BPSC 104 or BIOL 116 or ENSC 100; CHEM 008B, CHEM 08LB or CHEM 08HB, CHEM 08HLB; STAT 010, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Plant Physiological Ecology
description: Topics include plant responses to light, temperature, evaporative demand, and limiting soil conditions. Explores photosynthesis, plant-water relations, and plant-temperature relations. Gives attention to plant adaptation to climates with varying aridity and temperature extremes.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C or consent of instructor; university-level courses in mathematics, physics, and chemistry are recommended

subject: BPSC
title: Forest Ecology
description: An introduction to the ecology of forest ecosystems. Explores modern research and management in the field. Topics include major forest types within California, tree physiology, forest soils, forest population and community dynamics, wildfire, and forest management. Includes combination of indoor laboratory, field labs, and field trip to local forest. Cross-listed with BIOL 167.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 116

subject: BPSC
title: Plant Biochemistry and Pharmacology of Plant Metabolites
description: Explores plant biochemistry and the significance of plant metabolites in medicine and pharmacology. Focuses on biotechnology, medicinal plants, and plant-derived drugs as well as the biochemical and pharmacological mode-of-action of secondary plant metabolites. Also addresses plant-specific biochemical processes such as photosynthesis. Cross-listed with BCH 183.
prerequisites_text: BCH 110A or BCH 110HA, BCH 110B or BCH 110HB or BCH 100; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Planning For A Postgraduate Career in Life Sciences
description: Introduces life science majors to diverse career options in industry, government, and academia. Develops skills for finding and acquiring jobs. Emphasizes careers in the agricultural sciences, biotechnology, and related areas through presentations by professionals representing a variety of educational levels and careers. Cross-listed with ENTM 184.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; restricted to major(s) Biochemistry, Biology, Cell, Molecular, and Developme, Entomology, Microbiology, Neuroscience, Plant Biology; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Special Studies
description: Library, laboratory or field work designed to meet special curricular needs. A written proposal signed by the supervising faculty member must be approved by the major advisor and the Department Vice Chair. A written report must be filed. Course is repeatable, but total credit toward graduation may not exceed 6 units.

subject: BPSC
title: Seminar in Agricultural Careers in the 21st Century
description: Introduces students to diverse career options in agriculture and biotechnology through seminars and interviews with industry, government, and academic professionals. Develops skillsets for finding and acquiring jobs in agricultural and biotechnology. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC)
prerequisites_text: sophomore or junior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Senior Seminar
description: Emphasizes thinking across hierarchical levels and understanding structure-function relationships in plant biology. Includes lectures and presentation of classical or landmark papers. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: BPSC 104 or BIOL 104; 2 of the following: BIOL 143, BPSC 143, BPSC 133, BPSC 132, BIOL 132; restricted to class level standing of senior; restricted to major(s) Plant Biology; or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Senior Honors Thesis
description: Directed research and completion of a senior Honors thesis under the supervision of a faculty member. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: upper division standing; admission to University Honors or consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: Individual research conducted under the direction of a Botany and Plant Sciences faculty member. A written proposal must be approved by the supervising faculty member and undergraduate advisor. A written report must be filed with the supervising faculty member at the end of the quarter. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Individual Internship in Botany and Plant Sciences
description: An off-campus internship related to plant biology. The student conducts the internship in the public or private sector but is jointly supervised by an off-campus sponsor and a faculty member in Botany and Plant Sciences. Requires an initial written proposal and a final written report. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of instructor

subject: BPSC
title: Senior Research
description: Individual research on a problem relating to Botany/ Plant Science. A written proposal signed by the supervising faculty member must be approved by the major advisor and the Department Vice Chair. A written report must be filed with the supervising faculty member. Course is repeatable, but total credit toward graduation may not exceed 9 units.
prerequisites_text: senior status; a GPA of 3.2 or better in upper-division courses in Botany/Plant Science and Biology; or consent of instructor

subject: BUAS
title: Fundamentals of Insurance
description: Introduces the insurance industry and the pricing of actuarial risks. Topics include asymmetric information, adverse selection, and moral hazard as they apply to life insurance and property and casualty policies, state regulations, and models for regulatory capital and reinsurance.
prerequisites_text: BUS 106 or ECON 134 or BUS 133

subject: BUS
title: Personal Finance
description: Provides students with tools necessary to analyze the decision to finance their UCR education with student loans. Topics include personal budgets, student loans, interest rates, career planning, auto and health insurance, and other issues related to financing higher education. Credit is awarded for only one of BUS 001 or BUS 001H.

subject: BUS
title: Personal Finance
description: Honors course corresponding to BUS 001. Provides students with tools necessary to analyze the decision to finance their UCR education with student loans. Topics include personal budgets, student loans, interest rates, career planning, auto and health insurance, and other issues related to financing higher education. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Credit is awarded for only one of BUS 001 or BUS 001H.
prerequisites_text: admission to University Honors or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Business
description: Provides an overview of the field of business administration. Explores business goals and strategies; functional areas of business and their integration in policy and decision making; social responsibility; computers in business; and business trends and challenges including the international dimension.

subject: BUS
title: Financial Accounting and Reporting
description: A study of the concepts and techniques for measurement and communication of financial information. Includes interpretation of financial statements.

subject: BUS
title: Generation of Financial Accounting Information
description: A detailed study of the process of measuring, recording, and communicating financial accounting information. .
prerequisites_text: BUS 020 with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: BUS
title: Freshman Success in the Classroom
description: Provides first-year Business students with the tools needed to be successful in the classroom. Provides exposure to different resources, opportunities, and groups for networking to help with a smooth transition into a Business major. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: restricted to major(s) Actuarial Science, Business Analytics

subject: BUS
title: Freshman Success Beyond the Classroom
description: Provides tools needed to successfully prepare for a career while at the School of Business. Explores resources, opportunities, and networks to develop a career plan. Includes engagement in experiential learning to ensure success beyond the classroom. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: BUS 094; restricted to major(s) Actuarial Science, Business Analytics

subject: BUS
title: Transfer Success in the Classroom
description: Provides transfer Business students with the tools needed to be successful in the classroom and in preparing for their careers. Provides exposure to different resources, opportunities, and groups for networking to help with a smooth transition into a Business major. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: restricted to major(s) Actuarial Science, Business Administration, Business Analytics

subject: BUS
title: Business Pathways to Success
description: Provides new Business students with the tools needed to be successful in the classroom. Provides exposure to different resources, opportunities, and groups for networking to help with a smooth transition into a Business major. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: restricted to major(s) Pre-Business

subject: BUS
title: Personal Branding and Professional Development
description: Prepares for successful internships and develops critical career management skills through greater understanding of abilities and preferences as well as available job search resources. Explores career-enhancing techniques such as self-assessment, career research, resume writing, networking, interviewing, and professionalism. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).

subject: BUS
title: Management Writing and Communication
description: Focuses on writing and communication methods in the business environment. Topics include written and oral presentations, interpersonal skills, teamwork in the multicultural setting, and effective use of communication technologies. Fulfills the third-quarter writing requirement for students who earn a grade of “C” or better for courses that the Academic Senate designates, and that the student’s college permits, as alternatives to WRIT 030.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 040E; WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better; BUS 020; ECON 003 or ECON 003H; STAT 008; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Information Technology Management
description: Topics include computer hardware and software, business data processing, databases, telecommunications, systems analysis and design, cost-benefit analysis, and systems applications in business. Includes database and spreadsheet projects.
prerequisites_text: BUS 020; ECON 003; STAT 008; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Ethics and Law in Business and Society
description: Analyzes the legal, ethical, political, and social aspects of the business environment. Topics include ethics and social responsibility, government regulation, corporate governance, and global management issues.
prerequisites_text: BUS 020; ECON 003; STAT 008; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Marketing and Distribution Management
description: An introduction to the role of marketing in society emphasizing concepts, marketing methods, and institutions.
prerequisites_text: BUS 020; ECON 003 or ECON 003H, STAT 008; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Decision Analysis and Management Science
description: A survey of deterministic and probabilistic models for decision making. Topics include linear programming and extensions, networks, dynamic programming, decision trees, queuing models, and simulation. Explores the application of these models in decision making. Cross-listed with STAT 104.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010; or equivalents; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Production and Operations Management
description: Addresses the issues of design and control of production systems in manufacturing and service organizations. Covers product and process selection, capacity planning, location and layout design, project and job scheduling, inventory control, material planning, and quality control.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010; or equivalent

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Financial Management
description: An introduction to financial management and financial institutions. Includes time value of money, stock and bond valuation, risk and return, portfolio theory, capital budgeting, capital structure, dividend policy, and financial databases. Cross-listed with ECON 134. Credit is awarded for one of the following BUS 106, ECON 134, or BUS 133.
prerequisites_text: BUS 020; ECON 003 or ECON 003H; STAT 008 or ECON 101; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Organizational Behavior
description: Studies organizations from the behavioral science perspective. Topics include motivation, leadership, communication, groups, organization structure and culture, and control in complex organizations.
prerequisites_text: BUS 020; ECON 003; STAT 008; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Financial Evaluation and Managerial Analysis
description: A study of accounting data used for managerial planning and controlling of business operations. Provides an introduction to manufacturing operations and cost accounting systems, cost-volume-profit analysis, relevant costing, standard costing and variance analysis, and budgeting.
prerequisites_text: BUS 020; ECON 003; STAT 008; or equivalents; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Competitive and Strategic Analysis
description: Provides an understanding of strategic decision-making processes in organizations, the interrelationships among functional areas, and how decision making is affected by internal and external environments.
prerequisites_text: BUS 100W; BUS 103; BUS 108; BUS 106 or ECON 134 or BUS 133; restricted to major(s) Business Administration

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Data Mining and Visual Analytics
description: Covers the processes, methodologies and practices used to transform data into useful information to support business decision-making. Offers an opportunity to gain insights and hands-on-experience with basic functionality of industry standard data mining and visualization software tools such as Tableau, JMP and IBM’s Watson Analytic.
prerequisites_text: BUS 101

subject: BUS
title: Services Marketing
description: Covers the marketing of services and ideas. Focuses on marketing for service organizations such as hotels, hospitals, and banks. Provides understanding of the broader role of service provision for both service firms and goods firms.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103

subject: BUS
title: Consumer Behavior
description: Provides a basic understanding of the general models of choice behavior as it relates to marketing decision making. Emphasizes motivation, perceptions, learning, and social forces as they impact the choice process.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103

subject: BUS
title: Marketing Channels
description: Covers the concepts and strategies relating to the distribution of products and services through retail and wholesale business channels. Focus on the management of marketing and Salesforce activities within these channels of distribution.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103

subject: BUS
title: Marketing in A Global Environment
description: Covers the theory and practice of marketing across national borders. Provides an understanding of global marketing environments and examines the development of marketing strategies to maximize growth of global companies.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103

subject: BUS
title: Marketing Research
description: Covers types and sources of marketing information, the marketing research process, and techniques of data collection and analysis, including consumer and customer surveys and test marketing. Examines both quantitative and qualitative research with analysis of the values and limitations of data. Emphasis is placed on evaluation and interpretation of results.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103

subject: BUS
title: Pricing Strategy and Management
description: Integrates theory and practice into a framework for making pricing decisions. Prepares for addressing strategic and tactical pricing issues. Topics include customer demand and price sensitivity, psychological reaction to price, segmented pricing, price promotions, bundling, online pricing, dynamic pricing, competitive reaction, profitability analysis, and pricing strategy development.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103 or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Advertising and Integrated Marketing Communications
description: Covers the basic concepts and functions of advertising, sales promotion, and other communication tools in an integrated marketing communications framework.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103

subject: BUS
title: Digital Marketing
description: An introduction to the role of digital marketing in business-to-consumer and business-to-business marketing. Covers the application of traditional marketing principles to an electronic commerce environment and new digital marketing techniques made possible by this environment.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103

subject: BUS
title: Data-Driven Marketing
description: Examines marketing cases and develops data analytical skills for managerial decision making. Utilizes statistical software to manage, display, and analyze marketing information including consumer survey, relationship management, scanner, and socioeconomic data. Topics include attitude measurement, market segmentation and targeting, competition analysis, market performance analysis, and store location choice.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Global Strategy
description: Introduces global strategic management and how to win the global marketplace. Covers topics including the challenges of creating the right kind of organization, motivating a global workforce, entering new markets, creating global competitive advantage, and building a global mindset.
prerequisites_text: BUS 109 or equivalents

subject: BUS
title: Employee Benefits
description: Provides a foundation of knowledge regarding employee benefits and the design and management of employee benefit plans. Discusses current issues and recent developments in the ever-changing field regarding employee benefits-related topics.
prerequisites_text: BUS 107

subject: BUS
title: Spreadsheet Modeling For Decision-Making
description: Introduces the fundamental techniques of using data to make informed management decisions in the presence of uncertainty. Utilizes advanced Microsoft Excel functionality.
prerequisites_text: BUS 104 or STAT 104

subject: BUS
title: Business Analytics
description: Provides fundamental concepts and tools needed to understand the emerging role of business analytics in organizations. Applies basic business analytics tools in a spreadsheet environment. Introduces market-leading techniques that help identify and manage key data from business processes. Provides the essential tools required for data mining and business process re-engineering.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010 or ECON 101

subject: BUS
title: Simulation For Business
description: Introduces simulation as a tool for analyzing complex systems. Analyzes and discusses the theory and practice of modeling through simulation. Topics include modeling uncertainty and collecting input data, Monte Carlo simulation techniques, model verification and validation, and sensitivity analysis. Examines applications in finance, marketing, operations, and supply chain management.
prerequisites_text: BUS 104 or STAT 104; or equivalents

subject: BUS
title: Practical Business Forecasting
description: Teaches how forecasts are developed and utilized. Emphasizes common forecasting methods used in business and uses specific cases to illustrate these methods. Applications to business include forecasting sales, production, inventory, macroeconomic factors such as interest and exchange rates, and other aspects of both short- and long-term business planning.
prerequisites_text: BUS 105; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Quality Improvements
description: Explores Deming’s 14 points for management, graphical methods, fishbone diagram, Pareto analysis, control charts for attributes and variables, cusum and moving average charts, and process-capability. Also covers economic design, acceptance sampling, Taguchi method, parameter design, tolerance design, reliability, hazard rate, censoring, and accelerated life testing. Cross-listed with STAT 127.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010; or ECON 101

subject: BUS
title: Project Planning and Control
description: Covers issues related to planning and control. Explores the differences between projects and production systems; breakdown structures of project organization and work; sequencing and budgeting; resource management; project evaluation and control; and use of current project management software. Includes application of methodology to a real-world project.
prerequisites_text: BUS 104/STAT 104 or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Supply Chain Management
description: Focuses on management of the distribution of goods and services from plants, ports, and vendors to customers. Key topics include transportation, inventories, warehousing, materials handling, order processing, packaging, pricing, customer service standards, and warehouse and retail location.
prerequisites_text: BUS 105

subject: BUS
title: Quantitative Business Decision Models
description: Covers the modeling and analysis of decision problems in supply chain management. Includes logistics network design, integration of supply chain operations, and supply and sourcing decisions. Utilizes the electronic spreadsheet as the principal device for building models, as well as addresses the concepts of effective spreadsheet design and use. If BUS 130 has been completed with a passing grade with the title of “Supply Chain Modeling” the new BUS 130 “Quantitative Business Decision Models” may not be taken for credit.
prerequisites_text: BUS 104 or BUS 105 or STAT 104

subject: BUS
title: Fixed-Income Securities
description: Covers fixed-income securities and basic analytical tools in fixed-income markets. Topics include relative pricing of fixed-income securities, yield-curve estimation, securities with embedded options, and trading strategies. Utilizes instruments such as interest rate swaps, mortgage-backed securities, and credit derivatives.
prerequisites_text: BUS 133 or BUS 132; BUS 106 or ECON 134

subject: BUS
title: Foundations of Finance
description: Covers the mathematical and economic foundations of finance. Topics include intertemporal production and consumption; fisher separation; risk and return; two-fund separation; standard asset-pricing models; arbitrage; derivatives concepts and parity relationships; and international finance parity relationships. Credit is awarded for one of the following BUS 132 or BUS 133.
prerequisites_text: BUS 020; STAT 008 or STAT 010 or ECON 101

subject: BUS
title: Accelerated Foundations of Finance
description: Covers materials from BUS 106/ ECON 134 and ECON 132. Examines investment and operational decisions of individuals and companies. Covers relationship between investment decisions, wealth, and risk tolerance. Addresses operational decisions from the perspective of an entrepreneur or manager. Pursues strategies that personally appeal rather than investments that maximize shareholder value. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available. Credit is awarded for one of the following BUS 133, BUS 106, BUS 132, or ECON 134.
prerequisites_text: STAT 004 with a grade of B or better, BUS 020 with a grade of B or better or STAT 008 with a grade of B or better or STAT 010 with a grade of B or better or ECON 101 with a grade of B or better; ECON 003 with a grade of B or better or ECON 003H with a grade of B or better; ECON 102 with a grade of B or better or ECON 103 with a grade of B or better or ECON 104A with a grade of B or better or ECON 105A with a grade of B or better; or a score of 3 or higher on the Advance Placement exam in Statistics; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Corporate Finance
description: Explores capital budgeting under uncertainty, cost of capital, capital structure, and basics of corporate governance. May cover other related topics. Provides an understanding of the theoretical issues related to these topics. Emphasizes formulating optimal financial decisions. May include case-method teaching and data analysis.
prerequisites_text: BUS 133 with a grade of C- or better; 2 of the following: ECON 134, BUS 106, BUS 132

subject: BUS
title: Corporate Financial Policy
description: Covers application of option pricing in corporate finance, financial planning, working capital management, mergers and acquisitions, and risk management. May cover other related topics. Emphasizes formulating optimal financial decisions. May include case-method teaching and data analysis.
prerequisites_text: BUS 133 with a grade of C- or better or BUS 132 with a grade of C- or better; BUS 106 with a grade of C- or better or ECON 134 with a grade of C- or better

subject: BUS
title: Investments: Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
description: Provides a thorough study of the investment process. Topics include portfolio selection, asset-pricing models, term structure, and portfolio performance valuation. Discusses empirical uses of securities data and empirical issues in testing asset pricing models.
prerequisites_text: BUS 133 with a grade of C- or better; 2 of the following: BUS 106, ECON 134, BUS 132

subject: BUS
title: Investments: Derivatives Markets
description: Covers option market characteristics, option pricing theories, and speculative strategies used in local, national, and international markets. Analyzes other derivatives instruments including futures, forwards, and swaps. Discusses empirical uses of securities data related to derivatives markets.
prerequisites_text: BUS 133 with a grade of C- or better or BUS 132 with a grade of C- or better; BUS 106 with a grade of C- or better or ECON 134 with a grade of C- or better

subject: BUS
title: International Finance
description: A survey of international financial institutions and the financial factors that affect the modern multinational corporation. Covers trade and international investment theories and empirical analysis. Topics include the international financial systems, balance of payments, foreign exchange markets, measurement of foreign exchange risk, hedging, international asset pricing, and trade financing.
prerequisites_text: BUS 133 with a grade of C- or better or BUS 132 with a grade of C- or better; BUS 106 or ECON 134

subject: BUS
title: Real Estate Investments
description: Analysis of real estate development including consideration of site selection, market analysis, financing, design and construction, loan contracts, mortgage risks, and investment analysis.
prerequisites_text: BUS 133 or BUS 132; BUS 106 or ECON 134

subject: BUS
title: (E-Z) Current Topics in Finance
description: Addresses contemporary issues in finance. Includes financial markets, private equity, asset pricing, performance evaluation, derivative securities, market micro structure, corporate finance, corporate control and governance, and the global economy. Explores recent developments in theoretical, empirical, and applied finance. Also addresses the regulatory and ethical environment of finance. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: BUS 106 or ECON 134 or BUS 133

subject: BUS
title: Current Topics in Finance
description: Focuses on the current financial crisis. Includes bank, investment bank, insurance company, and other financial institution failures and the government and market responses to them. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: BUS 106 with a grade of C- or better or ECON 134 or BUS 133

subject: BUS
title: Trading Strategies
description: Introduces stock market anomalies. Includes ways to predict market strength, to profit, and to understanding the risk and trading costs of performing such trading strategies. Considers the most well-known empirical deviations from the capital asset pricing model (CAPM) and trading strategies.
prerequisites_text: BUS 133, BUS 136 or BUS 132, BUS 136, BUS 106 or ECON 134

subject: BUS
title: Banks and Risks of Financial Institutions
description: Examines financial institutions in the United States with an emphasis on banks and their competitors. Focuses on the risks these institutions are exposed to and their sources. Topics include deposits, loans, regulation, interest rate risk, credit risk, mutual funds, hedge funds, insurance, and pension funds.
prerequisites_text: BUS 132 or BUS 133; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Judgment and Decision Making
description: Covers decision making, including thinking and judgments; information selection and evaluation; learning and memory; the social side of judgment and decision making; fairness, moral obligations, and social dilemmas; and decision making in organizations.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Negotiation Fundamentals
description: Develops an understanding of the theory and processes underlying a broad spectrum of negotiation problems. Attains competency in negotiations by applying analytic and interpersonal skills covered in readings and lecture to regular exercises and debriefings.
prerequisites_text: BUS 107

subject: BUS
title: Designing and Leading Teams
description: A general survey of the dynamics and effective management of teams within organizations. Explores the nature of teamwork through the creation of shared goals and actions to facilitate organizational effectiveness. Addresses the roles of individuals in teams. Enhances theoretical knowledge of teams through critical application in real-team situations.
prerequisites_text: BUS 107; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
description: Discusses the nature of entrepreneurship and its role in the economy. Topics include identifying and evaluating business opportunities, creating a team, and acquiring financial and other necessary resources.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Entrepreneurial Finance
description: Focuses on the financing of entrepreneurial ventures. Provides an understanding of opportunity recognition skills, funding techniques, and institutions involved in the financing of new ventures. Includes financial modeling, cash needs assessment, valuation, deal structure, financing alternatives, simulation, and harvesting.
prerequisites_text: BUS 133 with a grade of C- or better or BUS 132 with a grade of C- or better; BUS 106 with a grade of C- or better or ECON 134 with a grade of C- or better

subject: BUS
title: Business Plan Development
description: Provides the skills necessary to assess new venture opportunities and convert them into businesses.
prerequisites_text: BUS 107; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Advanced Topics in Management and Decision-Making
description: Covers advanced topics in management and decision-making. Includes incentives and motivation, social labor, the psychology of money, competition and markets, grey marketing and revenge, dishonesty and cheating, decision-making in groups, other-regarding preferences, and welfare inferences and well-being.
prerequisites_text: BUS 107; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Corporate Strategic Analysis in Multi-Business Firms
description: Explores the distinct challenges multi-business organizations face when creating and reviewing their corporate-level strategies. Topics include mergers and acquisitions, alliances, outsourcing, reorganizations, diversification, and change implementation. Emphasizes how top management can identify opportunities, define the corporate headquarter’s role, and create value for the businesses it holds.
prerequisites_text: BUS 109, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Brand Management
description: Provides an understanding of how to manage a brand or a branded product. Topics include brand development and equity, brand architecture and brand leveraging, and managing a brand over the product life cycle.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103 or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Sales Management
description: Discusses strategic and tactical aspects of sales force management including sales force planning, deployment, compensation, and control. Also covers selling strategies and managing of customer relationships.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103

subject: BUS
title: Labor Economics
description: An analysis of labor demand, labor supply, market equilibrium, and policies affecting each. Topics include labor supply, labor demand, minimum wages, government transfers, education, job training, and discrimination. Cross-listed with ECON 153.
prerequisites_text: ECON 102 or ECON 104A

subject: BUS
title: Business Law
description: Studies law as an integral part of the business environment, a process derived from and changing with the larger society. Areas covered include contracts, torts, agency, partnerships, corporations, and bankruptcy.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing

subject: BUS
title: Managing Human Resources
description: Applies a strategic planning approach to managing relations between an organization and its human resources. Topics include processes of forecasting and job analysis, environmental scanning, recruitment and selection, evaluation and compensation, and dispute resolution.
prerequisites_text: BUS 107; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Leadership Development
description: Analyzes leadership theory and practice. Surveys areas pertaining to leadership, such as leadership theory, leadership style, oral and written communication, ethical leadership, interpersonal conflict management, and the dynamics of culture and gender in organization leadership.
prerequisites_text: BUS 107; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Managing Work Force Diversity
description: Covers management topics for understanding how to navigate, manage, and lead diverse organizations more effectively. Topics include diversity in organizations, cross-cultural management, research-based strategies for reducing bias in organizations, and workplace inclusion.
prerequisites_text: BUS 107; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Organizations as Cultural Systems
description: Examines the role of culture in the formation and management of complex bureaucratic organizations. Covers types of organizations and organizational cultures, the impact of the cultural environment, and problems posed by rapid cultural change. Offered in summer only. Cross-listed with ANTH 105.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: New Product Development
description: Examines the strategies that lead to successful development of new products. Discusses the tools and techniques used in different stages of a successful new product development process from opportunity identification to market testing and commercialization of the new product.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103 or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Industrial Organization
description: A study of the organization and structure of the American industrial system. Emphasizes production and pricing behavior and policies. Also addresses market structure and public policies regulating or influencing market behavior. Cross-listed with ECON 160.
prerequisites_text: ECON 104B

subject: BUS
title: Forensic and Fraud Auditing
description: An introduction to forensic accounting and fraud examination and how they pertain to both civil and criminal matters. Covers the characteristics of fraud, fraud prevention and detection, investigative techniques, asset recovery, and the use of information technology.
prerequisites_text: BUS 165B

subject: BUS
title: Managerial Economics
description: Examines applications of economic analysis to problems of management, especially of capital. Emphasis is on production economics and cost analysis. Cross-listed with ECON 162.
prerequisites_text: ECON 102 or ECON 104A

subject: BUS
title: Technology Entrepreneurship
description: Provides a process of starting a new technology-based venture from the original idea to commercialization. Introduces a set of cross-functional concepts in technology management, intellectual property laws, marketing, operations and strategy. Concepts apply to a class project focused on the development of a business plan for a technology-based startup.
prerequisites_text: BUS 101

subject: BUS
title: Marketing Strategy
description: Focuses on planning and development of marketing and product portfolio strategies for long-term success. Emphasizes marketing analysis and decision-making through the use of case studies and/or a computer-based marketing simulation.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103 or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting
description: In-depth study of financial accounting theory and practice. Develops an understanding of accounting concepts and generally accepted accounting principles and the ability to apply this technical knowledge to solve accounting problems. Topics include principal financial statements and accounting and valuation of various assets.
prerequisites_text: BUS 021 or equivalent

subject: BUS
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting
description: A continuation of study of financial accounting theory and practice. Topics include current liabilities and contingencies, long-term liabilities, contributed capital, retained earnings, and temporary and long-term investments.
prerequisites_text: BUS 165A

subject: BUS
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting
description: A continuation of study of financial accounting theory and practice. Covers the conceptual discussion and procedural presentation of financial accounting topics as well as recent developments in accounting valuation and reporting practices promulgated by practitioners in industry and public accountants.
prerequisites_text: BUS 165B

subject: BUS
title: Accounting Information Systems
description: Study of the concepts and techniques in the design and implementation of accounting information systems within companies’ operating environments. Emphasis is on the effects of the computer on these systems.
prerequisites_text: BUS 101, BUS 108, or equivalents

subject: BUS
title: Advanced Financial Accounting
description: Covers advanced accounting topics such as consolidated financial statements, accounting for multinational corporations, partnership accounting, and accounting for nonprofit organizations.
prerequisites_text: BUS 165C (may be taken concurrently)

subject: BUS
title: Individual Taxation
description: Concentrates primarily on the basic provisions of the federal income taxes imposed on individuals and the accounting for those taxes. While the major emphasis is on current tax provisions and tax planning, consideration is also given to the legislative and judicial development of these provisions.
prerequisites_text: BUS 108 or equivalent

subject: BUS
title: Federal Taxation For Corporations, Partnerships, Estates, and Trusts
description: Covers tax research, corporate taxation, partnership taxation, the wealth transfer taxes, income taxation of estates and trusts, international taxation, and tax administration.
prerequisites_text: BUS 168A

subject: BUS
title: Auditing
description: Covers the auditing environment, the auditor’s legal liability, audit responsibilities and objectives, audit evidence, audit planning and documentation, the auditor’s report, and management letters.
prerequisites_text: BUS 165B, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Quality Assurance in Auditing
description: Covers the audit process (internal control, compliance tests, sampling, substantive evidence gathering, electronic data processing auditing) and the audit procedures for various types of accounts such as sales, cash, accounts receivable, payroll, inventory, and capital acquisitions.
prerequisites_text: BUS 169A

subject: BUS
title: Financial Statement Valuation
description: Explains weighted average cost of capital as used in operating income based, revenue based, and market based valuation methods. Requires research to determine valuation of an existing publicly held company under all three methods. Also considers off balance sheet financing, credit risk analysis, and minority interests.
prerequisites_text: BUS 165B, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Systems Analysis and Design
description: Involves detailed analysis, specification, design, and implementation of computer-based information systems. Includes economic analyses, evaluation of alternatives, analysis or design tools, and systems project management and planning. Case studies are used.
prerequisites_text: BUS 101 or equivalent

subject: BUS
title: Information Economics
description: Discusses economic concepts and strategies related to the network economy. Topics include economic issues surrounding information goods, competition in electronic business, pricing strategies, and intellectual property protections. Examines business strategies for the information (software) and infrastructure (hardware) elements of electronic business.
prerequisites_text: BUS 103; ECON 003 or ECON 003H

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Databases For Management
description: Covers physical and conceptual aspects of database management systems, including familiarity with the variety of database systems based on different data models. Examines the role of database systems in management information systems (MIS) and issues in database design for effective support of MIS. Requires the use of a database package.
prerequisites_text: BUS 101 or equivalent

subject: BUS
title: Electronic Commerce
description: Reviews the technological evolution of electronic commerce (EC). Investigates how EC can be used to interact with customers, other organizations, and those within the organization. Studies technical innovations, provides a critical evaluation of strategies, and examines current applications and their impact on the business environment.
prerequisites_text: BUS 101

subject: BUS
title: Business Data Communications
description: Surveys components of telecommunication systems; examines major design and analysis issues in the development and implementation of computer communication systems. Studies both voice and data communication systems including local area networks, wireless systems, satellite systems, and distributed computer and database systems. Emphasizes evaluation of these systems for business purposes.
prerequisites_text: BUS 101

subject: BUS
title: The Sociology of Work in Organizations
description: Emphasizes the roles of individuals in organizations. Topics include the effects of jobs on workers, long-term trends in the nature of work, and differences in work among major segments of the labor force. Cross-listed with SOC 176.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Labor Relations
description: Explores the foundation of knowledge regarding labor in the United States. Emphasizes the historical development of unionism, labor legislation, union structure, bargaining issues, contract negotiations and administration, and labor-management relations.
prerequisites_text: BUS 010

subject: BUS
title: International Trade
description: A study of the pure theory of trade, trade policy, and international factor movements. Includes illustrative applications to current issues and problems. Cross-listed with ECON 178.
prerequisites_text: ECON 102 or ECON 104A

subject: BUS
title: Business Application of Geographic Information Systems
description: Includes introduction to and use of geographic information system (GIS) for business applications. Provides basic understanding on how location information is used in business processes for decisions. Offers an opportunity to gain hands-on experience with basic functionality of industry standard business mapping software tools including ArcGIS and Business Analyst Online.
prerequisites_text: BUS 101

subject: BUS
title: (E-Z) Topics in Accountancy
description: Consist of topics in Accountancy for business majors.
prerequisites_text: see individual segments for prerequisites

subject: BUS
title: Accounting Research
description: Introduces methods, tools, and critical thinking skills needed to conduct professional research in accounting and auditing. Topics include identification and framing of complex accounting issues, navigation of the authoritative literature promulgated by standard-setting bodies, and communication of research findings in a clear and professional manner.
prerequisites_text: BUS 165B; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Accounting Ethics & Professional Responsibilities
description: Provides the ethical grounding that professional accountants need to identify ethical issues that they might face and to respond effectively to them. Includes exposure to ethics-related issues in financial accounting and reporting, management accounting, audit, taxation, accounting information systems, forensic accounting, and accounting-related consulting.
prerequisites_text: BUS 108

subject: BUS
title: Data Analytics For Accountants
description: Introduces the mindset, tools, and techniques of data analytics as applied to the accounting profession. Explores practical application of how to use modern software to solve real-world accounting problems. Topics include acquisition and transformation of messy data, performing descriptive and diagnostic analyses, and visualizing findings in interactive dashboards.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010; BUS 108; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Governmental and Not-For-Profit Accounting
description: Introduces accounting for nonprofit entities including their financial reporting objectives and examination of government auditing standards. Examines the basic principles of governmental accounting under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP). Emphasizes the state and local government financial reporting model promulgated by the Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB).
prerequisites_text: BUS 165B

subject: BUS
title: Business Modeling and Optimization
description: Teaches the analytical approach to business decision making and performance improvement. Focuses on how to structure and analyze business problems to arrive at optimal solutions and compelling insights. Covers applications in marketing, operations, supply chain, and finance. Techniques include probability, statistics, and optimization.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010 or ECON 101; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Business Data Analytics and Visualization
description: Teaches statistical methods for descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analysis. Provides opportunities to apply these acquired skills in various business applications in operations, finance, and marketing. Utilizes tools such as R Programming for data analysis and Tableau for data visualization.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010 or ECON 101

subject: BUS
title: Business Intelligence For Analytical Decisions
description: Demonstrates an understanding of the processes and techniques of business data collection, analysis, and visualization. Explains and applies the logic of optimization and attribution in business intelligence. Also explains the terminology and tools of business intelligence. Facilitates understanding of machine learning and deep learning as part of artificial intelligence.
prerequisites_text: BUS 101; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Social Network Analytics
description: Increases conceptual knowledge of social network principles. Diversifies abilities to compile, measure, and manage network data. Develops a toolkit for analyzing characteristics of individuals, relationships, and groups. Expands technical knowledge for using network characteristics to predict both individual behavior and group and population outcomes.
prerequisites_text: BUS 104, BUS 107; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Data Science and Machine Learning in Marketing
description: Studies how to harness customer engagement and transaction data using artificial intelligence and machine learning tools to gain marketing insights. Develops data-driven marketing strategies.
prerequisites_text: BUS 119; or consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Special Studies
description: A project to be undertaken under faculty supervision. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of instructor and program chair

subject: BUS
title: R’course - Variable Topics
description: An opportunity for UCR undergraduate students to develop leadership skills, innovate the undergraduate curriculum, and promote democratic, experiential education. Original course topics are variable and unique from other departmental course offerings, designed to highlight the student facilitators’ expertise while working closely with a faculty mentor. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: permission needed from the department; restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior

subject: BUS
title: Individual Internship in Business Administration
description: Provides active participation in the work of a business concern or a public or quasi-public agency. Combines academic instruction and supervised field experience. A maximum of 4 quarter units may be counted toward the degree requirements for Business Administration. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; restricted to major(s) Business Administration; and consent of instructor

subject: BUS
title: Senior Honors Research
description: Involves research in business administration under faculty supervision. Students submit a written report. Graded In Progress (IP) until the last quarter is completed, at which time a final grade is awarded. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units. Business Analytics
prerequisites_text: senior standing with a major in Business Administration; admission to University Honors or consent of instructor

subject: CAH
title: Introductory Cahuilla
description: An introduction to the Cahuilla language. Focuses on the development of listening, speaking, and writing skills. Also explores Cahuilla culture and the sociopolitical aspects of learning and speaking a Native American language.

subject: CAH
title: Introductory Cahuilla
description: An introduction to the Cahuilla language. Focuses on further development of listening, speaking, and writing. Also explores Cahuilla culture and the sociopolitical aspects of learning and speaking a Native American language.
prerequisites_text: CAH 001 with a grade of C- or better

subject: CAH
title: Introductory Cahuilla
description: An introduction to the Cahuilla language. Focuses on further development of listening, speaking, and writing. Also explores Cahuilla culture and the sociopolitical aspects of learning and speaking a Native American language.
prerequisites_text: CAH 002 with a grade of C- or better

subject: CAH
title: Cahuilla Literature and Linguistics
description: Builds upon skills developed in first-year Cahuilla to further develop proficiency in listening, speaking, and writing the Cahuilla language. Explores complex grammatical and discourse constructions through guided linguistic analysis of Cahuilla literature (focusing on traditional narrative texts). Also includes practice in developing and narrating original stories.
prerequisites_text: CAH 003 with a grade of C- or better

subject: CBNS
title: Concepts in Medical Cell Biology
description: Introduces fundamental concepts in molecular cell biology, with emphasis on human health and disease. Modules involve lectures and interactive, problem-oriented activities with faculty. Through classical and contemporary examples, students become acquainted with the scientific process as they discover insights into human biology and genetics.
prerequisites_text: MATH 003 with a grade of C- or better or MATH 006A, may be taken concurrently or MATH 06LA, may be taken concurrently or MATH 006B, may be taken concurrently or MATH 005A, may be taken concurrently or MATH 007A, may be taken concurrently or MATH 009A, may be taken concurrently or MATH 007B, may be taken concurrently or MATH 009B, may be taken concurrently or STAT 010 with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; restricted to major(s) Cell, Molecular, and Developme, Undeclared-Life Sciences; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: The Human Brain: A User’s Guide
description: Introduction to contemporary neuroscience. Topics include foundational principles of brain organization, nerve and glial cell form and function, synaptic transmission, and the neural mechanisms underlying human behavior and physiology. Discusses neuroscience methods and neurological diseases and disorders. Intended for non-Neuroscience majors. Credit is not awarded for CBNS 010 if it has already been awarded for CBNS 106 or PSYC 110.

subject: CBNS
title: Adventures in Cell, Molecular & Developmental Biology: Issues, Careers, and More 1 or
description: An introduction to issues and related research in the CMDB major and pathways available after earning a bachelor?s degree. Topics include research in faculty labs, ethics, study habits, and the application of the major to current issues and careers. Targets first-year UCR students. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of freshman; restricted to major(s) Cell, Molecular, and Developme, Undeclared-Life Sciences; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Fundamentals of Cell Biology
description: Introduces the principles of eukaryotic cell biology. Includes an examination of the molecules and systems that mediate cell function and an overview of membrane architecture and function, cell signaling and signal transduction, the cytoskeleton, organelles, protein targeting and secretion, and the nucleus and nuclear transport. Credit is not awarded for CBNS 101 if it has already been awarded for BIOL 113 or BIOL 114.
prerequisites_text: CHEM 008C and CHEM 08LC or CHEM 08HC and CHEM 08HLC and BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA (BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA may be taken concurrently)

subject: CBNS
title: Introduction to Neuroscience
description: An introduction to cellular, organismal, and behavioral neuroscience for science majors. Topics include structure and functions of the brain, neurons, and synapses; sensory systems and perception; control of movement; neurobiology of hormones and sexual behavior; biorhythms; learning; memory; and psychoses.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005A and BIOL 005B with grades of “C-” or better, CHEM 001A, CHEM 001B, CHEM 001C; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Introduction to Developmental Biology
description: Emphasizes common principles and key concepts that govern development of multiple eukaryotic systems, and how genes control cell behavior during development.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 102, CHEM 008C and CHEM 08LC or CHEM 08HC and CHEM 08HLC; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Epigenetics
description: Introduction to mechanisms that cause a heritable change in phenotype without a change in the genetic code. Covers DNA modifications, histone modifications, and noncoding RNAs that influence the expression, maintenance, and inheritance of traits. Discusses impacts of epigenetics on multicellular life such as learning, memory, disease, and crosstalk with environments. Cross-listed with BPSC 109.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 102; BIOL 107A or BCH 110C

subject: CBNS
title: Human Neuroanatomy: Structure-Function Relationships
description: Provides in-depth study of human functional neuroanatomy including gross anatomy of the brain and spinal cord, microscopic anatomy (histology) of cellular components, and fine structure of the nervous system at the electron microscope (EM) level. Emphasizes understanding the neuroanatomy of key structures (e.g., hypothalamus, brainstem, hippocampus).
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 with a grade of “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Cellular Neuroscience: Membrane and Synaptic Phenomena
description: An examination of cellular and molecular mechanisms of nervous system function using concepts drawn from the study of vertebrates and invertebrates with emphasis on mammalian systems. Cross-listed with PSYC 120.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Neuroscience Laboratory
description: Laboratory experiments using electrophysiological, chemical, and anatomical research methods fundamental to understanding neurons and neural systems. Cross-listed with PSYC 120L.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 120, may be taken concurrently or PSYC 120, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Developmental Neuroscience
description: A study of the development of nervous systems. Examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms of neural development and the determinants of cell birth and death, axonal pathfinding, neuronal connections, and development of neural systems underlying behavior. Cross-listed with PSYC 121.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Systems Neuroscience
description: A study of the structure and function of motor and sensory systems in vertebrate and invertebrate nervous systems. Cross-listed with PSYC 124.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Neuropharmacology
description: Examines synaptic neurotransmitter systems, mechanisms, and pharmacological agents and effects, which are fundamental to neural information processing. Cross-listed with PSYC 125.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 120/PSYC 120

subject: CBNS
title: Neuroscience of Learning and Memory
description: Covers mechanisms of learning and memory across levels of analysis including genetic, neuronal, systems, and theory. Topics include the multiple memory systems, memory consolidation, working memory, emotional memory, recognition memory, spatial memory, and human amnesia. Cross-listed with PSYC 126.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 or PSYC 110; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Behavioral Control Systems
description: An analysis of neural mechanisms that underlie behavior, concentrating on motor control. Topics range from command systems, to central pattern generators, to cortical control of voluntary movement and brain-machine interfaces (neuroprosthetics). Cross-listed with PSYC 127.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 120/PSYC 120; CBNS 124/ PSYC 124 strongly recommended

subject: CBNS
title: Immunology
description: A study of humoral and cellular immunology. Topics include lymphoid systems, cells, antigens, antibodies, antibody formation, cellular immunity, and tumor and transplantation immunology. Discusses in detail diseases and altered immune states associated with each topic. Cross-listed with BIOL 128.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC; PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA

subject: CBNS
title: Brain Control of Bodily Functions
description: Emphasizes principles of organization and function related to endocrine and other physiological systems. Selected topics include control of breathing, body water, temperature, cardiovascular function, and the stress response.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 124/PSYC 124 with a grade of “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Computational Neurophysiology Laboratory: Simulating Neuronal Membrane Properties
description: Introduces computer modeling techniques to enhance understanding of neuronal membrane physiology. Selected topics include biophysical models of single neurons including passive properties and action potential firing, channels regulating neuronal firing properties, synaptic interactions, and simple circuits. Cross-listed with PSYC 123L.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106; CBNS 120, may be taken concurrently or PSYC 120, may be taken concurrently; and consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Invertebrate Neuroethology
description: Addresses principles of neuroethology with emphasis on invertebrate examples. Topics include introduction to invertebrate nervous systems, sensory systems, motor control, circadian rhythms, navigation, learning and memory, and social behavior. Cross-listed with ENTM 131.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C, CHEM 001C or CHEM 01HC, CHEM 008B or CHEM 08HB, MATH 005B or MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB, PHYS 002B or PHYS 02HB, PHYS 02LB or PHYS 02HLB, BCH 100 or BCH 100H or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Scientific Writing For Cell, Molecular and Developmental Biologists
description: An introductory course in scientific writings. Includes preparing scientific manuscripts, research proposals, and other types of technical presentations. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 102, BIOL 107A, CBNS 101, CBNS 108; a major in Cell, Molecular, and Developmental Biology; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Educational Outreach Training in Neuroscience
description: Introduction to multiple approaches and activities that can be used when teaching neuroscience concepts. Builds proficiency in organizational and presentation skills, as well as provides opportunities for educational outreach. Topics include components of oral presentation, models of teaching and learning styles, and published successes in neuroscience outreach. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 120/PSYC 120 and CBNS 124/PSYC 124 with grades of “C” or better and upper division standing in Neuroscience

subject: CBNS
title: Molecular Foundations of Neurological Disorders
description: Introduces the molecular and cell biology of human nervous system disorders. Covers topics like neurodevelopmental and autoimmune diseases, acquired brain injuries, neurodegeneration, sensory-motor impairments, memory deficits, and psychiatric disorders, while examining the underlying molecular and cellular pathology and resulting cognitive and behavioral symptoms.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: CBNS
title: Cancer Biology
