description: One or two of the following segments are offered every year according to need. E. Plautus; F. Terence; G. Virgil; H. Catullus; I. Horace; J. Ovid; K. Propertius; L. Tibullus; N. Cicero; O. Livy; P. Tacitus; Q. Juvenal; R. Lucretius; S. Seneca; T. Pliny; U. Medieval Latin; Z. Renaissance Latin.
prerequisites_text: LATN 003

subject: LATN
title: Sallust
description: Close reading of selections from Sallust. Primary focus on building a proficiency in reading Latin prose.
prerequisites_text: LATN 003 with a grade of “C-” or better or equivalent

subject: LATN
title: The Roman Novel
description: Involves reading and discussion of Latin prose fiction as represented by Petronius’ Satyricon and/or Apuleius’ Metamorphoses. Emphasizes the development of the romantic novel in Latin.
prerequisites_text: LATN 003

subject: LATN
title: Special Studies
description: To be taken as a means of meeting special curricular needs. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: LATN 003

subject: LBST
title: Introduction to Liberal Studies
description: Introduces the richness of the Liberal Studies tradition. Incorporates approaches and integrates learning from the Natural Sciences, Social Sciences, and Arts and Humanities.

subject: LBST
title: Writing Across the Disciplines in Liberal Studies
description: Develops expository and analytical writing skills. Explores the varying expectations, forms, and objectives across the range of disciplines incorporated in the Liberal Studies major. Focuses on multi- and interdisciplinary writing to prepare for upper-division courses offered in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences. Fulfills the third-quarter writing requirement for students who earn a grade of “C” or better for courses that the Academic Senate designates, and that the student’s college permits as alternatives to WRIT 030.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 040V; WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better

subject: LBST
title: Special Studies
description: Individual Study, 2 to 10 hours; written work, . 5 to 2.5 hours; tutorial, .5 to 2.5 hours. Includes preparation of a written proposal endorsed by a supervising instructor as a means of meeting individual curricular needs.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LBST
title: Seminar in Liberal Studies
description: Facilitates student efforts to bring together the knowledge, skills, and interests developed to this point through all aspects of their education. Includes a paper or project and completion of an e-portfolio. Management
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: LGBS
title: History of Queer Cinema
description: An introduction to the aesthetic hallmarks, political impulses, and theoretical responses that distinguish queer cinema as a unique, important tradition within film history. Provides a historical overview of global, independent, Hollywood, and alternative queer production from the 1900s to the present. Cross-listed with MCS 112, and GSST 112.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LGBS
title: Queer Texts and Bodies
description: A study of topics on gender, sexuality and sexual identity. Covers issues such as gay and lesbian texts and contexts; sexual ideologies and literature; marginalized writers and texts; and the uses of theories of sexualities in the study of literature. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 12 units. Cross-listed with ENGL 122.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: LGBS
title: Critical Approaches to Heterosexuality
description: Examines the late nineteenth-century origins and twentieth-century evolution of the meaning of heterosexuality in the United States. Includes the medical, psychological, and political history of heterosexuality; the race and gender components of heterosexuality; and the intersections of heterosexuality and queerness. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Cross-listed with GSST 128.
prerequisites_text: one of the following courses: GSST 001, GSST 001H, GSST 001S, LGBS 001

subject: LGBS
title: Queer Identities and Movements in the United States
description: Examines important twentieth- and twenty-first century developments in queer culture and activism in the United States. Focuses on the origins of sexual identity; the relationship between sexuality, race, and gender; queer representation in art and media; and central issues in queer theory. Cross-listed with GSST 134.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LGBS
title: Love, Desire, and Lesbian Sexuality
description: Expands upon the notion of lesbian identification and sexuality. Emphasizes the influence of feminism on the interdisciplinarity of lesbian studies and the complexity of lesbianism across class, race, ethnic, age, and national and international differences. Cross-listed with GSST 135.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LGBS
title: Critical Queer Politics
description: Presents Euro-American configurations of modern sexuality to map queer communities and homosexual presence across time and space. Critically explores the invisibilities, injustices, erasures, distortions, silences, and voices produced as a result of queer mobility, global gay, and global queer liberation. Cross-listed with GSST 137. Education Abroad Education Abroad is an excellent opportunity to learn more about another country and its culture while taking courses to earn units toward graduation. Students should plan study abroad well in advance to ensure that the courses taken fit with their overall program at UCR. Consult the departmental student affairs officer for assistance. For further details, visit Education Abroad at ea.ucr.edu or call (951) 827-4113. See Education Abroad in the Educational Opportunities section in the beginning of this catalog.
prerequisites_text: one of the following courses: GSST 001, GSST 001H, GSST 001S; or consent of instructor

subject: LING
title: Language and Linguistics
description: An introduction to modern linguistics. Covers the nature of language; language structure; grammars; the languages of the world; historical and comparative linguistics; and interdisciplinary approaches including anthropological and psycholinguistics.

subject: LING
title: Grammar
description: Fundamental concepts of grammatical structure. Includes parts of speech, paradigms, word families, agreement and government, the grammar of sentences and longer units of discourse, and style.

subject: LING
title: Phonetics
description: Develops practice in pronouncing and recognizing sounds from many languages. Covers methods of transcribing and analyzing these sounds.
prerequisites_text: LING 020; or consent of instructor

subject: LING
title: Syntax
description: Survey of various approaches to syntax including transformational. Examines syntactic structures of English and other languages. Applies to: English, foreign languages, philosophy, and mathematics.
prerequisites_text: LING 020

subject: LING
title: Morphology
description: Studies word structure, the lexical component of language, allomorphy, types of morphemes, and inflexional and derivational morphology. Examines various theories of lexical/morphological organization in the brain. Provides examples from English and other Indo-European languages.
prerequisites_text: LING 020; LING 111 or LING 121

subject: LING
title: Phonology
description: Introduction to the study of functional sound units in speech, including phonotactics, morphophonemics. Various theories are examined, including generative. Applications: speech correction, speech analysis, English, foreign languages.
prerequisites_text: LING 111

subject: LING
title: Semantics
description: Introduces the study of meaning and its metalinguistic preliminaries. Explores lexical, sentence, and utterance meaning (including speech acts, text, and discourse). Provides a survey of theories of meaning, such as structural semantics and language as a semiotic system.
prerequisites_text: LING 121

subject: LING
title: (E-Z) Topics in Dynamic and Comparative Linguistics
description: Comparative analyses of language groups such as Spanish and Portuguese, Slavic languages, and Native American languages. E. Historical Linguistics; F. Dialectology; G. Language Change; I. Sociolinguistics.
prerequisites_text: LING 111; LING 121 or LING 141

subject: LING
title: Language and the Brain
description: Interdisciplinary introduction to the study of language and the brain. Includes brain evolution for language, neural bases for language production and language comprehension, aphasiology and language disorders, and additional special topics. Cross-listed with PSYC 128.
prerequisites_text: LING 020 or PSYC 110 or PSYC 135 or CBNS 106; or consent of instructor

subject: LING
title: Anatomy and Physiology of Speech, Language, and Swallowing
description: An in-depth study of the anatomical structures involved in speech, language, and swallowing and their physiological functions. Includes knowledge of the speech subsystems (respiration, phonation, resonance, and articulation), neural features related to language, and the structures involved in deglutition.
prerequisites_text: LING 111 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: LING
title: A Linguist’s Guide to Speech Language Pathology
description: Introduces the scope of practice of Speech Language Pathology (SLP). Offers broad overviews of the disorders evaluated, diagnosed, and treated by speech-language pathologists.
prerequisites_text: LING 020 with a grade of C- or better, LING 163 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to major(s) Education, Society, Human Dev, Linguistics, Psychology

subject: LING
title: Structural/Descriptive Linguistics
description: An overview, from the original sources, of the contribution of major figures and schools in linguistics from Saussure through early Chomsky. Cross-listed with ANTH 167.
prerequisites_text: LING 020 or consent of instructor

subject: LING
title: Statistics For Linguistics
description: An introduction to statistics as it is used in linguistic research. Examines linguistic data using R statistical software. Covers descriptive statistics, regression models, and Bayesian inferences.
prerequisites_text: LING 141 with a grade of C- or better, LING 121 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: LING
title: Special Studies
description: To be taken with the consent of the chair of the Committee as a means of meeting special curricular problems. Course is repeatable.

subject: LING
title: Tutorial Activities
description: Enlarging understanding of linguistics through conducting tutorial sessions in introductory courses, under the supervision of faculty members responsible for the courses involved. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). May be repeated for a maximum of three quarters.
prerequisites_text: junior or senior standing and nomination by faculty

subject: LING
title: Senior Thesis
description: Independent research and preparation of a thesis completed under the supervision of a faculty member. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: senior standing or consent of instructor

subject: LING
title: Senior Honors Thesis
description: Intensive study, research, and preparation of a thesis in consultation with a faculty member. To be taken during two or three successive quarters; course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: invitation by faculty to pursue honors work in Linguistics; senior standing or consent of instructor

subject: LING
title: R’course: Variable Topics
description: An opportunity for UCR undergraduate students to develop leadership skills, innovate the undergraduate curriculum, and promote democratic, experiential education. Original course topics are variable and unique from other departmental course offerings, designed to highlight the student facilitators’ expertise while working closely with a faculty mentor. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 8 units. Related Courses Refer to departmental listings for course descriptions. Anthropology

subject: LNST
title: Introduction to Latin American Studies
description: Introduces key issues in Latin American Studies and how scholars from diverse fields address them. Topics include indigenous cultures; colonial history; poverty; race, gender, and class inequalities; democracy and dictatorship; revolution; and civil war. Integrates film, literature, and music into the course.

subject: LNST
title: Latin American Folk and Popular Styles
description: assigned listening, 3 hours. Introduction to the vast array of folk and popular styles of music in Latin America, with an emphasis on cultural and ethnic interaction and exchange in the context of Latin American history, politics, and society. Cross-listed with MUS 015.

subject: LNST
title: Latin American Classical Heritage
description: assigned listening, 3 hours. Survey of the rich heritage of Latin American classical music from Renaissance sacred polyphony to contemporary styles. Emphasis on the gradual emergence of Latin American music from European domination and the establishment of distinctive national traditions in the post-colonial era. Cross-listed with MUS 016.

subject: LNST
title: Music of Mexico
description: Covers music from 1521 to the present day. Explores the rich musical tradition of Mexico, as well as the relationship between its art and popular music. Cross-listed with MUS 017.
prerequisites_text: musical training and knowledge of Spanish is useful, but not required

subject: LNST
title: Art of Pre-Columbian America
description: A survey course that provides a background to the ancient art of Mexico, Central America, and the Andean region of western South America. Discusses art of pre-Columbian America according to the three broad cultural regions of Mesoamerica, the lower part of central and northwestern South America, and the Andean area. Cross-listed with AHS 027, and ANTH 027.

subject: LNST
title: Art and Architecture of Latin America
description: Introduces Latin American art and architecture from the European conquest to the present. Topics include religious and secular art and architecture; hybridization of indigenous and imported styles; national styles after independence; Mexican murals; women artists; Latin American modernismo; and Chicano and Border art. Cross-listed with AHS 028.

subject: LNST
title: Dance of Mexico
description: Covers the traditional dances of Mexico at the beginning level. Includes attendance at dance concerts outside of class. Recommended for both nondancers and dancers. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with MUS 073A.

subject: LNST
title: Dance of Mexico
description: Covers the traditional dances of Mexico at the beginning level. Includes attendance at dance concerts outside of class. Recommended for both nondancers and dancers. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with MUS 073B.
prerequisites_text: LNST 073A/MUS 073A is recommended

subject: LNST
title: An Introduction to the Study of Spanish and Comparative Linguistics
description: An introduction to the study of Spanish and comparative linguistics. Cross-listed with SPN 104.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: LNST
title: Imagining the Nation: Film and Media in Latin America
description: Studies the role of media and film in creating a national imaginary in Latin America. Focuses on one region or nation--such as the Andes, the Caribbean, Mexico, Argentina, or Chile--and relates the local history to the global context. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units. Cross-listed with SPN 185.
prerequisites_text: MCS 020; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: The Phonology of the Spanish Language
description: Provides a descriptive and normative analysis of the phonological system of the Spanish language. Focuses on the phonetic characteristics of contemporary Peninsular and Hispano-American Spanish. Cross-listed with SPN 105.
prerequisites_text: LING 020; SPN 101A, SPN 101B or SPN 109A, SPN 109B; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Spanish in the United States
description: A sociolinguistic study of the Spanish language in the United States. Cross-listed with SPN 107.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Gender, Media, and Latin America
description: Explores the way Latin Americans have thought of and represented gender across a variety of media including essays, film, novel, short story, and performance. Compares the possibilities and limitations of these media for representing gender in the Latin American context. Cross-listed with MCS 179, SPN 179, and GSST 179.
prerequisites_text: MCS 020 or upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: The Art of the Aztec Empire
description: An introduction to the art of the Aztec Empire. Studies architecture, sculpture, ceramics, painting, lapidary work, gold work, and feather work. Explores the relationship between art and ritual and art and the imperial state. Cross-listed with AHS 112 and ANTH 151.
prerequisites_text: AHS 027/ANTH 027/LNST 027 or upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: History of Brazilian Art & Architecture
description: The history of Brazilian art and architecture from the nineteenth century to present. Explores visual culture including painting, sculpture, prints, murals, architecture, urbanism, landscape design, and installation art. Studies artworks and buildings through a social historical framework, taking into consideration topics like colonialism, modernization, underdevelopment, race, nationalism, internationalism, and globalism. Cross-listed with AHS 114.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Modern and Contemporary Art of Latin America
description: A study of Latin American art from circa 1900 to the present. Considers national and regional histories and artistic trajectories beginning with the advent of an artistic avant-garde. Investigates the relationships between European and Latin American developments. Cross-listed with AHS 115.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Architecture and Arts of the Andes
description: An introduction to architecture, urbanism, and related material culture of the Andes from ancient times to the present. Focuses on the diverse and rich architectural heritage of an important building center in the Americas. Addresses architecture’s relationship to artistic and material production such as painting, pottery, sculpture, city planning, and textiles. Cross-listed with AHS 116.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Visual Culture of the Incas
description: An introduction to the art, architecture, and urban form of the Inca civilization. Examines how these elements influenced state formation, conquest, and resistance. Includes studies of urban plans, buildings, paintings, textiles, prints, sculpture, metalwork, and ceramics. Cross-listed with ANTH 157, and AHS 117.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Major Topics in Hispanic Literature: Latin America
description: Reading and analysis of major texts of authors from Latin America. Cross-listed with SPN 120C.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: LNST
title: Conceptual Art in Latin America
description: Considers conceptual art made across Latin America, from 1960s to present. Focuses on subversive strategies artists developed to critique military dictatorships then in power, while circumventing legalized censorship. Considers localized versions of conceptual art in Santiago, Buenos Aires, Rio de Janeiro, Havana, Mexico City, and situate them within international movement. Cross-listed with AHS 124.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: (E-Z) Topics in Latin American Film and Media
description: Intensive formal, historical, and theoretical analysis of a theme or issue in Latin American film and media. Cross-listed with MCS 125 (E-Z), and SPN 125 (E-Z).
prerequisites_text: See individual segments for Units, prerequisites, and activities

subject: LNST
title: Indigenous Video and Latin America
description: Intensive formal, historical, and theoretical analysis of a theme or issue in Latin American film and media. E. Indigenous Video and Latin America. Cross-listed with MCS 125 (E-Z) and SPN 125(E-Z)
prerequisites_text: MCS 020 or upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Imagining the Nation: Film and Media in Latin America
description: Study of the role of media and film in creating a national imaginary in Latin America. Focus is on one region or nation such as the Andes, the Caribbean, Mexico, Argentina, or Chile relating local history to the global context. Cross-listed with MCS 125I, and SPN 125I.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: LNST
title: Introduction to Maya Hieroglyphs
description: Introduces the Maya hieroglyphs and critically evaluates its political history. Topics include three Maya calendars, a basic grammar (logographs, syllables, verbs, pronouns), three writing methods (transcriptions, transliteration, and translation), dynastic events, gods, supernaturals, and political interactions. Cross-listed with ANTH 129A, and CPAC 129A.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 001 or ANTH 001H or ANTH 001W or ANTH 005 or ANTH 007 or ANTH 007S; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: The Linguistics of Ancient Maya Writing
description: Analyzes and critically evaluates the linguistics of Ancient Maya Writing. Topics include grammar (transitive, intransitive, positional, active, passive, mediopassive, antipassive, inchoactive verbs, tense, aspect, transitive perfect, noun, pronoun, morphosyllable, phonology); three writing methods (transcriptions, transliteration, and translation); title and rank; scripts and ideologies; and dynastic interactions. Cross-listed with ANTH 129B, and CPAC 129B.
prerequisites_text: ANTH 129A; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Latin America: the Quest For Development and Democracy
description: A comparative examination of central issues in and components of Latin American political life. Covers economic development, regimes and alliances, guerrilla wars, the armed forces, human rights, and democratic consolidation. Includes Argentina, Chile, Venezuela, and Peru. Cross-listed with POSC 162. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 162, LNST 142, LNST 142S, or POSC 162S.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Latin America: the Quest For Development and Democracy
description: A comparative examination of central issues in and components of Latin American political life. Covers economic development, regimes and alliances, guerrilla wars, the armed forces, human rights, and democratic consolidation. Includes Argentina, Chile, Venezuela, and Peru. Cross-listed with POSC 162S. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 162S, LNST 142S, LNST 142, or POSC 162.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: LNST
title: Borderlands History of the United States
description: Examines the frontier in U.S. history focusing on the Western frontier and Spanish borderlands. Cross-listed with HISA 137.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Politics of Mexico
description: A survey of contemporary Mexican politics. Emphasis is on recent economic and social changes and their impact on Mexico’s political system. Topics include relations with the United States, the rise of drug trafficking in Mexico, and the recent emergence of opposition politics. Cross-listed with POSC 158.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Caribbean Culture and Society
description: An overview of the Caribbean region from a historical, cultural, and political perspective. Emphasizes contemporary issues affecting the Caribbean and the struggle of its people to maintain their identities. Cross-listed with ANTH 142G, and ETST 148.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Colonial Latin America
description: A history of Latin America from pre-Columbian times to independence with an emphasis upon selected themes concerning the social, economic, and cultural aspects of colonialism. Cross-listed with HISA 160.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Nineteenth-Century Latin America
description: Topics include the breakdown of political order and the problem of the nation-state, liberalism and conservatism, slavery and abolition, foreign intervention and capital investment, the reemergence of political order in the Age of Liberalism (1860-1900), and social and cultural change. Cross-listed with HISA 161.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Twentieth-Century Latin America
description: Topics include the Mexican Revolution, the Great Depression, populism, industrialization, revolution, and the emergence of conservative regimes in the age of neoliberalism. Cross-listed with HISA 162.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Economic Development in Latin America
description: A comparative analysis of the major trends in Latin American economies in the twentieth century. Includes historical legacies, primary export economies, the theory and practice of import substitution industrialization, and the debt crisis. Also covers stabilization and structural adjustment, poverty and income distribution, the informal and agricultural sectors, and the environment. Cross-listed with ECON 185.
prerequisites_text: ECON 102 or ECON 103 or ECON 104A or ECON 105A

subject: LNST
title: Contemporary Public Policy Challenges in Latin America
description: A survey of the wide-sweeping policy reforms since the 1980s and of contemporary public policy challenges in Latin America. Challenges discussed include extremely high levels of poverty and inequality; inadequate educational and healthcare systems; pressures for land reform; problems of trade competitiveness; and recurring currency crises. Cross-listed with ECON 187.
prerequisites_text: ECON 002 or ECON 002H; ECON 003 or ECON 003H; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: United States and Latin American Relations
description: Explores international relations between the United States and the nations of Latin America. Examines different theories for explaining changes in the conduct of U.S.-Latin American relations over time. Topics include democracy and empire, revolution and counter-insurgency, economic integration and trade, petroleum politics, drug trafficking, and migration flows. Cross-listed with POSC 161.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: LNST
title: Economic Development in Brazil
description: An analysis of the successes and failures of economic development in the largest country in Latin America. Reviews current issues facing Brazilian policy makers. Topics include historical legacies, import substitution and industrialization, poverty and inequality, agriculture and land reform, and the environmental impact of development. Cross-listed with ECON 189.
prerequisites_text: ECON 102 or ECON 104A; ECON 103 or ECON 105A

subject: LWSO
title: Introduction to the Study of Law and Society
description: An introduction to the interdisciplinary study of the role of law and legal institutions in society. Examines the role of criminal, tort, contract, constitutional, or other areas of the law in society from different disciplinary perspectives. Credit is awarded for one of the following LWSO 100 or LWSO 100H.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: LWSO
title: Honors Introduction to the Study of Law and Society
description: Honors course corresponding to LWSO 100. An introduction to the interdisciplinary study of the role of law and legal institutions in society. Examines the role of criminal, tort, contract, constitutional, or other areas of the law in society from different disciplinary perspectives. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Credit is awarded for only one of LWSO 100 or LWSO 100H.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: LWSO
title: (E-Z) Topics in Law and Society
description: Addresses current topics in law and society.
prerequisites_text: LWSO 100 or LWSO 100H

subject: LWSO
title: Convicting the Innocent
description: Considers the causes of false convictions.
prerequisites_text: LWSO 100 or LWSO 100H; upper-division standing

subject: LWSO
title: Symposium in the Law
description: A discussion of legal matters of common interest, in conjunction with experts from outside the university. After completing LWSO 180A, LWSO 180B, and LWSO 180C, students may repeat the sequence once for credit; total credit for each course may not exceed 2 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of instructor in the preceding quarter

subject: LWSO
title: Symposium in the Law
description: A discussion of legal matters of common interest, in conjunction with experts from outside the university. After completing LWSO 180A, LWSO 180B, and LWSO 180C, students may repeat the sequence once for credit; total credit for each course may not exceed 2 units.
prerequisites_text: LWSO 180A

subject: LWSO
title: Symposium in the Law
description: A discussion of legal matters of common interest, in conjunction with experts from outside the university. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). After completing LWSO 180A, LWSO 180B, and LWSO 180C, students may repeat the sequence once for credit; total credit for each course may not exceed 2 units.
prerequisites_text: LWSO 180B

subject: LWSO
title: Science and Law
description: Discusses the intersection between science and law. Also compares legal and scientific procedures and decision making.
prerequisites_text: LWSO 100 or LWSO 100H

subject: LWSO
title: Senior Seminar in Law and Society
description: Aims to synthesize multidisciplinary perspectives and knowledge provided by other courses in the Law and Society Program through readings, group discussion, and research on an issue or problem in law and society. Covers topics such as law and morality, law and social change, law and religion, and law and culture. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available.
prerequisites_text: LWSO 100 or LWSO 100H; senior standing in Law and Society/ Anthropology, Law and Society/Economics, Law and Society/History, Law and Society/ Philosophy, Law and Society/Political Science, Law and Society/Psychology, or Law and Society/Sociology

subject: LWSO
title: Individual Internship in Law and Society
description: An individual internship in the professional legal or policy-making community. Requires a substantive paper relating the internship to the student’s area of study. Liberal Studies
prerequisites_text: LWSO 100 or LWSO 100H; consent of instructor and department chair; upper-division standing

subject: MATH
title: College Mathematics Fundamentals and Problem Solving
description: Prepares for success in a college-level mathematics course. Focuses on conceptual and problem solving. Emphasizes practicing symbolic reasoning, evaluating expressions, the meaning of quantities, variables, expressions, formulas, changes in quantities, inequalities, systems of equations, and functions (linear, exponential, logarithmic, quadratic, polynomial, rational, radical). Workload credit only; Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: a score on the Mathematics Advisory Examination, as determined by the Mathematics Department; restricted to freshman or an approved summer session enrollment; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to College Mathematics For Business and the Social Sciences
description: Covers functions and their graphs including linear and polynomial functions, zeroes, and inverse functions as well as exponential and logarithmic functions and their inverses. Also includes counting including elementary probability. Involves applications to business and social sciences. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 004, MATH 005A, MATH 006A, or MATH 006B.
prerequisites_text: MATH 003 or MATH 004L, may be taken concurrently; the Mathematics Department determines the study program pathway based upon the score on the Mathematics Advisory Examination; or a score of 2 on the AP Calculus AB Exam; not open to students in the Bourns College of Engineering or the College of Natural and Agricultural Sciences or to students majoring in Economics or Business Economics

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to College Mathematics For Business and the Social Sciences Workshop
description: Just-in-time lessons and activities to enhance student foundations on functions and properties of functions from four perspectives (verbal, visual, numeric, and symbolic) to complement and support MATH 004. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: MATH 004, may be taken concurrently; the Mathematics Department determines the study program pathway based upon the score on the Mathematics Advisory Examination; not open to students in the Bourns College of Engineering or the College of Natural and Agricultural Sciences or to students majoring in Economics or Business Economics; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: The Principles of Calculus 1
description: A study of inequalities, absolute value, functions, graphing, logarithms, trigonometry, roots of polynomials, counting, vectors, and other elementary concepts of mathematics. Some sections may be offered online. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 005A, MATH 004, MATH 006A, or MATH 006B.
prerequisites_text: a score of 2 on the AP Calculus AB Exam or a sufficiently high score on the Mathematics Advisory Examination, as determined by the Mathematics Department

subject: MATH
title: The Principles of Calculus 2
description: An introduction to application of finite approximation to study functions of one variable. Topics include sequences, series, differential calculus, and antiderivatives. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 005B, MATH 007A, MATH 009A, or MATH 09HA.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005A with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: The Principles of Calculus 3
description: Further topics on infinite series including test of convergence and Taylor’s series. An introduction of integral calculus of one-variable with applications. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 005C, MATH 007B, MATH 009B, MATH 009C, MATH 09HB, or MATH 09HC.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005B with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus: An Introduction to Functions 1
description: Develops and refines quantitative reasoning, covariational reasoning, problem solving, and algebraic proficiency in preparation for calculus. Topics include functions, properties of functions, ways to create new functions, and modeling real-world situations with functions. Specific functions covered include linear, exponential, and logarithmic functions. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 006A, MATH 004, or MATH 005A.
prerequisites_text: MATH 003 or MATH 06LA, may be taken concurrently; the Mathematics Department determines the study program pathway based upon the score on the Mathematics Advisory Examination; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus: An Introduction to Functions 2
description: Develops and refines quantitative and covariational reasoning skills and problem solving skills in preparation for calculus. Topics include functions, properties of functions, modeling real world situations with functions, limits, and continuity. Specific functions covered include polynomial, rational, trigonometric, and inverse trigonometric functions. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 006B, MATH 004, or MATH 005A.
prerequisites_text: MATH 006A with a grade of B- or better or MATH 006A with a grade of C- or better; MATH 06LB, may be taken concurrently; NOTE: MATH 006A with a grade of C-, C, or C+ requires concurrent enrollment in MATH 06LB; or MATH 006A with grades of B- or better may enroll in MATH 06LB as an option; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Calculus For Life Sciences
description: Introduction to the differential calculus of functions of one variable for students majoring in Life Sciences. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 007A, MATH 005B, MATH 009A, or MATH 09HA.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005A or MATH 006B

subject: MATH
title: Calculus For Life Sciences
description: Introduction to the integral calculus of functions of one variable. For Life Sciences majors. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 007B, MATH 005C, MATH 009B, or MATH 09HB.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 007A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HA with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: First-Year Calculus
description: Introduction to the differential calculus of functions of one variable. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 009A, MATH 005B, MATH 007A, or MATH 09HA.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 006B

subject: MATH
title: First Year Calculus
description: Introduction to the integral calculus of functions of one variable. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 009B, MATH 005C, MATH 007B, or MATH 09HB.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009A or MATH 09HA

subject: MATH
title: First Year Calculus
description: Further topics from integral calculus, improper integrals, infinite series, Taylor’s series, and Taylor’s theorem. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 009C, MATH 005C, or MATH 09HC.
prerequisites_text: MATH 009B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HB with a grade of C- or better or MATH 007B with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Calculus of Several Variables
description: Topics include Euclidean geometry, matrices and linear functions, determinants, partial derivatives, directional derivatives, Jacobians, gradients, chain rule, and Taylor’s theorem for several variables.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 007B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HB with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent

subject: MATH
title: Calculus of Several Variables
description: Covers vectors; differential calculus, including implicit differentiation and extreme values; multiple integration; line integrals; vector field theory; and theorems of Gauss, Green, and Stokes.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A with a grade of “C-” or better or equivalent

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Discrete Structures
description: Introduction to basic concepts of discrete mathematics emphasizing applications to computer science. Topics include propositional and predicate calculi, elementary set theory, functions, relations, proof techniques, elements of number theory, enumeration, and discrete probability. Cross-listed with CS 011.
prerequisites_text: CS 009A or CS 010A or MATH 005C or MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB

subject: MATH
title: Calculus For Business
description: Explores relations and functions (e.g., linear, polynomial, logarithmic, and exponential). Addresses differential calculus of functions of one and two variables as well as integration (indefinite and definite) with applications to business and economic problems. Credit is not awarded for MATH 022 if a grade of “C-” or better has already been awarded for MATH 007A, MATH 009A, MATH 09HA, or MATH 005B.
prerequisites_text: MATH 004 with a grade of C- or better or MATH 006B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 005A; or a sufficiently high score on the placement examination, as determined by the Mathematics Department

subject: MATH
title: Applied Linear Algebra
description: A study of matrices and systems of linear equations, determinants, Gaussian elimination, vector spaces, linear independence and linear transformation, orthogonality, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. Also examines selected topics and applications. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 031 or EE 020B.
prerequisites_text: CS 010A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 007B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HB with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Ordinary Differential Equations For Physical Sciences and Engineering
description: Introduction to ordinary differential equations; complex numbers; trigonometric, compact and exponential Fourier Series; frequency spectrum; and Laplace transform, Fourier transform, and their application to the solution of integro-differential equations as they appear in the physical sciences and engineering. Cross-listed with EE 020A. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 045, EE 020A, or MATH 046.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 007B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HB with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Ordinary Differential Equations
description: Introduction to first-order equations, linear second-order equations, and Laplace transforms, with applications to the physical and biological sciences. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 046, EE 020A, or MATH 045.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 007B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HB with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus Study Group: An Introduction to Functions 1
description: Just-in-time lessons and activities to enhance student foundations on functions and properties of functions from four perspectives (verbal, visual, numeric, and symbolic) to complement and support MATH 006A. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: MATH 006A, may be taken concurrently; the Mathematics Department determines the study program pathway based upon the score on the Mathematics Advisory Examination; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus Study Group: An Introduction to Functions 2
description: Just-in-time lessons and activities to enhance student foundations on functions and properties of functions from four perspectives (verbal, visual, numeric, and symbolic) to complement MATH 006B. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: MATH 006A with a grade of C- or better, MATH 06LB, may be taken concurrently; NOTE: MATH 006A with a grade of C-, C, or C+ requires concurrent enrollment in MATH 06LB; or MATH 006A with grades of B- or better may enroll in MATH 06LB as an option; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: First-Year Honors Calculus
description: Honors course corresponding to MATH 009A. Honors course corresponding to MATH 009A for students with strong mathematical backgrounds. Introduces the differential calculus of functions of one variable. Emphasis is on theory and rigor Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 09HA, MATH 005B, MATH 007A, or MATH 009A.
prerequisites_text: admission to University Honors

subject: MATH
title: First-Year Honors Calculus
description: Honors course corresponding to MATH 009B. Honors course corresponding to MATH 009B for students with strong mathematical backgrounds. Introduces the integral calculus of functions of one variable. Emphasis is on theory and rigor. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 09HB, MATH 005C, MATH 007B, or MATH 009B.
prerequisites_text: MATH 09HA with a grade of B or better; admission to University Honors

subject: MATH
title: First-Year Honors Calculus
description: Honors course corresponding to MATH 009C. Further topics from integral calculus, improper integrals, infinite series, Taylor’s series, and Taylor’s theorem. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 09HC, MATH 005C, or MATH 009C.
prerequisites_text: MATH 09HB with a grade of B or better or MATH 009B with a grade of B or better; admission to University Honors

subject: MATH
title: An Introduction to Mathematical Proofs
description: An introduction to communicating mathematics through proofs. Topics include basic logic, set theory, functions, and various proof techniques such as induction, direct, contrapositive, contradiction, and cases. May also include equivalence relations, countability, number theory, structure of the real numbers, sequences, and continuity.
prerequisites_text: MATH 009B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HB with a grade of C- or better or MATH 007B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Advanced Problem Solving
description: Develops advanced problem-solving skills through rigorous mathematical exploration focusing on preparing for the William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition. Explores challenging problems in various mathematical areas including algebra, geometry, number theory, functional equations, combinatorics, geometry, and calculus, emphasizing non-standard approaches. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 4 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Optimization
description: Introduction to classical optimization including unconstrained and constrained problems in several variables, Addresses Jacobian and Lagrangian methods and the Kuhn-Tucker conditions. Covers the basic concepts of linear programming including the simplex method and duality with applications to other subjects.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A with a grade of “C-” or better; MATH 031 with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: MATH
title: Game Theory
description: Examines games in extensive, normal, and characteristic form as models of conflict and/or cooperation. Covers two-person zero-sum games, minimax theorem, and relation to linear programming. Includes non-zero-sum games, Nash equilibrium theorem, bargaining, the core, and the Shapley value. Addresses economic market games.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A with a grade of C- or better, MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Combinatorics
description: A study of elements of combinatorics theory. Topics include chromatic polynomials, enumerating partitions of sets and integers, asymptotic enumeration, Polya theory, and Ramsey theory.
prerequisites_text: MATH 011 with a grade of C- or better or CS 011 with a grade of C- or better or MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra I
description: An introduction to vector spaces, matrices, and linear transformations.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently; MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra 2
description: Further study of topics in linear algebra including eigenvalues. Exploration of Hermitian and unitary matrices, positive definite matrices, and canonical forms.
prerequisites_text: MATH 131 with a grade of “C-” or better or equivalent

subject: MATH
title: Geometry
description: Analyzes elementary theory of affine and projective planes, the line at infinity, finite geometries, Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometries, groups of transformations, and other algebraic structures related to geometry.
prerequisites_text: MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better, MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis 1
description: Introduces basic numerical techniques for computing solutions of problems in science and engineering as well as computational implementation of such techniques using MATLAB and Python. Topics include floating point computation, error analysis, numerical methods for solutions of linear and nonlinear scalar and systems of equations, and numerical interpolation.
prerequisites_text: CS 010A with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently; MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis 2
description: Introduces basic numerical techniques for computing solutions of problems in science and engineering as well as computational implementation of such techniques using MATLAB and Python. Topics include numerical integration, Runge-Kutta methods for initial value problems, matrix factorizations, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors.
prerequisites_text: MATH 135A with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis 3
description: A continuation of Math 135B. Topics include least square method, Fourier series, numerical methods for PDEs, and numerical optimization.
prerequisites_text: MATH 135B with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to the Theory of Numbers
description: Covers prime and composite integers, number theoretic functions, diophantine equations, congruences, quadratic reciprocity, and additive arithmetic.
prerequisites_text: MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better, MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Differential Geometry
description: Examines elementary theory of curves and surfaces. Includes first and second fundamental forms.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A; MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Differential Geometry
description: Covers Gaussian curvature, geodesics, and the Gauss-Bonnet Theorem.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B with a grade of “C-” or better, MATH 138A with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: MATH
title: Polynomials and Number Systems
description: Topics include number systems, elementary number theory, rings, fields, polynomials, congruencies, and applications of finite fields.
prerequisites_text: MATH 011 with a grade of C- or better or CS 011 with a grade of C- or better or MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better; MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Set Theory
description: Covers algebra of subsets of a set. Addresses algebra of relations and functions. Explores cardinal and ordinal numbers and their arithmetic operations. Includes the well-ordering theorem, transfinite induction, and Zorn’s lemma.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A with a grade of C- or better; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Topology
description: Addresses elementary topology in metric spaces.
prerequisites_text: MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Topology
description: Explores geometric topology, algebra associated with finite complexes, and applications.
prerequisites_text: MATH 145A with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: MATH
title: Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations
description: Focuses on the theory of linear differential equations and transform methods.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HC with a grade of C- or better; MATH 010A with a grade of C- or better; MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently; MATH 046 with a grade of C- or better; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently

subject: MATH
title: Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations
description: Further study of the theory of linear differential equations and problems in valuing ordinary differential equations.
prerequisites_text: MATH 146A with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: MATH
title: Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations
description: Explores boundary value problems for partial differential equations, orthogonal expansions, and separation of variables.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B with a grade of “C-” or better, MATH 146B with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Fourier Analysis and its Applications
description: Covers Fourier series expansions of periodic functions, properties, and convergence; the Dirichlet kernel; Fourier integrals and the Fourier transform in one and several variables; the Plancherel theorem; and Fourier inversion. Includes applications of Fourier analysis (e.g., to spectral theory, numerical analysis, ordinary and partial differential equations, and wavelet transform).
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HC with a grade of C- or better; MATH 010B with a grade of C- or better; MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently; MATH 046 with a grade of C- or better or MATH 146A with a grade of C- or better; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Chaotic and Complex Dynamical Systems
description: Explores examples of dynamical systems, quadratic maps, maps of the circle, and higher-dimensional examples. Includes symbolic dynamics, Sarkovskii’s theorem, hyperbolicity, and structural stability. Introduces chaotic dynamical systems and the period doubling route to chaos. Also introduces basic notions from complex dynamics. Includes the Julia set and the Mandelbrot set.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B with a grade of “C-” or better; MATH 031 with a grade of “C-” or better; MATH 046 or MATH 146A with a grade of “C-” or better; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Probability and Mathematical Statistics
description: An introduction to the mathematical theory of probability and discrete and continuous distributions.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A with a grade of C- or better; MATH 010B with a grade of C- or better; MATH 046 with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently

subject: MATH
title: Probability and Mathematical Statistics
description: A continuation of MATH 149A. Topics include sampling and limit distributions.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A with a grade of “C-” or better, MATH 010B with a grade of “C-” or better, MATH 046 with a grade of “C-” or better, MATH 149A with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: MATH
title: Intermediate Analysis
description: A study of the concepts and theory of single-variable calculus. Covers the basics of real numbers, sequences, limits, continuity, and differentiation. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 150 or MATH 151A.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HC with a grade of C- or better; MATH 010B with a grade of C- or better; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Foundations of Real Analysis 1
description: Provides a rigorous development of mathematical analysis includes the formal theory of the real numbers, convergent sequences, monotone sequences, subsequences, convergent tests, limit superior, limit inferior, Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem, Cauchy sequences, limit of functions, continuous functions, extreme value theorems, intermediate value theorems, uniform continuity, and continuity of monotone functions. Credit is awarded for one of the following MATH 151A or MATH 150.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HC with a grade of C- or better; MATH 010B with a grade of C- or better; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Foundations of Real Analysis 2
description: Provides a rigorous development of mathematical analysis. Includes properties of the derivative; mean value theorem, intermediate value theorem, Taylor’s theorem, inverse function theorem, fundamental theorem of calculus; Riemann integrable functions, sequences and series of functions, pointwise and uniform convergence of functions, and the continuity, integral, and derivative of the limit.
prerequisites_text: MATH 151A with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Foundations of Real Analysis 3
description: Provides a rigorous development of mathematical analysis. Includes metric spaces, open and closed sets, connected sets, closure and boundary, convergent sequences, Cauchy sequences, completeness, compactness, Heine-Borel theorem, continuity, uniform continuity, limits, the derivative, gradients, curves, partial derivatives, the Jacobian, continuity and the derivative, and inverse and implicit function theorems.
prerequisites_text: MATH 131 with a grade of C- or better; MATH 151B with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: History of Mathematics
description: A survey from a historical point of view of various developments in mathematics. Emphasizes the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HC with a grade of C- or better; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning
description: Introduction to mathematical and computational concepts in machine learning methods with emphasis on developing new machine learning algorithms. Topics include linear algebra and vector calculus in application to supervised learning, regression, classification, unsupervised learning, clustering, and dimensionality reduction. Topics also include optimization and probability theory used in machine learning algorithms.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A with a grade of C- or better; MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Foundations of Deep Learning
description: Introduction to core mathematical principles in deep learning, emphasizing training neural networks for computer vision. Topics cover various architectures, image transformation techniques (segmentation, super-resolution, denoising), object detection, and transfer learning. Also explores key optimization tools and neural network visualization to ground theoretical innovations in deep learning, providing practical insights.
prerequisites_text: MATH 161A with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
description: Exploration of essential mathematical concepts for artificial intelligence, covering natural language processing, generative networks, and reinforcement learning. Topics include text classification, multimodal learning, and advanced generative models (GANs, diffusion models). Emphasizes domain adaptation, semi-supervised, and self-supervised learning with applications in real-world AI tasks.
prerequisites_text: MATH 161B with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Models and Computational Science
description: An introduction to mathematical and computational modeling using high-level computer programming languages such as C/C++. Includes implementation of parallel algorithms for solving linear systems, systems of differential equations, and running stochastic imulations on high performance CPU and GPU computer clusters.
prerequisites_text: MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better, MATH 135A with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Applied Dynamical Systems
description: Introduction to dynamical systems with applications to problems in Physics, Biology, Chemistry, and Engineering. Topics include phase plane analysis, stability of dynamical systems, and numerical methods for dynamical systems.
prerequisites_text: MATH 045 with a grade of C- or better or MATH 046 with a grade of C- or better; MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better; MATH 135A with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Complex Variables
description: An introduction to the theory of analytic functions of a complex variable. Includes mappings by elementary functions and complex integrals as well as Cauchy’s theorem, power series, and Laurent series.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B with a grade of C- or better; MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Complex Variables
description: Topics include the theory of residues, conformal mapping, and applications to physical problems.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B with a grade of “C-” or better, MATH 165A with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Mathematical Modeling
description: A detailed study of how mathematical methods are applied to specific problems in the sciences and engineering fields. Utilizes examples taken from the theories of mechanical vibrations, population dynamics, and flow phenomena.
prerequisites_text: MATH 146A

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Modern Algebra
description: An introduction to the fundamental concepts of modern algebra. Covers groups, subgroups, quotient groups, homomorphisms, symmetry groups, fundamental properties of rings, integral domains, ideals, and quotient rings.
prerequisites_text: MATH 110 with a grade of C- or better; MATH 131 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MATH
title: Modern Algebra
description: Covers fundamental concepts of modern algebra. Includes groups, fields, polynomials, geometric constructions, algebraic coding, and boolean algebras.
prerequisites_text: MATH 171 with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: MATH
title: Special Studies
description: To be taken with the consent of the chair of the department as a means of meeting special curricular problems. Course is repeatable.

subject: MATH
title: Independent Reading
description: Independent reading in materials not covered in course work. Normally taken in the senior year. Total credit for MATH 194 may not exceed 4 units.

subject: MATH
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: Involves a research project on a problem in, or related to, mathematics conducted under the supervision of a Mathematics faculty member. Students who submit a term paper receive a letter grade; other students receive a Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grade. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of instructor

subject: MATH
title: Internship in Mathematics
description: An academic internship to provide the student with career experience as a mathematician in a governmental, industrial, or research unit under the joint supervision of an off-campus sponsor and a faculty member in Mathematics. Each individual program must have the prior approval of both supervisors and the department chair. A final written report is required. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). May be repeated for a total of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, with at least 12 units of upper-division credits toward the major

subject: MCBL
title: Exploring Microbiology
description: Introduces the role of microbes in our daily lives. Includes food production and biotechnology; research topics in microbiology and career options and preparation; and preparation for postgraduate education. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 2 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to major(s) Microbiology

subject: MCBL
title: Introduction to Plant Pathology
description: An introduction to the study of plant diseases. Topics include diseases and disease-causing agents, host-pathogen interaction during disease development, and strategies for disease management. Includes optional, separate laboratory. Cross-listed with BIOL 120, and PLPA 120. Credit is awarded for one of the following PLPA 120, BIOL 120, MCBL 120, or PLPA 210.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; BCH 100 or BCH 100H or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; STAT 010

subject: MCBL
title: Introduction to Plant Pathology Laboratory
description: Covers fundamentals in the use of laboratory instruments and techniques for the detection, isolation, and identification of representative infectious agents that cause disease in plants. Cross-listed with BIOL 120L, and PLPA 120L. Credit is awarded for one of the following PLPA 120L, BIOL 120L, MCBL 120L, or PLPA 210.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC; PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; BIOL 120, may be taken concurrently or MCBL 120, may be taken concurrently or PLPA 120, may be taken concurrently; STAT 010, may be taken concurrently; BIOL 121/MCBL 121 and BIOL 124/MCBL 124 recommended; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Introductory Microbiology
description: An intensive introduction to the fundamental physiology and molecular biology of bacteria and viruses. Covers bacterial and viral molecular genetics, an introduction to microbial pathogenesis, and applications of microbiology in modern societies. Cross-listed with BIOL 121. Credit is awarded for one of the following MCBL 121, BIOL 121, or MCBL 131.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005A; BIOL 05LA or BIOL 020; BIOL 005B; BIOL 005C; CHEM 001C or CHEM 01HC; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002A, may be taken concurrently or PHYS 02HA, may be taken concurrently; PHYS 02LA, may be taken concurrently or PHYS 02HLA, may be taken concurrently; BCH 100, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110A, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110HA, may be taken concurrently; STAT 010; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Microbiology Laboratory
description: Laboratory exercises in diagnostic bacteriology, basic virology, and epidemiology. Includes fundamental quantitative and diagnostic microbiological procedures, basic mechanisms of microbial genetic exchange, and a project examining bacterial epidemiology. Cross-listed with BIOL 121L. Credit is awarded for one of the following MCBL 121L, BIOL 121L, or MCBL 131L.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 121 with a grade of C- or better or MCBL 121 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MCBL
title: Food Microbiology
description: Covers spoilage and preservation of food; food quality and indicator organisms; the role of microorganisms in the production of dairy goods and fermented beverages; food-borne pathogens and microbiological production of toxins; and classical and modern molecular methods for detection of food microorganisms. Cross-listed with BIOL 122.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC; PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; STAT 010; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Introduction to Comparative Virology
description: Considers viruses as infectious agents of bacteria, plants, and animals (vertebrates and invertebrates). Compares the major groups of viruses with respect to their biological and biochemical properties, molecular and genetic characteristics, and modes of replication. Cross-listed with BIOL 123, and PLPA 123.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; BCH 100, may be taken concurrently or BCH 100H, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110A, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110HA, may be taken concurrently; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; STAT 010; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Medical Microbiology
description: An intensive introduction to the fundamental physiology and molecular biology of bacteria and viruses. Covers research strategies for examining microbial pathogenic mechanisms. Cross-listed with BIOL 124.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC; PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; STAT 010; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Experimental Microbiology
description: Introduces the process of performing experimental research in a microbiology laboratory. Teaches skills used in formulating hypotheses, designing experiments, performing laboratory experiments, analyzing data, and preparing and presenting research in written and oral formats. Experimental systems utilized vary from quarter to quarter. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 102; BIOL 107A; MCBL 121 or MCBL 131; MCBL 121L or MCBL 131L; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; restricted to major(s) Microbiology; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Microbiomes
description: Introduces microbiomes which are the collections of microorganisms that inhabit particular environments or locations and play crucial roles in agriculture, the environment, and human health and disease. Covers fundamental knowledge about microbiomes and experimental strategies to understand and utilize microbiomes to prevent or treat human and plant diseases. Credit is awarded for one of the following MCBL 126 or MCBL 226.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC; PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; STAT 010; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Microbial Evolution
description: Explores essential roles microbes perform in biogeochemical cycles, directly influencing human, plant, and animal health and disease. Provides important platforms for research and biotechnology. Details the evolutionary history and processes that underlie the critical roles of microbes. Credit is awarded for one of the following MCBL 127 or MCBL 227.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC; PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; STAT 010; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Field Mycology: Ecology, Evolution, and Diversity of Fungi
description: An overview of fungal diversity, morphology, ecology, and societal impacts. Topics include fungal diversity, mushroom identification, fungal culturing, molecular methods, and bioinformatics. Explores impacts of fungi on ecosystem functions such as decomposition and symbiosis as well as on society including art, medicine, poisons, and food. Credit is awarded for one of the following MCBL 128 or MCBL 228.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Host Responses to Viral Pathogens
description: Explores host responses to viral infections. Presents content that promotes understanding of how viruses interact with innate immune responses of the mammalian host and how these responses impact disease outcomes for better or worse. Credit is awarded for one of the following MCBL 129 or MCBL 229.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Introductory Microbiology 2
description: An intensive introduction to the fundamental cellular and molecular biology of bacteria and viruses. Covers bacterial and viral molecular genetics, regulation, and physiology as well as an introduction to microbial pathogenesis. Restricted to major(s) in Microbiology. Credit is awarded for one of the following MCBL 131, BIOL 121, or MCBL 121.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; restricted to major(s) Microbiology; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Microbiology Laboratory 2
description: Laboratory and written exercises in diagnostic bacteriology, basic virology, and epidemiology. Topics include fundamental quantitative and diagnostic microbiological procedures, basic mechanisms of microbial genetic exchange, and a project examining bacterial epidemiology. Restricted to major(s) in Microbiology. Credit is awarded for one of the following MCBL 131L, BIOL 121L, or MCBL 121L.
prerequisites_text: MCBL 131 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to major(s) Microbiology; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Environmental Microbiology
description: Introduction to nonpathogenic microorganisms in the environment. Topics include an introduction to microbial biology and microbial and metabolic genetic diversity; methods; symbiotic interactions; biofilms; and geomicrobiology and biogeochemistry. Explores life in extreme environments and the effects of the physical and chemical environment on microbes. Cross-listed with ENSC 133.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005A, BIOL 05LA or BIOL 020, BIOL 005B, BIOL 005C; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: The Evolution of Conflict and Cooperation: Cheaters and Altruists
description: Explores the evolution of selfish and selfless behavior. An analysis of the evolutionary forces that create either conflict or cooperation among genes, microorganisms and their hosts, and kin. Cross-listed with ENTM 139.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; or consent of instructor

subject: MCBL
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: Individual research in microbiology performed under the guidance of the staff or faculty. Letter grades are assigned to students presenting a research paper; other students are graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 9 units.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor; upper-division standing

subject: MCBL
title: Individual Internship in Microbiology
description: Provides opportunity for career exploration in microbiology. Includes supervision by a faculty member and an off-campus sponsor. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 121 or MCBL 121 or MCBL 131; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; and consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to Media and Cultural Studies
description: Introduces the history and methods of media and cultural studies. Includes several key concepts, trends, texts, and lines of inquiry that have shaped this field since the birth of modern journalism and cinema. Identifies the particular strengths and foci of Media and Cultural Studies at UCR.

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to Immersive Media
description: Focuses on tools for fast prototyping interactive media. Combines contemporary board and pencil and paper game and card design with computer game design, VR, and digital/web production.
prerequisites_text: MCS 001 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Immersive Media Production
description: Focuses on creative activity. Students with existing expertise in a design field are brought together for a devised project.
prerequisites_text: MCS 002 with a grade of B- or better; permission of the instructor (auditioned by portfolio); or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to Moving Images: Film, Video and New Media
description: Explores issues and skills of video/film/media art based in production, history, and theory of the moving image. Introduces basic production, editing concepts and techniques of live-action production, story boards, image editing, and final authoring. Examines the moving image through installation, documentary, experimental film, video art, sound art, and performance. Cross-listed with ART 004.

subject: MCS
title: Media Studies: Theory and Practice
description: Introduces the broad field of media and communication studies, covers the history and the current state of various media industries, discusses Internet-based technological developments, examines media laws and policies, and explores the relationships among media, culture, society and audiences from different theoretical approaches.

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to Contemporary Critical Issues in Art
description: Examines basic principles and methodologies of theory as applied to the interpretation and creation of works of art. Includes screenings. Cross-listed with ART 006.

subject: MCS
title: Digital Journalism and Society
description: Explores the emerging field of digital journalism. Discusses its theoretical, professional, and practical dimensions. Topics include history, technology, political economy, content, and pattern of digital journalism; innovative journalistic practices; and the impact of digital media on contemporary culture, politics, and society.

subject: MCS
title: Music in Movies and Tv
description: An exploration of popular film and TV soundtrack music, emphasizing drama and musical style. Scene study features such films as The Matrix, Casablanca, The X-Files, and Altered States. Cross-listed with MUS 007.

subject: MCS
title: Cultural Studies: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives
description: Investigates culture through the frameworks of feminism, Marxism, and race theories. Analyzes the different methodologies cultural critics use to theorize subcultures, cultural policies, and consumption. Explores ways cultural works are not only produced and received but also distributed and circulated within national and transnational contexts.

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to Television Studies
description: An introduction to the study of television, including its stylistic conventions, primary genres, modes of production, economics, and important critical methodologies.

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to Film Studies
description: An introduction to the formal and narrative principles of film construction and to various critical approaches to the cinema, such as auteur and genre theory. Provides an overview of world cinemas.

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to Media Art
description: An introduction to the impact of media technology on the visual arts from photography to the Internet. Addresses mechanical reproduction, perception, gender, sexuality, identity, interactivity, cybernetics, and popular culture. Cross-listed with AHS 020.

subject: MCS
title: World Cinema
description: Introduction to world cinema as a fusion of national and international, culturally specific, and globally universal characteristics.
