Topics include realism, the role of world wars, Hollywood’s global reach, alternative aesthetics of third-world cinemas, cross-fertilization between Europe and Asia, and the function of international film festivals and the international film market. Cross-listed with CPLT 024.

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to the Built Environment: Suburbia
description: Introduces the history of suburbia from the Industrial Revolution to the present. Includes the rise of suburbs in England; classic suburbs in the United States; the spread of suburbs and mass transportation; the role of race and gender in suburbia; suburban sprawl in Southern California; and sustainability and suburban development. Cross-listed with URST 025.

subject: MCS
title: Art of the Synthesizer
description: Explores the history of synthesizers through the stories of pioneering electronic musicians. Introduces the concepts of modular synthesis through applied patch designs with virtual software. Cross-listed with MUS 026.

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to Video Game Studies
description: Offers an introduction to the critical study of video games. Considers questions about the meaning of play. Explores media form and content including video game representations and media effects on individuals and groups.

subject: MCS
title: Introduction to Global National Or Regional Media and Cultures
description: Provides a historical overview of a variety of media and cultures specific to a national or regional context. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 10 units. Cross-listed with SPN 046.

subject: MCS
title: Screenwriting: How Movies Work
description: An Introduction to writing for stage and screen. Addresses structure, character, dialogue, theme, and story. Cross-listed with CRWT 066, and TFDP 066.

subject: MCS
title: The Politics of Public Space
description: Introduces theories and history of public space in modern cities. Topics include public space during the Industrial Revolution; modern planning and urban renewal; political uses of public space including demonstrations and occupations; privatization and policing of public spaces; and changing concepts of public and private space in contemporary society. Cross-listed with URST 069.

subject: MCS
title: Race, Gender, and the Superhero
description: Explores the racialized and gendered construction of superheroes across the genres of comics, television, graphic novels, film, animation, Japanese manga and other digital forms. Content may emphasize themes of sustainability, and the history of superheroes in the US and Japan.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Topics in State Violence, Policing and Criminalization
description: Intensive formal, historical, or theoretical analysis of a theme or issue in criminalization, policing, and State violence.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Drug Markets A Critical Analysis
description: Examines the emergence, stability, and decline of illegal drug markets. Analyzes the meanings, behaviors, and interactions of illegal drug market participants. Emphasizes the roles of economic, political, and criminal justice factors in shaping and influencing illegal drug markets.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Gangs A Critical Analysis
description: Examines the origins, growth, and decline of gangs. Analyzes the meanings, behaviors, and interactions of gang members within their communities. Emphasizes the importance of the economy, politics, public perceptions, and historical context in shaping and influencing gang formation and structure.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Incarceration and Domestic Warfare in the United States
description: Offers a historical, analytical, and theoretical examination of the cultural formation of criminalization and incarceration in the United States. Contextualizes the US carceral regime’s roots in the cultural-political structures of racial chattel slavery, land conquest, settler colonization, and the statecraft of anti-Black violence.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Political Culture of Race and Policing: Domestic Warfare, Counterinsurgency, and Abolition
description: Introduces a critical, analytical, and theoretical approach to the culture of modern police and policing focusing on the United States. Examines how the cultures of law-and-order and domestic warfare normalize antiblack, racist, and colonial state violence.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Film and Media Theory
description: Covers different types of film and media theory. Addresses formalist, psychoanalytic, Marxist, feminist, and other approaches to the cinema and other media. Cross-listed with ENGL 104.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Global Communication
description: Introduces a variety of theoretical perspectives that inform global communication and media studies. Compares different world media systems. Surveys global media conglomerates and explores global communication in a digital age.
prerequisites_text: upper division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Topics in Media Production
description: Teaches basic skills in production of selected media such as podcasts, graphic novel, and social documentary. Includes weekly reading of material corresponding to the lecture. Also includes, but is not limited to, lab work, streaming, group work, extra-reading, and individual research.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Podcasting Production
description: A study of podcast methods and the use of sound. Teaches podcast production with a large creative component. No prior experience required.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Alternative Media Production and Social Movements
description: Engages with alternative media to think critically about why such media is necessary. Provides a forum to produce and present original research as media-makers.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Documentary Film Production
description: Explores possibilities for telling stories about society. Incorporates still and moving images; sounds from the field, studio, and archive; and creative and chaotic editing.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Comics Production
description: Provides guidance through the process of comic creation. Covers from concept and character design to scripting, layout, and final production. Develops skills in ideation (character development), sketching (“thumbnails”), inking, and lettering. No prior drawing experience required.
prerequisites_text: MCS 149 with a grade of C or better; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Electric Earth: Media Ecology Theory Culture
description: Introduces media ecology theory and history. Explores key topics, concepts, and issues at the upper-division level. Develops methods for thinking about contemporary media ecology, examining objects such as smart cities, animal technologies, and the media saturated planet. Outside class assignments include readings and conducting individual research and writing projects.
prerequisites_text: MCS 001 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Computation and Culture
description: Intensive formal, theoretical, or historical analysis of a topic in Computation and Culture. Each segment will consist of reading material corresponding to lecture. and the “activity” may include but is not limited to lab work, streaming, group work, extra-reading, individual research.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Algorithms and Everyday Life
description: Utilizes technologies including artificial intelligence, Tinder, and Uber to examine cultures of algorithms, data, and code. Explores the use of algorithms to shape futures, govern bodies, advance systemic violence, and conceal injustices. Also addresses the use of data to intervene unjust datascapes.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Critical Artificial Intelligence
description: Utilizes technologies including artificial intelligence, Tinder, and Uber to examine cultures of algorithms, data, and code. Explores the use of algorithms to shape futures, govern bodies, advance systemic violence, and conceal injustices. Also addresses the use of data to intervene unjust datascapes.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Topics in Film and Media History
description: Introduction to the technical and artistic developments of cinema up through the advent of film sound. Investigates the formal, cultural, and political aspects of visual culture internationally in the period roughly demarcated by the invention of photography, (around 1839) and the advent of full-fledged propaganda documentary.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: History of Media Theory
description: A survey of the historical development of media theory from the 1920s to the present. Uses a balanced approach to evaluate two major bodies of theory currently dominating the field of media studies: social/behavioral and critical /cultural theories.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Inventing the Moving Image: Cinema Before Sound
description: Considers topics in the history of film and media with attention to their aesthetic, socio-political, and economic contexts.
prerequisites_text: see individual segments for activities and prerequisites

subject: MCS
title: History of Documentary Film
description: A transnational survey of the documentary film from the silent era to the digital age. Topics include how to define nonfiction cinema; the social issue documentary of the 1930s; Cinema vÈritÈ; propaganda; ethnographic media; the essay film; experimental forms; media activism; re-enactment; and the role of changing technologies.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: History of Queer Cinema
description: An introduction to the aesthetic hallmarks, political impulses, and theoretical responses that distinguish queer cinema as a unique, important tradition within film history. Provides a historical overview of global, independent, Hollywood, and alternative queer production from the 1900s to the present. Cross-listed with LGBS 112, and GSST 112.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Cinematic War Memory
description: Examines cinematic confrontations involving World War II in Germany and Japan. Topics include desire between victims and perpetrators, representation of trauma, and ethical responsibility. All screenings have English subtitles. Cross-listed with CPLT 134, GER 134, and JPN 134.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: On Networks: Digital Culture, Media, Technology
description: Examines theories, histories, forms, aesthetics, and cultures of the network. Establishes touchpoints of network theory and history and uncovers key topic areas. Addresses how networked life transforms understandings of individuality and concepts of agency and helps foster collective units, propagate contagious affect, and re-organize space and place.
prerequisites_text: MCS 005

subject: MCS
title: Posthuman Bodies in Science, Media, and Culture
description: Introduces cultures and theories of posthuman media. Examines media technologies, representations, and representative practices in the sciences. Topics include biopolitics, posthumanism, ecosickness, and speculation. Approaches posthuman media studies with perspectives from queer theory, eco-feminist theory, and disability studies.
prerequisites_text: MCS 005

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Topics in German Cinema
description: Study of selected films, directors, and movements in German film. Films are in German with English subtitles. No knowledge of German is required. Cross-listed with GER 118 (E-Z).

subject: MCS
title: Weimar Cinema and After
description: An investigation of the silent and sound films of the Weimar era, focusing on the works of Fritz Lang, G. W. Pabst, and F. W. Murnau and their impact on film directors such as Werner Herzog and Rainer W. Fassbinder. Includes readings in film theory and in the literature and cultural history of the period. Cross-listed with GER 118E.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: The Cinema of Fritz Lang
description: In-depth study of the films of the Austrian-born director Fritz Lang (1890-1976), whose work spans the silent era, the Golden Age of Hollywood, and postwar Germany. Explores the evolution of film technique, changes in cinematic paradigms, and Lang’s engagement with ideology. Cross-listed with GER 118F.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Film and the Holocaust
description: Examines the moral, philosophical, and cultural legacy of the Holocaust in documentary and narrative films. Films and selected theoretical and literary texts involve key issues such as truthfulness, politicization, marginalization, universalization, trivialization, abstraction, representation of trauma, abstraction, aestheticization, and testimonies. Cross-listed with GER 118G.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Topics in Memory and Resistance 1
description: Introduces the theory, methods, ethics, and political stakes of Memory and Resistance work. Offers training in and application of needed media skills including the production of short-form media. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Topics in Memory and Resistance 2
description: Expands upon the conceptual, technical, and creative work completed in previous quarters. Engages in a large-scale collaborative media project with a grassroots organization. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: MCS 119A; restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Major Figures in Film and Media
description: Intensive analysis of the work of a significant figure in film, television, or other media who functions as an “auteur” (e.g. an influential director, star, or producer). Course is repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Live-Streaming and Gaming Enthnography: Online Research Methods
description: Develops a skill set of online research methods tailored to address questions concerning live-streaming, gaming, and online social media interaction.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Asian American Women: Writing the Self in Literature and Film
description: Analyzes Asian American autobiographies and films written and directed by women. Explores why the genre of autobiography is enabling and contentious within Asian American women’s writings. Examines films to see how such women filmmakers contend with memory, gender, and identity. Cross-listed with GSST 124, and SEAS 175.
prerequisites_text: MCS 010, upper-division standing, or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Latin America, Democracy, and the Media
description: Explores the construct of democracy in Latin America related to various media. Introduces current political and cultural issues in multiple countries. Critically reflects on the concept of democracy and how different social actors understand democracy. Evaluates the role of media in democratic processes.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Topics in Latin American Film and Media
description: Intensive formal, historical, and theoretical analysis of a theme or issue in Latin American film and media. Cross-listed with LNST 125 (E-Z), and SPN 125 (E-Z).
prerequisites_text: See individual segments for Units, prerequisites, and activities

subject: MCS
title: Indigenous Video and Latin America
description: An introduction to classic works of German literature and their film adaptations. Explores adaptations by film directors such as Welles, Kubrick, Visconti, and Fassbinder. Studies the nexus between literature, film, and theatre. Course conducted in English. Cross-listed with LNST 125 (E-Z) and SPN 125 (E-Z).
prerequisites_text: MCS 020 or upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Imagining the Nation: Film and Media in Latin America
description: Study of the role of media and film in creating a national imaginary in Latin America. Focus is on one region or nation such as the Andes, the Caribbean, Mexico, Argentina, or Chile relating local history to the global context. Cross-listed with LNST 125I, and SPN 125I.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Chicana/O Cultural Studies and Gender Politics
description: Examines the field of Chicana/o cultural studies and investigates the gender politics that attest to its intersectional approach. Considers how power and gendered politics have impacted the restructuring of the split subject in Chicana/o cultural studies. Cross-listed with GSST 166.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Disney: Producing Race, Gender and Sexuality
description: Investigates the articulation of race, gender, sexuality, and class in Disney-based productions. Examines how globalization, capitalism and consumption intersect in the production of race, gender, class, disabilities and sexualities. Considers the relation between the Disney Corporation and cultures as commodities and imperialist corporate politics. Credit is awarded for only one of MCS 129 or MCS 129S.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Disney: Producing Race, Gender and Sexuality
description: Investigates the articulation of race, gender, sexuality, and class in Disney-based productions. Examines how globalization, capitalism and consumption intersect in the production of race, gender, class, disabilities and sexualities. Considers the relation between the Disney Corporation and cultures as commodities and imperialist corporate politics. Credit is awarded for only one of MCS 129 or MCS 129S.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Filipino American Culture
description: Explores the politics of a range of Filipino American expressive, performative, and creative forms (e.g., Pilipino Culture Night) video, art, fiction, theater, in tandem with the study of theoretical and socio-historical scholarship in the interdisciplinary field of Filipino American Studies. Cross-listed with SEAS 130.
prerequisites_text: MCS 001

subject: MCS
title: Intermediate Photography and Digital Technology
description: Covers the complete cycle of photographic production from scanning to output. Emphasizes developing skill in creating digital photographic imagery for creative and cultural expression. Software and some digital equipment are provided. A 35mm single lens reflex (SLR) or digital cameras and flash drives are required. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units. Cross-listed with ART 131.
prerequisites_text: ART 003 or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Intersections of Media and Popular Culture
description: Focuses on production sites and distribution and consumption of media. Explores how theoretical frameworks converge in the examination of connections between cultural texts and social contexts and between media and society.
prerequisites_text: upper division standing or consent from instructor Examines the interconnections of media technologies, modes of audience engagement, and the political and economic contexts of audience formation

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Topics in Media and Environmental Justice
description: Examines issues related to media, environment, environmental justice, sustainability, and Anthropocene. Each segment consists of reading material corresponding to the lecture and the activity schedule type that may include but is not limited to lab work, streaming, group work, extra-reading, individual research.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Media, Sustainability, and the Future of Democracy
description: A critical cultural analysis of the discourses underlining and validating the degradation and destruction of our natural environments, engendering vast income inequalities.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Mediating the Anthropocene
description: Examines anthropogenic climate change and activism as cultural and media events.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Human and Nonhuman: Decolonial and Audiovisual Perspectives
description: Study of decolonial, Indigenous, and audiovisual approaches to conceiving the human/ nonhuman. Examines issues such as environmental justice, environmental cinema, Indigenous perspectives.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Transmedia: Demonstration Project
description: Introduces strategies for organizing and presenting materials, ideas, and arguments in various media. Includes visual, written, and audio texts; the spoken word; and performance.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Intermedia: Art, Media, and Culture
description: A study of performance, photography, video, film, television, installation, and other related “intermedias.” Focuses on intermedial artworks and how they are constructed, documented, analyzed, and viewed in the larger context of culture. Cross-listed with ART 135.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Mass Media and Popular Culture
description: A comparative analysis of the television, radio, record, cinema, and journalism industries as social institutions and a discussion of contemporary developments in mass communications theory. A study of the relationship between the social processes of modern society and the content of popular culture. Cross-listed with SOC 139.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: MCS
title: Alternative Media Production and Social Movements
description: Introduces the history, theory, and practice of alternative forms of media production. Focuses on how various media forms were used to disseminate information in order to motivate audiences to take action for social change. Provides opportunities to learn documentary making, experiment with media forms, and produce alternative media projects. Course is repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Gender in Southeast Asian Diasporic Literature and Film
description: Focuses on former Indochinese refugees who are producing literature and films in the United States and France. Examines how the perception of Indochina has been constructed, particularly how the region has been gendered female in the colonial imaginary. Explores the return of Southeast Asian immigrants to the Western gaze. Cross-listed with GSST 122, and SEAS 172.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Gender, Sexuality, and Visual Cultures
description: An intensive formal, historical, and theoretical analysis of gender and sexuality in film, television, and visual culture. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 12 units. Cross-listed with ENGL 143.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Race, Ethnicity, and Visual Culture
description: Intensive formal, historical, and theoretical analysis of race and ethnicity in film, television, and visual culture. Weekly screenings and readings. Cross-listed with

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Special Topics in Film and Visual Culture
description: An intensive formal, historical, and theoretical analysis of a theme or issue in film, media, television, and visual culture. Cross-listed with ENGL 145 (E-Z).

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Special Topics in Technoculture and Digital Media
description: Advanced study of theories and practices of reader and audience interaction with technologies of cultural production in general and digital media in particular. Includes praxis-oriented composition or research. Cross-listed with

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Topics in Afrofuturism
description: Examines topics in Afrofuturism and the creative visual arts.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Visual Culture and Afrofuturism
description: An introduction to the cultural production of space called Afrofuturism and the history of the black speculative arts. Includes how the speculative affects representations of race and blackness in literature, visual culture, and music.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Afrofuturism and the Visual Cultures of Horror
description: An introduction to the trope of the grotesque and the myriad societal fears regarding what the monster symbolizes in visual mediations of the horror genre. Analyzes the tensions between the imaginings of the monstrous and how identity is constructed and consumed.
prerequisites_text: MCS 001, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Afrofuturism and the Politics of the Black Superhero
description: Covers the political aspects of the superhero genre and its historical tensions with representations of black characters. Also explores how black superheroes speak to the cultural production system called Afrofuturism and its inherent celebration of agency regarding black subjectivity in the comics medium.
prerequisites_text: MCS 001, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Bodies in Motion: Cinema as Choreography
description: Introduction of cinema as a kind of choreography. Examines how it sets bodies in motion both on and in front of the screen. Considers some of the ways bodily movement was understood philosophically, scientifically, and bureaucratically at the moment cinema emerged.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Between the Panels: Introduction to United States and Identity in Visual Culture
description: An introduction to the history of the medium of comics In the United States. It will also examine the tensions between the mainstream focus of comics and graphic novels represented via the superhero genre and the alternatively diverse narratives that are afforded through the medium.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Intermediate Moving Images: Film Video and New Media
description: Examines the moving image through installation, documentary, experimental film, video art, sound art, and performance. Builds upon production and editing concepts introduced in ART 004/MCS 004. Explores issues and skills of video/film/media art based in production, history, and theory of the moving image. Covers editing theory, lighting, and sound editing. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 10 units. Cross-listed with ART 150.
prerequisites_text: ART 004/MCS 004

subject: MCS
title: Gender, Mechanization, and Shape
description: Utilizes film, video, and texts to examine the relationship among gender, mechanization, and shape during the twentieth century. Focuses on the performing arts, industrial and technological design, and the relationship of visual culture to changing notions of gender. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with DNCE171G.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Spectatorship
description: Explores the nature of film studies through the eyes of the audience. Uses film, videos, and texts (in addition to outside viewing of films in cinematic locales) to formulate how viewing film constructs the viewer’s subjectivity and a film’s cultural context. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with DNCE 171J.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Attractions, Interruptions, Disruptions: Narrative Film:fight Scenes, Dance Sequences,special Effect
description: Analyzes the way film regulates the movement of bodies on and off screen through narrative and what happens when the movement exceeds that regulations. Utilizes selected films to explore the fight scenes, dance sequences, and computer generated imagery in film. Includes screenings both in class and outside of class. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with DNCE 171K.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Bollywood
description: A study of the vast corpus of films that constitute the genre called Bollywood. Focuses on the genre’s music and dance styles. Includes weekly film screenings. No previous dance experience required. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with DNCE171M.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Televisual Bodies
description: Analyzes choreographic practices within television broadcast and marketing and their relation to popular culture. Also examines situational or tactical use and misuse of satellite, cablecast, and broadcast television by unintentional audiences that subsequently reconstitute themselves as communities via the programming. Focuses on video as an archival and/or choreographic tool. J. Corporations And Corporealities: Commercials, Culture, And Choreography; K. Television As Location: The Satellite Feed; M. Music Television (mtv) And Popular Culture. Course is repeatable to a maximum of units. Cross-listed with DNCE 172 (E-Z).
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Digitized Bodies
description: Provides a theoretical approach to digital subjectivities, bodies in motion, products, and realities. Addresses issues of liveness, new media, mediated cultural identities, speed, transfer, telepresence, and coded and encoded sexuality within programming. Focuses primarily on the body-computer interface. J. Digital Games, Violence, And The Body; K. Virtual Subjectivity: Persona, Identity, And Body. Course is repeatable to a maximum of units. Cross-listed with DNCE 173 (E-Z).
prerequisites_text: MCS 020; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Media, Gender, and Violence
description: Examines media representations of women and violence. Topics include feminist and queer theory, pornography, sexual violence, state violence, censorship, militarization, policing, and intersections with race, ethnicity, class, sexualities, and citizenship. Analyzes cinema, television, video, gaming, digital, print, and other visual and acoustic media. Course repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Advanced Moving Images: Film, Video and New Media
description: Expands on skills introduced in ART 150/MCS 150. Explores issues and skills connected with video/film/media art based on the production, history, and theory of the moving image. Covers recording, editing theory, lighting, and sound mixing. Examines time-based media through installation, documentary, experimental film, video art, sound art, and performance. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units. Cross-listed with ART 155.
prerequisites_text: ART 150/ MCS 150

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) South Asian Media and Cultures
description: Explores the construction of various South Asian media. Considers confluence of new technologies of production and distribution, as well as the liberalization and globalization of different economies and social structures. E. Bollywood.

subject: MCS
title: Race, Space, and Identity
description: Examines the intersection of race, space, and identity in modern and contemporary culture. Explores the critical and constitutive importance of race in the built environment. Topics include the racialization of space; colonialism and colonial cities; expositions and world’s fairs; segregation; race and the canon; decolonization; and urban renewal. Cross-listed with URST 159.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Tool, Technology, Technique
description: Practicum in video and digital production with an emphasis on capturing and editing the moving body. Students are encouraged to bring their own video or digital recording device. Editing equipment will be available. Cross-listed with DNCE 162.
prerequisites_text: DNCE 019 or MCS 019 or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Special Topics in Art Criticism and Theory
description: Advanced topics in contemporary art theory and criticism. Examines the reception, analysis, and theoretical underpinning of works of art in relation to contemporary and historical issues in the visual arts. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units. Cross-listed with ART 161.
prerequisites_text: MCS 001 with a grade of C- or better or ART 160 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Digital Media and Participatory Citizenship
description: A critical analysis of the new media environment. Explores options of operating as producers of culture. Includes design of an innovative intervention for circulation in the evolving digital media environment, as well as evaluation of its contribution and possible impact. Course is repeatable with consent of department or as topics change to a maximum of 12 units.

subject: MCS
title: Virtual Reality Beyond Images
description: Probes human activity systems, citizenship, simulations, and being digital. Surveys the realities of past, present, and futures with a critical eye towards embodiment, subjectivity, positionality, and social justice.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Topics in Asian Media and Cultures
description: Intensive formal, historical, and theoretical analyses of themes and issues in Asian media and culture.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Hong Kong Cinema
description: A survey of the evolution of Hong Kong cinema from the postwar era to the present. Topics include Hong Kong martial arts cinema and its global influence; New Wave Movement and its diverse styles including art and crime/gangster movies; as well as Hong Kong cinema’s post-handover status.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Global Chinese Martial Arts Cinema
description: Introduction to the historical development of Chinese martial arts cinema from the 1920s to 2020. Emphasizes this genre’s relationship with science and fate, with nationalism and modernity, with transnationalism and identity, and with soft power.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Chinese Media and Society
description: A general survey of the structure of China’s media system as well as the system’s significant transformation during the reform era (after 1978). Examines the development of newspaper, the Internet, television, and film.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MCS
title: Senior Seminar On the Anthropocene
description: Explores anthropogenic climate change.
prerequisites_text: MCS 133E, MCS 108, MCS 163, MCS 177, MCS 140, MCS 109E; or equivalent; restricted to class level standing of senior; restricted to major(s) Media and Cultural Studies; prior research and/or course work on sustainability, climate change, media or art production; and consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Reel to Real: Latin American Film and Social Change
description: Introduces Latin American film as it articulates with contemporary history and current events. Cross-listed with SPN 171.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: MCS
title: Topics in Film and Media Genres
description: Topics may include study of a specific film or media genre; comparative genre studies (including a survey of the history and theory of two or more genres); or analysis of the concept of genre in film and media studies. Each segment is repeatable as its content changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) International Cinemas
description: Considers non-Hollywood cinemas in the national, historical, political, and cultural contexts which produced them. E. Experimental And Avant-garde Film; F. French New Wave; G. New German Cinema; I. Italian Neorealism; M. Global Chinese Martial Arts Cinema; T. Third World Cinema; U. Global Perspective On The Vietnam War. Cross-listed with CPLT 173 (E-Z).
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: (E-Z) Comparative Studies in Film
description: Considers film in the context of the other arts. Compares the treatment of various themes or problems in film and other media. E. Film & Literature Avant-agarde. Cross-listed with

subject: MCS
title: Indigenous Media
description: Examines and compares the strategies indigenous videomakers use to counter the imperial gaze of cinema. Discusses possibilities for turning the art form of capitalism and colonialism into a tool for decolonization.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Gender, Media, and Latin America
description: Explores the way Latin Americans have thought of and represented gender across a variety of media including essays, film, novel, short story, and performance. Compares the possibilities and limitations of these media for representing gender in the Latin American context. Cross-listed with LNST 109, SPN 179, and GSST 179.
prerequisites_text: MCS 020 or upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Japanese Documentary
description: Studies the history of Japanese documentary cinema. Teaches strategies for reading nonfiction visual narrative. Explores other forms of documentation controversial in modern Japanese history including oral testimony, photography, and internet activism. Topics may include war, war protest, peace activism, environmental activism, nuclear politics, and green energy. Course is repeatable as topics and instructor change to a maximum of 8 units. Cross-listed with JPN 180, and AST 180.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Topics in Television Genres
description: An in-depth analysis of a selected television genre. May include history of the specific genre across time periods or may focus on a specific time period. Combines screenings of episodes and scholarly readings about the medium. Topics include aesthetics, political economy, and cultural critique. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units. Cross-listed with ENGL 182.
prerequisites_text: MCS 015

subject: MCS
title: Special Topics in Television Culture
description: Provides a comprehensive introduction to a particular debate in television studies. Topics vary with each offering and may include politics of representation; broadcast, cable and streaming; and in-depth analysis of a specific series. Combines historical with aesthetic approaches. Integrates screenings of episodes with scholarly readings. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units. Cross-listed with ENGL 183.
prerequisites_text: MCS 015; or equivalent

subject: MCS
title: Japanese Media and Cultural Studies
description: Investigates Japanese media and culture including film, television, video games, manga (comics), anime, music, and print and digital media. Analyzes the function of media relating to issues of national identity, imperial culture, collective memory, and censorship. Includes transnational circulation of Japanese cultural forms, alternative media, and historical changes in technologies. Cross-listed with AST 184, and JPN 184.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Media and Movements: Film, Video, Photography, and the Visual Arts
description: Focuses on key cultural movements or developments as global arts over the past century. Provides a thematic history of the avant-garde and experimental arts including painting, sculpture, photography, video, film, performance, installation, and new media art. Cross-listed with AHS 186.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Theorizing New Media
description: Approaches new media through its archaeology. Introduces theories of media and mediation, focusing on digital media and networked society. Draws from classic theory and from contemporary activist practice.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Media & Militarism
description: Studies the function and effects of militarism and media. Includes how militarism is represented through various media genres such as cinema, television, advertising, documentary films, video games, digital, and new media. Explores its intersection with gender, race, class, religion, and nation.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Political Culture of Race and Policing: Domestic Warfare, Counterinsurgency, and Abolition
description: Introduces a critical, analytical, and theoretical approach to the culture of modern police and policing focusing on the United States. Lectures and course assignments examine how the cultures of law-and-order and domestic warfare normalize antiblack, racist, and colonial state violence.
prerequisites_text: MCS 010; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Special Studies
description: Faculty-driven individual study to meet special curricular needs. Requires a final paper or creative project. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 15 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of instructor and program chair

subject: MCS
title: Junior Seminar
description: Critical study, practice, and assessment of cultural studies research methods. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: MCS 001, MCS 010; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; restricted to major(s) Media and Cultural Studies; or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: Senior Seminar
description: Advanced research in various fields of faculty interest. Includes completion of a research paper and a class presentation of its contents. Topics vary from year to year. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: senior standing or consent of instructor

subject: MCS
title: R’course: Variable Topics
description: An opportunity for UCR undergraduate students to develop leadership skills, innovate the undergraduate curriculum, and promote democratic, experiential education. Original course topics are variable and unique from other departmental course offerings, designed to highlight the student facilitators’ expertise while working closely with a faculty mentor. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 8 units.

subject: MCS
title: Individual Internship in Media and Cultural Studies
description: An internship in a professional organization or with an individual to gain skills and experience for a career in visual media. Requires the writing of reports, final paper, or the making of a creative project. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of instructor and the Media and Cultural Studies Chair

subject: ME
title: General Makerspace Fundamentals
description: Introduces makerspace-based fabrication techniques. Topics include methods of 3D printing, laser cutting, and sewing as well as measurements and design principles for fabrication and navigation of corresponding computer-aided design and slicing software. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 3 units.
prerequisites_text: ME 009 with a grade of C- or better; PHYS 040A with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 002A with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 02HA with a grade of B or better or PHYS 040HA with a grade of B or better or PHYS 041A with a grade of C- or better

subject: ME
title: Machining Fundamentals
description: Introduces basic machining techniques related to the field of mechanical engineering. Topics include metrology, milling, drilling, turning, and water-jet machining as well as design principles for machining and computer numerical codes. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 3 units.
prerequisites_text: ME 001LA with a grade of C- or better

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering
description: An introduction to the field of mechanical engineering. Topics include the mechanical engineering profession; machine components; forces in structures and fluids; materials and stresses; thermal and energy systems; machine motion; and machine design.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 040A or PHYS 002A or PHYS 02HA or PHYS 040HA or PHYS 041A

subject: ME
title: How Things Work: the Principles Behind Technology
description: Introduces the basic physical principles of engineering systems from everyday life such as automobiles, computers, and household appliances. Topics include conservation laws and the physics and chemistry of engineering systems. Does not confer credit towards a degree in the Bourns College of Engineering.

subject: ME
title: Energy and the Environment
description: Covers energy conservation, energy sources, market dynamics, and climate change. Addresses cultural, political, and social trends and their impact on the ecosystem. Discusses renewable and nonrenewable energy sources. Technical background not required. Does not confer credit towards a degree in the Bourns College of Engineering.

subject: ME
title: The Science of Mythbusting
description: Introduces to the scientific method for non-science majors. Explores the application of scientific concepts to test the validity of myths and events from news stories, movies, and other popular media. Provides critical reasoning skills necessary to interpret advertiser’s product claims, critique information on the World Wide Web, and understand new technologies.

subject: ME
title: Engineering Graphics and Design
description: Covers graphical concepts and projective geometry relating to spatial visualization and communication in design. Includes technical sketching, computer-aided design with solid modeling, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, and an introduction to the engineering design process.

subject: ME
title: Statics
description: Covers equilibrium of coplanar force systems; analysis of frames and trusses; noncoplanar force systems; friction; and distributed loads.
prerequisites_text: MATH 009C, PHYS 040A or PHYS 040HA

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Engineering Computation
description: An introduction to the use of MATLAB in engineering computation. Covers scripts and functions, programming, input/output, and two- and three-dimensional graphing. Introduces data analysis, numerical analysis, and numerical solutions for engineering problems.
prerequisites_text: MATH 009A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HA with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Computational Modeling in Mechanical Engineering
description: Introduces the concepts of computational modeling in mechanical engineering. Topics include formulation of mathematical models to solve problems involving vector analysis, complex numbers, linear algebra, and differential, and integral calculus. Explores analytical and numerical solutions to problems in mechanical engineering.
prerequisites_text: ME 018A, PHYS 040A with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 041A with a grade of C- or better

subject: ME
title: Thermodynamics
description: Introduces basic concepts and applications of thermodynamics relevant to mechanical engineering. Topics include work and energy, the first law of thermodynamics, properties of pure substances, system and control volume analysis, the Carnot cycle, heat and refrigeration cycles, the second law of thermodynamics, entropy, and reversible and irreversible processes. Credit is awarded for only one of CHE 100 or ME 100A.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A, ME 018B with a grade of C- or better, PHYS 040B or PHYS 040HB

subject: ME
title: Thermodynamics
description: Topics include the second law of thermodynamics, entropy function, entropy production, analysis of cycles, vapor power systems, gas power systems, refrigeration and heat pump systems, equations of state, thermodynamic property relations, ideal gas mixtures and psychrometrics, multicomponent systems, combustion, and reacting mixtures.
prerequisites_text: ME 100A

subject: ME
title: Dynamics
description: Topics include vector representation of kinematics and kinetics of particles; Newton’s laws of motion; force-mass-acceleration, work-energy, and impulse-momentum methods; kinetics of systems of particles and kinematics; and kinetics of rigid bodies.
prerequisites_text: MATH 046; ME 010 with a grade of C- or better; ME 018B with a grade of C- or better or CS 010B or MATH 031

subject: ME
title: Mechanics of Materials
description: Topics include mechanics of deformable bodies subjected to axial, torsional, shear, and bending loads; combined stresses; and their applications to the design of structures. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: ME 010 with a grade of C- or better, MATH 046

subject: ME
title: Fluid Mechanics
description: Introduces principles of fluid mechanics relevant to mechanical engineering. Topics include shear stresses and viscosity, fluid statics, pressure, forces on submerged surfaces, Bernoulli and mechanical energy equations, control volume approach, mass conservation, momentum and energy equations, the differential approach, turbulent flow in pipes, and lift and drag. Credit is awarded for one of the following ME 113 or CHE 114.
prerequisites_text: MATH 046; PHYS 040B or PHYS 040HB; ME 002 with a grade of C- or better; ME 010 with a grade of C- or better; ME 018B with a grade of C- or better

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Materials Science and Engineering
description: Covers materials classification, atomic structure and interatomic bonding, crystal structure of metals, imperfections in solids, diffusion, mechanical properties of engineering materials, strengthening mechanisms, basic concepts of fracture and fatigue, phase diagrams, ceramics, polymers, and composites.
prerequisites_text: CHEM 001B, PHYS 040C or PHYS 040HC; upper-division standing

subject: ME
title: Heat Transfer
description: Introduces the analysis of steady and transient heat conduction, fin and heat generating systems, two-dimensional conduction, internal and external forced convection, natural convection, radiation heat transfer, heat exchangers, and mass transfer. Credit is awarded for only one of CHE 116 or ME 116A.
prerequisites_text: MATH 046, ME 113 (ME 113 may be taken concurrently)

subject: ME
title: Heat Transfer
description: Covers analytical and numerical methods in heat transfer and fluid mechanics. Topics include heat conduction and convection, gaseous radiation, boiling and condensation, general aspects of phase change, mass transfer principles, multimode heat transfer and the simulation of thermal fields, and the heat transfer process.
prerequisites_text: ME 116A

subject: ME
title: Combustion and Energy Systems
description: Discusses premixed and diffusion flames; fuel-air thermochemistry; combustion-driven engine design and operation; engine cycle analysis; fluid mechanics in engine components; pollutant formation; and gas turbines.
prerequisites_text: ME 100A; ME 113; ME 116A; for ME 117 online section; enrollment in the Online Master of Science in Engineering program; graduate standing

subject: ME
title: Mechanical Engineering Modeling and Analysis
description: Introduces data analysis and modeling used in engineering through the software package MATLAB. Numerical methods include descriptive and inferential statistics, sampling and bootstrapping, fitting linear and nonlinear models to observed data, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration, and solution of systems of ordinary differential equations. Final project involves the development and evaluation of a model for an engineering system. Credit is awarded for only one of ENGR 118 or ME 118.
prerequisites_text: MATH 046, ME 018B with a grade of C- or better

subject: ME
title: Linear Systems and Controls
description: Introduces the modeling and analysis of dynamic systems, emphasizing the common features of mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, thermal, electrical, and electromechanical systems. Controls are introduced through state equations, equilibrium, linearization, stability, and time and frequency domain analysis.
prerequisites_text: EE 005 or EE 030A, EE 030LA; CS 010B, MATH 031 or ME 018B

subject: ME
title: Feedback Control
description: Introduces the analysis and design of feedback control systems using classical control methods. Topics include control system terminology, block diagrams, analysis and design of control systems in the time and frequency domains, closed-loop stability, root locus, Bode plots, and an introduction to analysis in state-space. Credit is awarded for one of the following ME 121 or EE 132.

subject: ME
title: Vibrations
description: Covers free and forced vibration of discrete systems with and without damping resonance; matrix methods for multiple degree-of-freedom systems; normal modes, coupling, and normal coordinates; and use of energy methods.
prerequisites_text: ME 103

subject: ME
title: Kinematic and Dynamic Analysis of Mechanisms
description: Explores the kinematic analysis of planar mechanisms including linkages, cams, and gear trains. Introduces concepts of multibody dynamics.

subject: ME
title: Design of Mechanisms
description: Involves design of planar, spherical, and spatial mechanisms using both exact and approximate graphical and analytical techniques. Requires a computer-aided design project.
prerequisites_text: ME 130

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Mechatronics
description: Introduces hardware, software, sensors, actuators, physical systems models, and control theory in the context of control system implementation. Covers data acquisition (Labview), sensors, actuators, electric circuits and components, semiconductor electronics, logic circuits, signal processing using analog operational amplifiers, programmable logic controllers, and microcontroller programming and interfacing. Uses MATLAB and Simulink.
prerequisites_text: EE 005 or EE 030A, EE 030LA

subject: ME
title: Microstructural Transformations in Materials
description: An introductory study of the fundamentals (thermodynamics and kinetics) controlling microstructural transformations in materials and their application to both liquid-solid and solid-solid transformations. Focuses on the important transformations that ultimately control the microstructures and properties of crystalline solids. Cross-listed with MSE 134.
prerequisites_text: ME 114 or consent of instructor

subject: ME
title: Transport Phenomena
description: Introduces new concepts of thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer: sychrometry, combustion, one-dimensional compressible flow, and turbomachinery. Integrates the most important concepts of transport of momentum, heat, and mass.
prerequisites_text: ME 100A, ME 113, ME 116A

subject: ME
title: Environmental Impacts of Energy Production and Conversion
description: Covers thermodynamics, heat transfer, and fluid mechanics as applied to the examination of the environmental impacts of energy production and conversion. Topics include pollution associated with fossil fuel combustion, environmental impacts of energy use, turbulent transport of pollutants, and principles used in the design of pollution control equipment.
prerequisites_text: ME 100A; ME 113; ME 116A; for the ME 136 online version section; enrollment in the Online Master of Science in Engineering program; graduate standing

subject: ME
title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
description: Covers the application of fluid mechanics to flows in the atmosphere and oceans. Topics include hydrostatic balance, Coriolis effects, geostrophic balance, boundary layers, turbulence, tracer and heat transport.
prerequisites_text: ME 100A, ME 113

subject: ME
title: Transport Phenomena in Living Systems
description: An introduction to the application of the basic conservation laws of mechanics (mass, linear momentum, and energy) to the modeling of complex biological systems. Emphasizes how these concepts can explain and predict life processes.
prerequisites_text: BIEN 105 or ME 113, MATH 046, PHYS 040B or PHYS 040HB

subject: ME
title: Ship Theory
description: Covers ship hull form, static and dynamic stability, ship response to waves, grounding and flooding, numerical integration of complex three-dimensional curved shapes and mathematical modeling of curved surfaces. Explores engineering approximations necessary for applications of fundamental principles to complex engineering systems such as ships.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Robotic Manipulation
description: Introduces mathematical representations of the configuration and spatial motion of robotic manipulators based on modern screw theory. Topics include forward, inverse, differential kinematics.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 040A with a grade of C- or better, MATH 031 with a grade of C- or better or ME 018B with a grade of C- or better or CS 30M with a grade of C- or better, MATH 046 with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent

subject: ME
title: Foundations of Robotics
description: Provides foundational knowledge on analysis, control, and programming of robots. Considers configuration space; rigid body motion; forward, inverse, and velocity kinematics; dynamics; trajectory planning; robot motion control; localization and mapping; and robot ethics. Integrates hands-on labs to program robots in simulation and experimentally by reading and interpreting sensor data. Cross-listed with EE 144. Credit is awarded for one of the following EE 144, ME 144, or EE 283A.
prerequisites_text: EE 020B or MATH 031 or ME 018B; EE 016 or CS 010B or ME 118; EE 106 or CS 141 or ME 120; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ME
title: Robotic Planning and Kinematics
description: Motion planning and kinematics topics with an emphasis in geometric reasoning, programming, and matrix computations. Motion planning includes configuration spaces, sensor-based planning, decomposition and sampling methods, and advanced planning algorithms. Kinematics includes reference frames, rotations and displacements, and kinematic motion models. Cross-listed with EE 145.
prerequisites_text: ME 120 or equivalent; or consent on instructor

subject: ME
title: Internal Combustion Engines
description: Covers engine types and their operation. Also addresses engine design and operating parameters, thermochemistry of fuel-air mixture, engine cycles, spark ignition and compressed ignition engines, and emissions. Credit is awarded for one of the following ME 148 or ME 248.
prerequisites_text: ME 100A; ME 113; ME 116A; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS) Technology
description: Covers the fundamentals of MEMS technology including MEMS device design, fabrication, and characterization. Provides hands-on experience in crafting real MEMS devices from initial design to the prototyping stage. Cross-listed with MSE 141.
prerequisites_text: MSE 001; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ME
title: Finite Element Methods
description: Covers weak form formulation, the Galerkin method and its computational implementation, mesh generation, data visualization, as well as programming finite element codes for practical engineering applications.
prerequisites_text: ME 118

subject: ME
title: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
description: Introduces the theory and experimental techniques for testing the mechanical behavior of materials and structures. Covers the fundamental mechanisms of deformation and failure of metals, ceramics, polymers, composite materials, and electronic materials as well as structural design and materials selection.
prerequisites_text: MSE 002A, MSE 002B, MSE 002C or ME 114; ME 110 or MSE 110; restricted to class level standing of senior

subject: ME
title: Failure Analysis and Prevention
description: Topics include failure modes due to overload, fatigue, fracture, and creep. Also addresses statistical analysis, probability of failure, quality assurance, and elements of fracture mechanics. Cross-listed with MSE 143. Credit is awarded for one of the following ME 157, MSE 143, or MSE 233B.
prerequisites_text: ME 114 with a grade of C or better; restricted to class level standing of senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ME
title: Advanced Solidification Processing
description: An overview of the fundamentals of solidification processing. Includes integrated interplay of heat flow, mass transport, and solid/liquid interfacial kinetics during discontinuous change of state from liquid to solid of single phase and polyphase materials. Cross-listed with MSE 148. Credit is awarded for one of the following MSE 148, ME 158, ME 279, or MSE 248C.
prerequisites_text: MSE 143 or ME 157; restricted to class level standing of senior; or consent of instructor

subject: ME
title: Experimental Techniques
description: Covers the principles and practice of measurement and control and the design and implementation of experiments. Topics include dimensional analysis, error analysis, signal-to-noise problems, filtering, data acquisition and data reduction, and statistical analysis. Includes experiments on the use of electronic devices and sensors and practice in technical report writing.
prerequisites_text: EE 005; ME 018B with a grade of C- or better

subject: ME
title: Experimental Techniques
description: Analysis and verification of engineering theory using laboratory measurements in advanced, project-oriented experiments. Involves fluid flow, heat transfer, structural dynamics, thermodynamic systems, and electromechanical systems.

subject: ME
title: Machine Design
description: An introduction to the fundamentals of strength-based design. Topics include deflection and stiffness, static failure, and fatigue failure.
prerequisites_text: ME 009, ME 103 (can be taken concurrently), ME 110, ME 114

subject: ME
title: Professional Topics in Engineering
description: Topics include technical communication, team work, project management, engineering economics, professional ethics, and computer-aided design. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available.
prerequisites_text: senior standing in Mechanical Engineering major; ME 009

subject: ME
title: Mechanical Engineering Design
description: Outlines the defining of a design problem and the conception and detail of the design solution. Explores design theory, design for safety, reliability, manufacture, and assembly. Graded In Progress (IP) until ME 175B and ME 175C are completed, at which time a final, letter grade is assigned.
prerequisites_text: senior standing in Mechanical Engineering. ME 113, ME 116A, ME 170A, ME 174, ME 175A (may be taken concurrently)

subject: ME
title: Mechanical Engineering Design
description: Students create, test, and evaluate a prototype based on the project design generated in ME 175B. Lecture topics include prototyping techniques, design verification, and special topics in design. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available.
prerequisites_text: senior standing in Mechanical Engineering; ME 175B

subject: ME
title: Technological Entrepreneurship
description: Introduces concepts of business and management required to convert a technology into a viable business. Topics include technological assessment, market analysis, strategy, decision making, legal and intellectual property issues in business, financial analysis, business ethics and communication. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available
prerequisites_text: senior standing in Mechanical Engineering

subject: ME
title: Sustainable Product Design
description: Introduces the principles of sustainable product design. Topics include life cycle design; design for reliability, maintainability, and recycling/reuse/remanufacture; materials selection; and manufacturing processes. Includes project in which students analyze the environmental impact of a product and redesign it to reduce the impact. Credit is awarded for only one of ME 176 or ME 210.

subject: ME
title: Optics and Lasers in Engineering
description: Introduces basic principles of optics and lasers, wave equations, interferometry, diffraction, Fourier optics, light-matter interactions, ultrafast and nonlinear optics, and nanophotonics. Frames introductory concepts with experimental design and computer analysis. Includes applications and analytical exercises with microscopy and spectroscopy, smart-phone camera hacks, thin-film and bulk materials characterization, and communication systems. Credit is awarded for one of the following ME 180 or ME 280.
prerequisites_text: EE 005, MATH 010B; or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: ME
title: Special Studies
description: Individual study to meet special curricular needs. Requires a final written report. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 9 units.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor, department chair, and Mechanical Engineering Undergraduate Program Committee chair

subject: ME
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: Directed research in a particular subject relevant to mechanical engineering. Requires a final written technical report. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and Mechanical Engineering Undergraduate Program Committee chair

subject: ME
title: R’course: Variable Topics
description: An opportunity for UCR undergraduate students to develop leadership skills, innovate the undergraduate curriculum, and promote democratic, experiential education. Original course topics are variable and unique from other departmental course offerings, designed to highlight the student facilitators’ expertise while working closely with a faculty mentor. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: permission needed from department; sophomore standing or better

subject: MEIS
title: Islam and Feminism
description: Focuses on the intersections between Islam and feminism. Topics include feminist interpretations of the Qur’an, Muslim women’s movements and activisms in Islamic and non-Islamic societies, and the complex interactions between the nation-state, religion, gender, and sexuality. Cross-listed with GSST 012, and RLST 011. Credit is awarded for one of the following RLST 011, GSST 012, MEIS 012, GSST 012H, MEIS 012H, or RLST 011H.

subject: MEIS
title: Honors Islam and Feminism
description: Honors course corresponding to MEIS 012. Focuses on the intersections between Islam and feminism. Topics include feminist interpretations of the Qur’an, Muslim women’s movements and activisms in Islamic and non-Islamic societies, and the complex interactions between the nation-state, religion, gender, and sexuality. Cross-listed with GSST 012H, and RLST 011H. Credit is awarded for one of the following RLST 011H, GSST 012H, MEIS 012H, GSST 012, MEIS 012, or RLST 011.

subject: MEIS
title: Gender, Sexuality, and Islam
description: Focuses on the intersections between gender, sexuality, and religion in Islamicate societies. Discusses the ways in which those formations have been shaped by histories of slavery, imperialism, colonialism, human rights discourses, neoliberalism, contemporary practices of Islamophobia, nationalism, and global LGBTQ activism. Cross-listed with GSST 110, and RLST 105.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior

subject: MEIS
title: The Postclassical Maghreb
description: A study of ancient Mediterranean influences on modern North Africa. Emphasizes 19th and 20th century colonial and postcolonial literature, art, and cinema from Algeria, Morocco, Libya, and Tunisia. Engages extensively with Greek, Roman, and Punic sources from classical antiquity. Cross-listed with CLA 150, CPAC 150, and CPLT 150.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MEIS
title: Palestine/Algeria
description: Considers two distinct and related literary and historical moments: Palestine and Algeria. Topics include the relations between language and context; literature and literary historiography; genre and idiom; violence and the body; and the state and institutional practices of reading. Cross-listed with ARLC 151, and CPLT 151.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MEIS
title: Introduction to Arabic Literature
description: An introduction to Arabic literature that focuses on language and rhetoric. Considers major issues such as colonialism, secularism, modernity, language, and the state. Utilizes texts from literature, law, and philosophy. Cross-listed with ARLC 155, and CPLT 155.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MEIS
title: Jews and Arabs
description: Traces the formation of the shared and divided history of the Jewish and Arab peoples. Focuses on the literary and institutional dimensions of this history, as well as the formation of related areas of study, such as religion, philosophy, literature, and psychoanalysis. Cross-listed with ARLC 156, CPLT 156, and RLST 156.

subject: MEIS
title: Senior Research
description: Directed original research in topics related to the Middle East, Islamic studies, or Islamic cultures. Administered under the direction of members of the Middle East and Islamic Studies Steering Committee or an approved faculty member. . Graduate Course
prerequisites_text: senior standing; consent of Middle East and Islamic Studies Steering Committee chair

subject: MHHS
title: Introduction to Medical and Health Humanities
description: Introduces medical and health humanities. Explores the importance of humanities and arts to medicine, the diverse understandings of health and illness, and the complex social and economic forces that inform how people are cared for during times of illness. Mandatory course in the Medical and Health Humanities minor.

subject: MHHS
title: Meditation as Medicine: A Critical Exploration
description: A critical exploration of the transformation of Buddhist meditation traditions over the last twenty-five centuries. Addresses the foundational techniques and debates in India; mass meditation as colonial resistance in Burma; recent interest in the brain sciences; and the commodification of mindfulness, compassion, and selflessness in the neoliberal marketplace. Cross-listed with AST 117, and RLST 119.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MHHS
title: The Buddha’s Brain: Mind, Reality, and Power in the Buddhism-Science Dialogue
description: A critical history of the “Buddhism-Science dialogue.” Focuses on contested characterizations of mind, brain, and personhood. Includes reading and analyzing primary sources in the Indo-Tibetan Buddhist tradition alongside the brain sciences. Prepares for advanced courses and research in religious studies, the medical humanities, and Asian studies. Cross-listed with AST 131, and RLST 131.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MHHS
title: Seminar in Medical and Health Humanities
description: Examines selected topics in the medical and health humanities from religion, anthropology, literature or history to creative arts. Analyzes the role of humanities in medicine. Develops skill sets through seminars with medical humanities experts. Mandatory course in the Medical and Health Humanities minor. Medicine
prerequisites_text: MHHS 001 with a grade of C- or better

subject: MSE
title: Introduction to Materials Science and Engineering
description: Covers the historic origins of Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) as well as its role in the modern society and among modern subjects. Provides general overview for typical career paths as well as roles and responsibilities of MSE graduates in various positions with cross references to the current MSE curriculum. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).

subject: MSE
title: Fundamentals of Materials Science and Engineering
description: Covers fundamental topics in materials science and engineering, such as materials classification, atomic structure, and interatomic bonding, crystal structures and elements of crystallography, diffusion and mechanical behavior. The laboratory hands on experience complements topics covered during the lectures. Credit is awarded for one of the following MSE 002A or MSE 002L.
prerequisites_text: MSE 001

subject: MSE
title: Fundamentals of Materials Science and Engineering
description: Covers fundamental topics in materials science and engineering such as phase binary and ternary phase diagrams; phase transformations; applications and processing of metal alloys, structures, properties; and processing of ceramic materials, polymers, and characterization techniques. The laboratory hands on experience complements topics covered during the lectures. Credit is awarded for one of the following MSE 002B or MSE 003L.
prerequisites_text: MSE 001

subject: MSE
title: Fundamentals of Materials Science and Engineering
description: Covers fundamental topics in materials science and engineering, such as composite materials, corrosion and degradation, electrical, thermal, magnetic and optical properties of materials as well as environmental, economic and ethical aspects. The laboratory hands on experience complements topics covered during the lectures. Credit is awarded for one of the following MSE 002C or MSE 004L.
prerequisites_text: MSE 001

subject: MSE
title: General Materials Laboratory Spring
description: Provides hands-on laboratory experience in topics related to the Structure-Composition-Processing-Performance relationship of ceramics, electronic materials, metals, and polymers. Experiments cover mechanical testing and properties of different materials classes and introduce students to microscopic characterization techniques. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: MSE 001 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to major(s) Materials Science and Engineer; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: General Materials Laboratory Fall
description: Provides hands-on laboratory experience in topics related to the Structure-Composition-Processing-Performance relationship of ceramics, electronic materials, metals, and polymers. Experiments cover materials processing and failure modes of different materials classes. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: MSE 001 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to major(s) Materials Science and Engineer; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: General Materials Laboratory Winter
description: Provides hands-on laboratory experience in topics related to the Structure-Composition-Processing-Performance relationship of ceramics, electronic materials, metals, and polymers. Experiments cover electrical, thermal, optical, and magnetic properties. Introduces composites and the factors that affect its properties and mechanical performance. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: MSE 001 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to major(s) Materials Science and Engineer; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Materials Thermodynamics
description: An introduction to classical and statistical thermodynamics principles of interest to materials scientists and engineering. Explore criteria for equilibrium, reaction and phase equilibria, equations of state, and phase diagrams. Includes applications of thermodynamics in materials processing and phase stability.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A, PHYS 040B or PHYS 040HB; restricted to class level standing of junior, senior, or masters; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Statics & Mechanics of Materials
description: Covers basic principles of statics including equilibrium equations and free body diagrams, axial loading, torsion and shear forces, and stresses analysis and principal stresses. Also addresses column stability analysis and buckling as well as practical implications to materials science and engineering problems.
prerequisites_text: MATH 009C, PHYS 040A or PHYS 040HA

subject: MSE
title: Transport Phenomena in Materials Science and Engineering
description: Covers fundamental aspects of heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation as well as mass transfer by diffusion. Provides introduction to internal and external flows including laminar and turbulent conditions and boundary layer problems as well as coverage for boiling and condensation.
prerequisites_text: MSE 100

subject: MSE
title: Microstructural Transformations in Materials
