description: An introductory study of the fundamentals (thermodynamics and kinetics) controlling microstructural transformations in materials and their application to both liquid-solid and solid-solid transformations. Focuses on the important transformations that ultimately control the microstructures and properties of crystalline solids. Cross-listed with ME 134.
prerequisites_text: ME 114 or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Introduction to Inorganic Material Synthesis
description: Introduction to the synthesis methods of modern materials. Topics include solid-state reactions, gas-phase and solution-phase synthesis, templating methods, synthesis and modification of inorganic polymers, semiconductor thin-film deposition, and the growth of nanomaterials.
prerequisites_text: CHEM 008A or CHEM 08HA; PHYS 040C or PHYS 040HC; MSE 100 or CHE 100; ME 114 or MSE 002A, MSE 002B, MSE 002C or CHEM 008B; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Tissue Engineering
description: Covers progress in cellular and molecular biology and engineering. Provides the basis for advancing tissue repair and regeneration with the goal of restoring compromised tissue functions. Presents methods for cell culture, tissue design and development, manipulation of the cell/tissue microenvironment, and current strategies for functional reconstruction of injured tissues. Cross-listed with BIEN 136.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005B; CHEM 001C or CHEM 01HC; BIEN 140A or CEE 140A; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS) Technology
description: Covers the fundamentals of MEMS technology including MEMS device design, fabrication, and characterization. Provides hands-on experience in crafting real MEMS devices from initial design to the prototyping stage. Cross-listed with ME 151.
prerequisites_text: MSE 001; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Corrosion Science
description: Introduces the principles of corrosion in metals and alloys. Discusses the relevant elements of electrochemistry, electrochemical corrosion, thermodynamics, and the kinetic aspects of corrosion. Includes projects that provide practical hands-on experience using state-of-the-art computational techniques in materials science. Credit is awarded for one of the following MSE 142 or MSE 233A.
prerequisites_text: MSE 134; restricted to class level standing of senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Failure Analysis and Prevention
description: Topics include failure modes due to overload, fatigue, fracture, and creep. Also addresses statistical analysis, probability of failure, quality assurance, and elements of fracture mechanics. Cross-listed with ME 157. Credit is awarded for one of the following ME 157, MSE 143, or MSE 233B.
prerequisites_text: ME 114 with a grade of C or better; restricted to class level standing of senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Metallurgical Processing
description: Covers traditional and modern metallurgical processing techniques such as refining, melting, casting, forging, rolling, welding, soldering, heat treatment, and powder processing including additive manufacturing approaches. Also covers physical principles, processing details and processing equipment, and common applications.
prerequisites_text: ME 114 with a grade of C- or better or MSE 002A with a grade of C- or better; MSE 002B with a grade of C- or better; MSE 002C with a grade of C- or better

subject: MSE
title: Advanced Solidification Processing
description: An overview of the fundamentals of solidification processing. Includes integrated interplay of heat flow, mass transport, and solid/liquid interfacial kinetics during discontinuous change of state from liquid to solid of single phase and polyphase materials. Cross-listed with ME 158. Credit is awarded for one of the following MSE 148, ME 158, ME 279, or MSE 248C.
prerequisites_text: MSE 143 or ME 157; restricted to class level standing of senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Materials Science of the Solid State
description: Explores at an advanced level the quantum mechanical behavior of electron motion and atom vibration in a periodic solid and their effect on the electronic and thermal properties of matter. The course discusses modern materials science research problems. Credit is awarded for one of the following MSE 155 or MSE 211.
prerequisites_text: EE 138

subject: MSE
title: Atomistic Modeling of Solid State Materials
description: Introduces a basic understanding of computational methods in materials science. Emphasizes the fundamentals of density functional theory and its use in the solid-state context. Includes projects that provide practical hands-on experience using state-of-the-art computational techniques in materials science. Credit is awarded for one of the following MSE 156 or MSE 224.
prerequisites_text: MSE 155; restricted to class level standing of senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MSE
title: Nanostructure Characterization Laboratory
description: Covers structure of materials at the nanoscale, including semiconductors, ceramics, metals, and carbon nanotubes. Explores relationships among morphology, properties, and processing. Addresses primary methods of characterization, including scanning electron microscopy, scanning probe microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and transmission electron microscopy. Also covers elementary discussions of X-ray, vibrational, and electron waves in solids and introductory diffraction theory.
prerequisites_text: ME 114

subject: MSE
title: Analytical Materials Characterization
description: Analysis of the surfaces of materials via ion, electron, and photon spectroscopies. Covers Rutherford back scattering; secondary ion mass spectroscopy; electron energy loss spectroscopy; Auger electron spectroscopy; X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy; photoluminescence; extended X-ray absorption fine structure; Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy; Raman spectroscopy; sputtering; high-vacuum generation; and focused ion beam milling. Cross-listed with EE 161.
prerequisites_text: MSE 160

subject: MSE
title: Senior Design
description: Covers preparation of formal engineering reports and statistical analysis on series of problems illustrating methodology from various branches of applied MSE. Addresses the following design process elements; problem definition; generation specification; documentation; review process; prototype fabrication; testing and calibration; cost estimation; and federal guidelines. Term project and oral presentation required. Graded In-Progress (IP) until MSE 175A and MSE 175B are completed, at which time a final, letter grade is assigned.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of senior; restricted to major(s) Materials Science and Engineer

subject: MSE
title: Senior Design
description: Covers preparation of formal engineering reports and statistical analysis on a series of problems illustrating methodology from various branches of applied materials science and engineering. Addresses the entire design process: design problem definition; generation of a design specification; documentation; design review process; prototype fabrication; testing and calibration; cost estimation; and federal guidelines. Requires a term project and oral presentation. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available.
prerequisites_text: MSE 175A; senior standing in Materials Science and Engineering

subject: MSE
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: Research conducted under the supervision of a MSE faculty member on selected problems in materials science and engineering supporting the focus area of the student. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units; maximum of 4 units may count toward the technical elective requirement.
prerequisites_text: sophomore or junior or senior standing in Materials Science and Engineering or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Basic Musical Concepts
description: Covers the fundamentals of music including notations, rhythm, major and minor scales, intervals, tonality, and triads. Includes ear training, sight singing, and elementary analysis. Musical literacy not required. To be taken during freshman year in preparation for the Music Major.

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Western Music
description: A survey of the major styles and genres of Western music. Emphasis on creative and analytical listening without the use of musical notation. Designed for the general student with an interest in music and cultural practice. No previous musical background required.

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Opera
description: Explores social, political, gender-related, and moral issues represented in 10 major operas between the seventeenth and twentieth centuries. Introduces dramatic and musical structures of opera, value of performance, and operatic conventions shared by composers, singers, and audience.

subject: MUS
title: Women in Music
description: A survey course designed primarily for nonmajors. Examines representative works by women composers from antiquity to the present.

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to World Music
description: A survey of people, identity, and music making. Includes listening to music from many cultural contexts. Also covers a variety of scholarly topics in world music. Cross-listed with ANTH 006.

subject: MUS
title: Music in Movies and Tv
description: An exploration of popular film and TV soundtrack music, emphasizing drama and musical style. Scene study features such films as The Matrix, Casablanca, The X-Files, and Altered States. Cross-listed with MCS 009.

subject: MUS
title: Popular Music Cultures of the United States
description: Explores the so-called popular musics and music cultures of the United States and the social history of these cultures to provide students with a sonic understanding of these extremely fractured, ever reconstituted “United States.”

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Digital Music
description: Teaches basic theory and practical skills for understanding digital audio, recording, editing, and processing sound. Includes work with audio and MIDI sequencers with the goal of writing musical compositions with computer notation programs.

subject: MUS
title: Advanced Fundamentals
description: Advanced study of musical notation, meter and rhythm. Includes major and minor scales, keys, tonal functions, compound meter, and mixed meter. Also provides training in sight singing, interval recognition, and chord quality identification for triads and seventh chords. To be taken during freshman year in preparation for the Music Major.
prerequisites_text: MUS 001; or a passing score on a diagnostic examination and consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Music and Culture
description: Introduces methods and develops skills for understanding music in society. Includes an overview of music’s social roles, including personal identity, nationalism, and political movements. Students listen to music of multiple genres and geocultural areas, participate in activities and workshops, and develop writing skills to describe and analyze musical practices.

subject: MUS
title: Popular Musics of the World
description: Introduction to issues surrounding popular and urban musics of the world focusing on three major geocultural areas: Africa, Asia, and the Americas. Emphasizes the relationship between mass-mediated music and issues of cultural hegemony, resistance, and subversion. Analyzes the cultural impact of media technology on music performance and reception. Cross-listed with ETST 014, and URST 014.

subject: MUS
title: Latin American Folk and Popular Styles
description: assigned listening, 3 hours. Introduction to the vast array of folk and popular styles of music in Latin America, with an emphasis on cultural and ethnic interaction and exchange in the context of Latin American history, politics, and society. Cross-listed with LNST 015.

subject: MUS
title: Latin American Classical Heritage
description: assigned listening, 3 hours. Survey of the rich heritage of Latin American classical music from Renaissance sacred polyphony to contemporary styles. Emphasis on the gradual emergence of Latin American music from European domination and the establishment of distinctive national traditions in the post-colonial era. Cross-listed with LNST 016.

subject: MUS
title: Music of Mexico
description: Covers music from 1521 to the present day. Explores the rich musical tradition of Mexico, as well as the relationship between its art and popular music. Cross-listed with LNST 017.
prerequisites_text: musical training and knowledge of Spanish is useful, but not required

subject: MUS
title: Music of Spain
description: A survey of Spanish music from the Middle Ages to the present. Covers regional folklore and popular styles (especially flamenco) as well as developments in classical music through the major style periods. Examines music in its historical and cultural context. Knowledge of Spanish and music not required.

subject: MUS
title: Music of Brazil
description: An exploration of Brazilian music from nineteenth to early twentieth-first centuries with an emphasis on traditional and popular practices and styles. Discusses the music of different regions and periods in their social, political, ethnic, and aesthetic contexts. Credit is awarded for only one of MUS 019 or MUS 113.

subject: MUS
title: Music of Scotland
description: Examines the rich heritage of Scottish music from the Middle Ages to the modern day, including folk, popular, and classical traditions. Emphasis is on the music of the Scottish highlands and the bagpipe. Explores the role of music during war and peace within the context of Scottish history.

subject: MUS
title: Canntaireachd: Scottish Classical Music
description: Examines the Scottish classical music called Canntaireachd. In-depth study of the music, its leading performers and composers, within the context of Scottish history and culture. Special emphasis on the singing of the music as soloists and as a choir.

subject: MUS
title: Audio Recording and Production
description: Introduces the fundamentals of audio recording. Includes basic design and uses of a recording studio, digital audio workstations, and microphones, as well as recording, processing, and mixing techniques. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.

subject: MUS
title: Global Hip Hop: Rap Cultures Around the World
description: An introduction to the history and contemporary practice of hip hop music and culture around the world. Emphasizes the role of hip hop in the formation of identity including race, ethnicity, gender, and sexuality, as well as the politics of language, localization and globalization, and political activism.

subject: MUS
title: Art of the Synthesizer
description: Explores the history of synthesizers through the stories of pioneering electronic musicians. Introduces the concepts of modular synthesis through applied patch designs with virtual software. Cross-listed with MCS 026.

subject: MUS
title: Harmony
description: First of a three-quarter long study of harmony. Includes diatonic primary and secondary chords in root position and inversions, four-part vocal writing, melodic harmonization, and introduction to non-chord tones. Highly recommended to complete this requirement during sophomore year. Open to non-majors with consent of instructor.
prerequisites_text: MUS 010; or a passing score on a diagnostic examination. MUS majors are required to concurrently enroll in MUS 031A; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Harmony
description: Second of a three-quarter long study of harmony; diatonic chords and non-chord tones followed by diatonic seventh chords. Begins the study of chromatic harmony with secondary dominants. Highly recommended to complete this requirement during sophomore year. Open to non-majors with consent of instructor.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030A; Music majors are required to concurrently enroll in MUS 031B; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Harmony
description: Last course of a three-quarter long study of harmony. Includes chromaticism associated with secondary dominants followed by secondary leading tone chords, the Neapolitan chord and augmented sixth chords, and modulations. Highly recommended to complete this requirement during sophomore year. Open to non-majors with consent of instructor.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030B; MUS majors are required to concurrently enroll in MUS 031C; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Music Theory and Musicianship I
description: First of a three quarter-long applied skill-based course integrating concepts learned while concurrently enrolled in MUS 030A. Involves basic sight singing, rhythmic reading, melodic and harmonic dictation, and keyboard harmony. Highly recommended to complete this requirement during sophomore year.
prerequisites_text: MUS 010; or a passing score on a diagnostic examination. MUS majors are required to concurrently enroll in MUS 030A; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Music Theory and Musicianship I
description: Second of a three-quarter-long applied skills-based course integrating concepts from MUS 030B. Addresses application of non-chord tones to existing melodies and melodic dictation above a harmonic sequence going diatonic triads to diatonic seventh chords and secondary functional chords. Recommended to complete this requirement during sophomore year.
prerequisites_text: MUS 031A; Music majors are required to concurrently enroll in MUS 030B; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Music Theory and Musicianship I
description: Third of a three-quarter long applied skills-based course integrating concepts learned while concurrently enrolled in MUS 030C. Covers sight singing, harmonic diction, and melodic dictation with secondary leading-tone, Neapolitan, and augmented-sixth chords. Highly recommended to complete this requirement during sophomore year.
prerequisites_text: MUS 031B; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Class Piano
description: Develops fundamental skills in piano performance for beginning players. Topics include sight reading, scales, basic improvisation, harmonization, transposition, and repertoire studies. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: MUS 010; or consent of the instructor following the piano diagnostic exam.; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Class Piano
description: Second of a two-quarter sequence to develop fundamental skills in piano performance. Topics include sight reading, scales, improvisation, harmonization, transposition, and repertoire studies. Successful completion fulfills the Department of Music’s piano proficiency requirement for music majors. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: MUS 032A; or consent of the instructor following the piano diagnostic exam; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Composition
description: Introduces the art of music composition through applied exercises. Covers basic computer music notation. Course is a prerequisite for Music Majors in the Composition Track.
prerequisites_text: MUS 001, MUS 010, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Introduction to Songwriting
description: Explores fundamentals of songwriting from writing lyrics to finding a structure. Focuses on analyzing several songs and techniques from various time periods and creating model exercises.

subject: MUS
title: Dance of Mexico
description: Covers the traditional dances of Mexico at the beginning level. Includes attendance at dance concerts outside of class. Recommended for both nondancers and dancers. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with LNST 073A.

subject: MUS
title: Dance of Mexico
description: Covers the traditional dances of Mexico at the beginning level. Includes attendance at dance concerts outside of class. Recommended for both nondancers and dancers. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with LNST 073B.
prerequisites_text: LNST 073A/MUS 073A is recommended

subject: MUS
title: (E-Z) Private Instruction: Voice, Keyboard, and Strings
description: Consists of a half-hour lesson and practice for 5 to 10 hours each week (see the note regarding fees under the Major Requirements section). Offered as demand indicates. E. Voice; F. Classical Piano; G. Jazz Piano; I. Harpsichord; J. Carillon; K. Jazz Guitar; L. Electronic Bass Guitar; M. Lute; N. Classical Guitar; O. Viola Da Gamba; P. Piano Proficiency; Q. Organ; R. Violin; S. Viola; T. Violoncello; U. Double Bass Viol; V. Harp. Course is repeatable to a maximum of units.

subject: MUS
title: (E-Z) Private Instruction: Brass, Woodwinds, Percussion, and Other Instruments
description: Consists of a half-hour lesson and practice for 5 to 10 hours each week (see the note regarding fees under the Major Requirements section). Offered as demand indicates. E. Trumpet; F. Trombone; G. Tuba; I. French Horn; J. Flute; K. Oboe; L. Clarinet; M. Bassoon; N. Saxophone; O. Recorder; P. Percussion; R. Bagpipe; S. Scottish Drums; Z. Caribbean Steele Pan. Course is repeatable.

subject: MUS
title: Music Resources and References
description: Introduces the methods of finding and using music resources and references. Explores the musical resources of the UCR libraries and beyond. Topics include but are not limited to UCR’s music collections (print, online, and audio formats) including scores, databases, reference sources, journals, and multimedia.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor and/or successful completion of one or more introductory course(s) in the discipline

subject: MUS
title: History of Western Music: Middle Ages to 1700
description: An intensive survey of music history and literature from the Middle Ages to 1700. Involves score reading, listening, and analysis of pieces with emphasis on historical characteristics.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030A, MUS 030B, MUS 030C; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: History of Western Music: 1700- 1900
description: An intensive survey of music history and literature from the 1700 to 1900. Involves score reading, listening, and analysis of pieces with emphasis on historical characteristics.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030A, MUS 030B, MUS 030C; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: History of Western Music: Twentieth-Century
description: An intensive survey of music history and literature from 1900 to the present. Involves score reading, listening, and analysis of pieces with emphasis on historical characteristics.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030A, MUS 030B, MUS 030C; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Brazilian Music
description: Introduces the music of Brazil, focusing on the history and the current variety of musical languages, styles, and forms of the present. Analyzes the crucial question of national identity in Brazilian culture and society through the study of its music.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Opera
description: Study of selected operas from the Western repertory for 1600 to the present.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Renaissance and Baroque Music of Latin Europe and Latin America
description: Study of the sacred and secular musics of Italy, France, the Iberian Peninsula, and Latin America, 1450-1750. Emphasis is on the repertoires, styles, and genres that are relevant to understanding the musical past of the Americas, from (Alta) California to South America.
prerequisites_text: MUS 112A, MUS 112B, MUS 112C; or upper-division standing and consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: History of Jazz
description: An overview of the history of jazz music emphasizing its development in the United States from the nineteenth century to the present. Topics include jazz’ origins in southern African American musical practices, the blues, swing, bebop, cool jazz, Latin jazz, and the genre’s contemporary internationalization.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, senior, credential only, or masters; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Music and Ritual
description: Examines music cross-culturally in a ritual context. Incorporates readings from ethnomusicology, anthropology, folklore, and performance studies. Addresses how music operates within specific ritual events and how it relates to cosmology. Also examines the role of music in achieving altered states (dreams, meditation, trance, and possession), as well as helping to constitute gendered authority.

subject: MUS
title: Music, Politics, and Social Movements
description: Examines the role of music in social and political movements. Emphasis is on understanding the textual and musical features of politically engaged music within its historical, social, and cultural context.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Javanese Music and Culture
description: Examines Javanese traditional and contemporary music. Focuses on the music of the Javanese gamelan and its relation to larger cosmological themes. Other topics include rural versus court traditions, popular music, mass media, piracy, Hindu roots, modernity, and local practices versus global trends. Cross-listed with AST 119.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Contemporary Native American Music
description: Explores the music of Native American peoples today, the contexts and behaviors with which such music is associated, and the ways these elements are discussed within Native communities. Emphasis is on “Pan Indian” music, including music for pow wows and syncretic religious music, and Native popular music, including folk, country, rock, and hip-hop.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Why Music Matters: Sound, Culture, and Everyday Life
description: Explores how music shapes identity and how people connect to the world around them through sound. Through listening, reading, discussion, and creative projects, examines how music reflects social movements, expresses belonging, and creates change.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: MUS
title: Music and Performance in the Andes
description: Introduction to the musical practices of the central Andean countries, including indigenous, mestizo, Creole, and Afro-Andean traditions. Music is presented as part of a broader realm of performance in the Andes, incorporating dance, ritual, drama, and popular culture, and its relationship with notions of identity, nationalism, modernity, folklore, and politics.

subject: MUS
title: Southeast Asian Performance
description: Introduction to the roles and genres of expressive culture in Southeast Asia, including dance, music, theater, film, and digital culture. Performance is discussed as both a time-honored and a contemporary medium for cultural production, from the courts to everyday experience. Cross-listed with AST 123, ANTH 126, DNCE 123, and SEAS 123.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Music of Asian America
description: Explores music as a window on the cultural politics of Asian America. Examines expressive culture as a constitutive site for ethnic identities and emergent political formations. Covers music of Asian immigrants and of subsequent generations, including Asian American jazz and hip-hop. Cross-listed with AST 124.

subject: MUS
title: Music of Central America, Mexico, and the Caribbean
description: A survey of different musical traditions from Central America, Mexico, and the Caribbean, with an emphasis on popular music. Examines the impact of intercultural contact on the musical styles of these regions. A background in Western music is not required.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Gender, Sexuality, and Music in Cross-Cultural Perspectives
description: An overview of gendered performance genres from a number of cultures. Explores gender-specific music and notions of gender that are often constructed, maintained, transmitted, and transformed through music and performance. Cross-listed with ANTH 177, and GSST 126.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Music Cultures of Southeast Asia
description: A survey of music, dance, theatre, and ritual in the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Myanmar (Burma), Laos, Cambodia, and Vietnam. Designed for the student interested in the performing arts and cultures of mainland and insular Southeast Asia. No Western music background is required. Cross-listed with ANTH 176, AST 127, DNCE 127, ETST 172, and SEAS 127.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Counterpoint
description: A study of techniques of composing simultaneous, independent melodic lines within selected harmonic and stylistic contexts. Includes but is not limited to sixteenth-century counterpoint. To be taken during junior year.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030C, MUS 031C; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Counterpoint
description: A study of advanced techniques of composing simultaneous, independent melodic lines within selected harmonic and stylistic contexts. Includes but is not limited to eighteenth-century counterpoint. To be taken during junior year.
prerequisites_text: MUS 130A; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Music Theory and Musicianship 2
description: Study and practice of music theory. Includes advanced ear training, sight singing, melodic and harmonic dictation, rhythmic skills, keyboard skills, twentieth-century harmony, twelve-tone serialism, atonalism, and electronic and computer music.
prerequisites_text: MUS 031C

subject: MUS
title: Music Theory and Musicianship 2
description: Study and practice of music theory. Includes advanced ear training, sight singing, melodic and harmonic dictation, rhythmic skills, keyboard skills, twentieth-century harmony, twelve-tone serialism, atonalism, and electronic and computer music.
prerequisites_text: MUS 131A

subject: MUS
title: Music Theory and Musicianship 2
description: Study and practice of music theory. Includes advanced ear training, sight singing, melodic and harmonic dictation, rhythmic skills, keyboard skills, twentieth-century harmony, twelve-tone serialism, atonalism, and electronic and computer music.
prerequisites_text: MUS 131B

subject: MUS
title: Instrumentation
description: Investigation of the technical and color possibilities of various instruments, with scoring projects.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030A, MUS 030B, MUS 030C; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Orchestration
description: Advanced scoring projects with emphasis on stylistic aspects and relationship of orchestral color to form.
prerequisites_text: MUS 010; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Jazz Theory
description: Examines concepts and practices in harmony, melody, rhythm, and form as they relate to jazz and other popular idioms. Provides basic ear training for the recognition of changes in traditional jazz tunes, primary blues forms, modulations, and classic jazz bridges.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030A; MUS 031A or MUS 031B or MUS 031C; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Composition Seminar
description: Assists in the successful composition of pieces in a variety of genres and media. Includes compositional models and the creation of musical scores. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030A, MUS 030B, MUS 030C; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Form and Analysis in Western Music
description: Studies the dynamic design produced by musical elements functioning in context and their significance in shaping music. Explores different approaches to analysis using works in contrasting styles and forms and through practical application of course material.
prerequisites_text: MUS 030C, MUS 031C; strongly recommend music majors complete this course during their junior year, or first-quarter available upon transferring; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: American Musical Subcultures: A Genealogy of Rock
description: A historical and cultural overview of the genre of American popular music known as “rock.” Covers themes ranging from musical form and structure, aesthetics, and audio technology to community and individualism, gender and racial identity, political resistance, and the music industry. Cross-listed with HISA 139.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: American Musical Subcultures: A Genealogy of Rock Practicum
description: A historical and cultural overview of the genre of American popular music known as “rock.” Covers themes ranging from musical form and structure, aesthetics, and audio technology to community and individualism, gender and racial identity, political resistance, and the music industry.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; requires concurrent enrollment in 080E, 080G, 080M, 080K, 081P or 180E, 180G, 180M, 180K, 181P, or enrollment in instrument lessons on another rock instrument; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Film and Video Game Scoring
description: An introduction to scoring films and video games. Explores instrumentation, drama, orchestration, and new technologies in a multimedia context. Discusses approaches to storytelling in virtual, digital, and cinematic art forms.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Digital Audio and Sound
description: College math is recommended. An introduction to the theory and practice of manipulating digital sound. Provides an understanding of digital audio devices associated with media production and of audio processing in general. Topics include basic psychoacoustics, digital audio theory, and digital audio editing.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Digital Audio and Sound
description: Advanced theory and practice of manipulating digital sound. Includes sound processing, synthesis, and composition, as well as multimedia and audiovisual composition and interactive media production. Provides an understanding of dedicated software for sound, music, and multimedia, including the programming environment Max/MSP. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.

subject: MUS
title: Genealogy of Electronica
description: Examines the history of electronica and electronic music. Focuses on particular issues, including youth culture, dance and ecstatic trance, subcultures and club cultures, hallucinogenic drugs and psychedelic aesthetics, globalization, audio piracy, media and audio technologies, music and politics, and gender and sexuality.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Advanced Contemporary Analysis: Music After 1945
description: A study of the diverse range of styles and movements of Western art music from 1945 through the present. Examines critical repertoire through a historical context including issues of pitch derivation, formal architecture, and compositional aesthetics. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available.
prerequisites_text: MUS 138 or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Sound Studies and Sound Art
description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary field of sound studies and sound art. Explores cultural, social, political, and philosophical issues of sound, listening, and auditory media. Examines the contemporary practices of sound production including the experimental field of sound art. Cross-listed with GBST 148.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Composition Forum and Studio
description: Individual or group lessons featuring applied composition exercises and listening assignments in various styles. Students share works in progress and attend guest lectures during a weekly forum. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: MUS 037; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; open to Music Majors in the Composition Track; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Instrumental Technique: Strings
description: Study of basic techniques of orchestral string instruments.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Instrumental Technique: Woodwinds
description: Study of basic techniques of orchestral woodwind instruments.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Instrumental Technique: Brass
description: Study of basic techniques of orchestral brass instruments.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Instrumental Technique: Percussion
description: Study of basic techniques of orchestral percussion instruments.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Instrumental Technique: Voice Studio
description: An introduction to performance that provides singers an opportunity to present and perform the material on which they are currently working. Also reviews the International Phonetic Alphabet and how it may be applied to improve a singer’s pronunciation and understandability by an audience. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 4 units.
prerequisites_text: MUS 080E and MUS 180E

subject: MUS
title: Orchestral Conducting
description: Fundamentals of baton technique, score study, transposition, and stylistic analysis as they relate to problems of conducting.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Choral Conducting
description: Study of choral repertoire, rehearsal methods, voice production, and techniques of conducting.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Queerness and Music (currently Titled “homosexuality and Music
description: Uses a topical rather than a chronological approach to investigate homosexuality on the part of composers, performers, critics, theorists, and historians and how this has shaped the history of music in the West.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: (E-Z) Critical Approaches to the Western Canon
description: Critical study of selected repertoires within Western music, and the multiple and potentially problematic aspects of their construction as iconic and paradigmatic. E. Beethoven: The Music &the Myth.
prerequisites_text: MUS 112A; MUS 112B; MUS 112C

subject: MUS
title: (E-Z) Seminar in Dance and Music
description: Introduces relationships and representations between music and dance. Explores musical and choreographic form, compositional strategies, hybridization of style, cultural meanings and registers in which these were made, the agencies such representations enabled, interpretive communities, and cross-cultural interactions. Cross-listed with DNCE 155 (E-Z).

subject: MUS
title: Representations of Spain in Dance and Music, 1700-2000
description: Introduces representations of Spain articulated in music and dance of Europe and the Americas from the eighteenth through twentieth centuries. Cross-listed with DNCE 155E.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: The Ballets Russes
description: Explores how the Diaghilev Ballets Russes’ repertoire and collaborative practices challenged the nature of artistic labor; negotiated traditional patronage and new commercial modes; engaged with cultural nationalism, gender role contention, and emerging models of sexuality; and deployed representational strategies that played into period debates about power and social organization. Cross-listed with DNCE 155F.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Topics Interdisciplinary Approaches to Composition
description: Examines interdisciplinary and critical approaches to composition (understood in a broad sense) that are not part of the regular curricular offerings. Course content varies and is announced as the course is offered. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Orchestra
description: Study and performance of standard orchestral literature. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Collegium Musicum
description: Study and performance of Medieval, Renaissance, and Baroque music. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: University of California, Riverside Chorale
description: Study and performance of standard choral literature. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 32 units.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Chamber Singers
description: Study and performance of works selected from different genres and periods. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Jazz Ensemble
description: Study and performance of literature for large jazz ensemble and stage band, and preparation of improvised solos. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Wind Ensemble
description: Study and performance of literature for the concert band. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: (E-Z) Chamber Music
description: Study and performance in varied small ensembles. E. Musical Instrument Digital Interface (midi) Ensemble; F. Improvisatory Ensemble; G. Chamber Music. Course is repeatable to a maximum of units.

subject: MUS
title: Senior Recital
description: Preparation and presentation of a formal recital. Limited to advanced performers only. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Javanese Gamelan Ensemble: Beginning
description: Study and performance of the Central Javanese gamelan, consisting mainly of gongs and gong-chime instruments. Readings and discussions focus on Javanese culture. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with AST 168 and SEAS 168
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Taiko Ensemble
description: Study and performance of Japanese drumming. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. Course is repeatable. Cross-listed with AST 169.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Rondalla Ensemble
description: Study and performance of the Filipino rondalla, an ensemble consisting of various sizes of lute-like and guitar-like instruments. Discussions focus on Filipino culture. Cross-listed with AST 170 and SEAS 170. Courses is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Latin American Music Ensemble
description: Study and performance of select Latin American folk music traditions, with special emphasis on music of the Andean region. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Beginning Mariachi Ensemble
description: A study and performance of selections from the Mexican folk music tradition. Emphasizes mariachi and son jarocho. Includes popular corridos and rancheras. Students who participate in a performance and submit a written review receive a letter grade; other students receive a Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grade. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Intermediate Mariachi Ensemble
description: A study and performance of selections from the Mexican folk music tradition. Emphasizes mariachi and son jarocho. Includes popular corridos and rancheras. Students who participate in a performance receive a letter grade; other students receive a Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grade. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: MUS 175A or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Bagpipe Ensemble
description: Study and performance of Scottish bagpipe music. Students who participate in a performance receive a letter grade; other students receive a Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grade. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Music of North India: Tabla (drums)
description: Explores the tradition of the Hindustani/North Indian tabla, which are a pair of drums that accompany improvised solos on melody instruments such as the sitar. Considers the tabla as a virtuosic solo instrument. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Music Improvisation Ensemble
description: Participation in an improvisational ensemble comprised of electronic (preferably laptop computer based) and/or electro-accoustical musical instruments. Rehearsals will cover a range of improvisational techniques from highly structured to free form and from tonality to noise experimentation. Normally graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC), but students may petition the instructor for a letter grade on the basis of assigned extra work or examination. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 24 units.
prerequisites_text: upper division standing and consent of instructor

title: (E-Z) Private Instruction: Voice, Keyboard, and Strings
description: Consists of an one-hour lesson and practice for 5 to 10 hours each week (see the note regarding fees under the Major Requirements section). Offered as demand indicates. E. Voice; F. subject: MUS
title: Percussion Ensemble
description: Study and performance of percussion ensemble literature. Course is repeatable..
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Genealogy of Hip Hop
description: Introduces hip hop culture from its origins to its contemporary global spread. Focuses particularly on rap music, addressing themes evoked in hip hop practice, particularly regionalism, feminism, gender identity, racialization, and globalization.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: MUS
title: Arts, Management, and Community
description: An introduction to business and arts management including the study of film and television production, stage management, and music production. Offers hands-on experience for practicing management skills working in partnership with local organizations and artists of Riverside and the Inland Empire. Cross-listed with TFDP 185. Credit is awarded for only one of MUS 185/TFDP 185 or MUS 185S/TFDP 185S.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor
