subject: PHIL
title: (E-Z) Topics in Hostory of Philosophy
description: Topics include E. Ancient Philosophy; F. Medieval Philosophy; I. French Renaissance Philosophy; J. Early Modern Philosophy; M. Moral Theories Of Hume And Kant; N. Nineteenth-century Philosophy; O. Kant And Post-kantian European Moral Philosophy; Q. Political Philosophy; R. Origins Of Analytical Philosophy.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N

subject: PHIL
title: Readings in Classical Chinese Philosophy
description: Introduces selections from key philosophical texts in classical Chinese. Focuses on a combination of Chinese reading and philosophical understanding. Cross-listed with CHN 106.
prerequisites_text: CHN 104 or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Formal Logic
description: An introduction to first-order logic, the core of the logic often used in contemporary philosophy, mathematics, computer science, and linguistics.
prerequisites_text: CS 011/ MATH 011 or CS 120A/EE 120A or CS 150 or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Intermediate Logic
description: The basic metatheory of first-order logic; with an emphasis on the precise relation between its syntax (formulas, rules of inference, and proofs) and semantics (interpretations, truth, validity), leading to the soundness and completeness theorems.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 124 or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Advanced Logic
description: Advanced metatheory of first-order logic, leading to a discussion of some of the important incompleteness, undecidability, and non-expressability results of twentieth-century logic. Includes the writings of Godel, Church, and Turing.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 124 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Advanced Topics in Logic
description: A study of selected non-truth-functional and nonstandard logics. Includes modal logics, tense logics, free logics, paraconsistent logics, and set theory. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 124 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to Arabic Philosophy
description: An introduction to Arabic philosophical texts. Provides close and literary reading of texts in philosophy, as well as considers the impact these texts have had or can have on Western cultural formation. Cross-listed with ARLC 154, and CPLT 154.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: History of Philosophy in India
description: An examination of the main philosophical themes, figures, and texts in premodern India. Pays particular attention to Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain philosophy. Cross-listed with AST 130, and RLST 129.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Theory of Knowledge
description: An inquiry into the nature of human knowledge its possibilities, criteria, scopes, and limitations.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Twentieth-Century Analytic Philosophy
description: A discussion of some major issues and thinkers in the tradition dominant in twentieth-century British and American philosophy. May include Frege, Russell, Carnap, Quine, Kripke, and D. Lewis.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Language
description: A study of some of the traditional issues in the philosophy of language, such as analyticity, theories of reference, truth, speech act theory, and philosophical theories of formal grammars.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Metaphysics
description: An investigation of some of the traditional problems in Western philosophy that have been labeled metaphysical. Addresses the existence of God, the relationship between mind and body, the determinism versus free will debate, and the nature of time and space.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Mind
description: A study of several theories of the nature of mind. Analyzes particular issues occasioned by these theories including the mind-body problem, personal identity, emotions, human action, self-knowledge, knowledge of other minds, and explanations of human behavior.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Psychology
description: Examines philosophical issues arising in the context of empirical psychology. Topics may include moral development, artificial intelligence and the modeling of cognition, the nature of perception and memory, fallacies in human reasoning, mechanisms of self-understanding, and mental illness and personhood.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Biology
description: Examines philosophical issues central to the life sciences. Topics include life, evolutionary theory, fitness, the units of selection, information, genetic and epigentic inheritance, and the evolution of minds.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 006 or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 114 or PHIL 133 or PHIL 134 or PHIL 135 or PHIL 137 or PHIL 144; BIOL 002 or BIOL 003 or BIOL 005A or BIOL 005B or BIOL 005C or BIOL 010 or BIOL 020 or BIOL 030 or BIOL 034; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Science
description: Discusses topics including understanding scientific objectivity in the light of history and sociology of science; realism and anti-realism about scientific theories; scientific methodology and its logic; and the nature of scientific explanation.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: (E-Z) Philosophy of Agency
description: An investigation of problems that arise in attempts to understand human agency. Includes the nature and explanation of action, intention, free will and moral responsibility, and weakness of will. E. Autonomy, Identification And Moral Psychology; F. Action, Intention, And Responsibility; G. Kinds Of Agency; I. Individual And Collective Agency.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Mathematics
description: Discusses topics including abstract nature of mathematical objects, the sources of mathematical knowledge, the relation between mathematics and logic, and the infinite in mathematics. Considers the development of some selected parts of mathematics (especially arithmetic, geometry, algebra, and set theory) and of various corresponding philosophical positions (platonism, formalism, intuitionism, structuralism). Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 124; or one mathematics course; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Topics in Metaphysics
description: An in-depth discussion of selected issues in contemporary metaphysics, such as abstract objects, essentialism and identity, laws of nature, free will, and determinism. Course is repeatable as content changes.
prerequisites_text: one course in philosophy or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Advanced Topics in the Philosophy of Language
description: An in-depth study of a particular topic in the philosophy of language. Potential topics include context-sensitivity (how the meaning of a sentence depends upon nonlinguistic facts about context); theories of meaning (e.g., the Frege-Russell account in terms of propositions, the Lewis-Stalnaker possible worlds account, and Davidson’s truth theory account). Courses is repeatable as content changes to a maximum of 8 units. Credit is awarded for only one of PHIL 142 or PHIL 242.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 107 or PHIL 132 or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Advanced Topics in Philosophy of Mind
description: Examines a selected topic in philosophy of mind. Potential topics include consciousness and self-consciousness; intentionality and theories of mental content; mental causation; consciousness and free will; introspection and knowledge of other minds; perception; emotion; imagination; concepts and rationality; artificial minds; and animal minds. Course is repeatable as content changes to a maximum of 8 units. Credit is awarded for only one of PHIL 144 or PHIL 244.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 107 or PHIL 134 or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Psychiatry
description: Explores philosophical issues arising from psychiatric treatment and research. Topics include definitions of mental health and mental illness, concepts of disorder and abnormality, functionalism, the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, psychosis, delusions, hallucinations, anxiety, depression, addiction, autonomy, the nature of explanation and understanding, and moral and legal responsibility.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence
description: An advanced introduction to the philosophy of computer science and artificial intelligence.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 124; PHIL 132 or PHIL 135 or PHIL 136 or PHIL 137; restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior

subject: PHIL
title: Pragmatics
description: An introduction to the study of language use in context. Topics include implicature, presupposition, speech acts, relevance theory, and the semantics-pragmatics interface. Emphasizes theoretical frameworks and empirical data from linguistics, philosophy of language, and cognitive science.
prerequisites_text: CS 011 or MATH 011 or LING 020 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 130 or PHIL 132; restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Information
description: Examines key issues in the philosophy of information. Includes theories of semantic and naturalistic information, informational ontologies, and the intersections of logic, computation, and cognition. Topics include informational pluralism, structural realism, digital ontology, semantic content, and the use of information in cognitive science and the biological sciences.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 124; PHIL 132 or PHIL 135 or PHIL 136 or PHIL 137; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy in Literature
description: An examination of philosophical issues raised by selected novelists, poets, and playwrights.
prerequisites_text: one course in philosophy or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Existentialism
description: An examination of philosophical and literary works which deal with the significance of some fundamental human experiences: identity crises, choice and commitment, anxiety and death, the experience of meaninglessness, and alienation.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Twentieth-Century Continental Philosophy
description: Examines the character and consequences of several recent movements in continental philosophy including hermeneutics, structuralism, deconstruction, and critical theory. Discusses authors including Heidegger, Gadamer, Habermas, Derrida, and Foucault.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Marxist Critique
description: An examination of the ideas central to the tradition of Western Marxism: ideology, critique, reification, instrumental reason, the domination of nature, and communicative action. Theorists discussed typically include Hegel, Marx, Lukacs, Adorno, Horkheimer, Benjamin, and Habermas. Credit is awarded for only one of PHIL 153 or PHIL 253.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Phenomenology
description: A study of the structures and conditions of the lived experience of the world. Explores the major issues, methodology, and historical development of the phenomenological tradition in philosophy. Discusses philosophers including Edmund Husserl, Edith Stein, Martin Heidegger, Max Scheler, Jean-Paul Sartre, Simone de Beauvoir, and Maurice Merleau-Ponty.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Peace in the Middle East
description: A study of the roots of the Middle Eastern crises. Focuses on the Arab-Israeli conflict and possible solutions toward peace. Addresses problems through historical, religious, and political lines of inquiry. Cross-listed with RLST 155.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Religion
description: A historical, critical examination of the concepts and arguments involved in the Judeo-Christian God-hypothesis, and the influence of this world view upon the ideals and values of the Western world.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Ethics
description: A study of the major classical moral philosophers in the Western tradition and of some selected problems of metaethics.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Human Nature and Radical Evil
description: An advanced study of theories of human nature and evil.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Political Philosophy
description: An inquiry into some of the main philosophic issues arising from political life, such as the nature and justification of authority, democracy, natural rights, justice, equality, and civil disobedience.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Justice
description: A philosophical analysis of the concept of justice.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Law
description: An inquiry into the nature of criminal law, the relation between law and morality, the nature of legal responsibility, and the obligation to obey the law. Credit is awarded for one of the following PHIL 165 or PHIL 165H.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Honors Philosophy of Law
description: Honors course corresponding to PHIL 165. An inquiry into the nature of criminal law, the relation between law and morality, the nature of legal responsibility, and the obligation to obey the law. Credit is awarded for one of the following PHIL 165H or PHIL 165.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; admission to University Honors; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Feminism
description: An analysis of current concepts and debates in feminist philosophy including gender equality, gender difference, and the relation of sex and gender. Situates various approaches to these topics in the history of philosophy.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Biomedical Ethics
description: A philosophical discussion of newly emerging issues, both ethical and social, in biology and medicine, such as genetic engineering, euthanasia, experimentation with human subjects, abortion, behavior control, and patient’s right to know.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Ethics and Families
description: Analyzes ethical issues with regard to families. Explores gender relations in traditional marriages; the ethics of same-sex marriage; the morality of abortion, surrogate mothering, and cloning; the justice of school vouchers; the grounds for universal health care; and possible gender inequalities in divorce.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: (E-Z) Topics in Value Theory
description: Topics include E. Ethics; F. Aesthetics; G. Political Philosophy; I. Social Philosophy; J. Philosophy Of Law.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 001 or PHIL 001H or PHIL 002 or PHIL 002H or PHIL 003 or PHIL 003H or PHIL 003W or PHIL 004 or PHIL 005 or PHIL 006 or PHIL 007 or PHIL 007H or PHIL 008 or PHIL 008H or PHIL 009 or PHIL 009H or PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 012 or PHIL 030E or PHIL 030F or PHIL 030G or PHIL 030I or PHIL 030J or PHIL 030K or PHIL 030M or PHIL 030N; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: PHIL
title: Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
description: Examines the ethics of artificial intelligence including algorithmic bias, rights of AI entities, and societal impacts.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: PHIL
title: Feminist Bioethics
description: An exploration of the ways in which feminist theory provides insight on contemporary issues in bioethics. Topics include women in clinical research, cosmetic surgery, abortion, contract gestation, fetal protection policies, and the politics of mental illness.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Reading Philosophical German
description: Develops reading strategies and translation skills for German philosophical texts through a review of grammar and readings in the original language. Prepares for a graduate-level translation exam and independent research in German. Intermediate to advanced German reading proficiency required; familiarity with German philosophical works is recommended but not required. Cross-listed with GER 172.
prerequisites_text: GER 002R or GER 004 or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Sex and Sexuality
description: Investigates philosophical issues relating to human sexual behaviors and identities. Topics include attempts to distinguish sexual from nonsexual activities; the construction and medicalization of sex and sexuality; and historical and contemporary ethical evaluations of various sexual activities and identities (homosexuality, heterosexuality, masturbation, sadomasochism, various fetishisms, polyamory, and other nonmonogamies).
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Art and Aesthetics
description: Examination of the main topics in the philosophy of art and aesthetics through both historical and contemporary sources. Addresses the following questions: What is art? What is beauty? What is the relation between the beautiful, the true, and the good? Is beauty mind-dependent? Are there objective standards for judging artworks?
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Perception
description: Examines the nature of perception (especially vision) from a philosophically informed interdisciplinary point of view.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 010 or PHIL 010H or PHIL 107 or PHIL 124 or PHIL 130 or PHIL 132 or PHIL 133 or PHIL 134 or PHIL 135 or PHIL 137 or PSYC 001 or PSYC 002 or PSYC 110 or PSYC 132 or PSYC 134; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: PHIL
title: Advanced Topics in the Theory of Knowledge
description: Examines key issues in contemporary research in the theory of knowledge. Topics may include the analysis of knowledge, recent work on radical skepticism, empirical findings relevant to theories of knowledge, semantic and contextualist approaches, social epistemology, and feminist approaches to knowledge.
prerequisites_text: PHIL 008 or PHIL 124; LING 151 or PHIL 130 or PHIL 131 or PHIL 132 or PHIL 133 or PHIL 134 or PHIL 136 or PHIL 137 or PHIL 139 or PHIL 142 or PHIL 143 or PHIL 144 or PHIL 145 or PHIL 146 or PHIL 147; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: PHIL
title: Special Studies
description: Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: to be taken with the consent of the department chair as a means of meeting special curricular problems

subject: PHIL
title: Senior Seminar
description: Advanced seminar for Philosophy majors. Course is repeatable as content changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: two upper-division courses in philosophy; senior standing in Philosophy or Philosophy/Law and Society or consent of instructor

subject: PHIL
title: Senior Thesis
description: Course is graded In Progress (IP) until the thesis is completed. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: enrollment by request of student with approval of department chair

subject: PHIL
title: R’course: Variable Topics
description: An opportunity for UCR undergraduate students to develop leadership skills, innovate the undergraduate curriculum, and promote democratic, experiential education. Original course topics are variable and unique from other departmental course offerings, designed to highlight the student facilitators’ expertise while working closely with a faculty mentor. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: permission needed from department; sophomore standing or better

subject: PHIL
title: Individual Internship in Philosophy
description: An intern assignment in government, education, science, business, or other field related to philosophy. Students write a substantive philosophical paper pertaining to the work done in the internship. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics
description: Covers topics in classical mechanics including Newton’s laws of motion in one and two dimensions; gravity; work, energy, and conservation of energy; momentum and collisions; rotational motion; and orbital motion. First part of the course covers the principles of physics underlying the biological and life sciences. Credit is awarded for one of the following PHYS 002A, PHYS 02HA, PHYS 040A, PHYS 040HA, or PHYS 041A.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in PHYS 02LA; MATH 007A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HA with a grade of C- or better or MATH 005B with a grade of C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics
description: Second part of the introductory course that covers the principles of physics underlying the biological and life sciences. Topics include fluids and fluid flow; thermodynamics; mechanical oscillations; sound and light waves; geometrical optics; reflection; refraction; lens; microscopy; interference; and diffraction. Credit is awarded for one of the following PHYS 002B, PHYS 02HB, PHYS 040B, PHYS 040HB, or PHYS 041B.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in PHYS 02LB; MATH 007B, may be taken concurrently or MATH 009B, may be taken concurrently or MATH 09HB, may be taken concurrently or MATH 005C, may be taken concurrently; PHYS 002A with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 02HA with a grade of C- or better; PHYS 02LA with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 02HLA with a grade of C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics
description: Third part of an introductory course covering the principles of physics underlying the biological and life sciences. Topics include electromagnetism, quantum physics, and Coulomb’s Law. Covers electric field, electrical potential, resistors, capacitors, simple circuits, magnetic forces and Faraday’s Law. Also addresses basic quantum physics of light, atoms, and radioactivity. Credit is awarded for one of the following PHYS 002C, PHYS 02HC, PHYS 040C, PHYS 040HC, or PHYS 041C.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in PHYS 02LC; PHYS 002B with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 02HB with a grade of C- or better; PHYS 02LB with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 02HLB with a grade of C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: History of the Universe
description: An introduction to “The Big Bang” model and its observational tests. Topics include dark energy, dark matter, rapid growth of universe at early times, leftover radiation from “The Big Bang”, galaxy formation, bending of light by gravity, black holes, extraterrestrial life, and the likely fate of the universe.

subject: PHYS
title: The Violent Universe
description: An introduction to violent phenomena that power the universe, specifically phenomena that illustrate basic astrophysical principles. Topics include impacts in our planetary system: explosions of stars, bursts of star formation, galaxy collisions, black holes, quasars, cosmic jets, and the “Big Bang.”

subject: PHYS
title: Space Time, Relativity, and Cosmology
description: A non-mathematical presentation on gravity, understanding of the universe, and how present theories originated. Topics include the ancient Greeks, Galileo, Newton, the speed of light, Einstein’s special and general relativity, the lifetimes of stars, supernovas, gravitational waves, the Big Bang, cosmic inflation, and the multiverse.

subject: PHYS
title: Color and Sound: Dimensions in Communication
description: Discusses the interplay between visual and aural sensory experiences and the physical principles of light and sound. Topics include visual perception and pattern recognition; the color spectrum; optical instruments; anatomy of the camera and the eye; lasers and holography; vibrations and sound waves; acoustics; reverberation; and sound production in speech, music, and high-fidelity audio devices. Involves demonstrations and illustrations.

subject: PHYS
title: How Things Work
description: Surveys the physical basis of modern technology emphasizing electronics and electrical devices. Topics include electro- and magneto-statics and dynamics (xerographic copiers, magnetic levitation, electrical power distribution); communication (radio, TV, computers, tape recorders, CD players); and imaging (cameras, DVD players, x rays, magnetic resonance imaging).

subject: PHYS
title: Principles of Physics
description: Topics include classical laws of motion, force, energy, electricity and magnetism, properties of matter, atomic structure, waves, sound, light, heat, the Earth, and the solar system and universe. Includes demonstrations and visual illustrations. Not open to students with credit or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 002A or PHYS 02HA or PHYS 002B or PHYS 02HB or PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC or PHYS 040A or PHYS 040HA or PHYS 040B or PHYS 040HB or PHYS 040C or PHYS 040HC or PHYS 040D or PHYS 040E.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005A is recommended

subject: PHYS
title: Linear Algebra For Physics
description: This course covers the essential mathematics for quantum mechanics at the upper-division level. It applies linear algebra finite and infinite dimensional vector spaces. Topics include matrices, linear equations, bases, eigenvectors and eigenvalues, functions as infinite-dimensional vectors, differential operators as matrices, Fourier transforms, and eigenfunctions of common differential operators.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B with a grade of C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: Energy and the Environment
description: Covers the physics of energy (thermal, kinetic, potential, chemical, nuclear), its storage and use, primary sources of energy (fossil fuel, nuclear, wind, solar) and their relative effects on the environment. Particular emphasis on determining individual carbon footprints, physical models of global climate change and identifying pathways toward a sustainable infrastructure.

subject: PHYS
title: Exploring the Universe: An Adventure in Astronomy
description: An astronomy course for non-science students. The excitement of an evolving and sometimes violent universe of stars and galaxies is explored in a descriptive manner. Here, the union of modern and ancient observations with astrophysical laws will provide a sophisticated but by no means complete picture of the universe. Special topics such as Astrology and Extraterrestrial Life will be discussed.

subject: PHYS
title: Dna in Your Life: the Physical Basis For Structure, Function, and Control
description: An introduction to various medical, biological, and commercial aspects of physical DNA science.

title: Introductory Physics For Physics Majors
description: Covers relativity oscillations, mechanical waves, fluids, electrostatics, magnetism, and circuits. Credit is awarded for one of the following PHYS 041B, PHYS 040C, or PHYS 040HC.
prerequisites_text: MATH 007B with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently or MATH 009B with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently or MATH 09HB with a grade of B or better, may be taken concurrently or MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently; PHYS 002A with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 040A with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 041A with a grade of C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: Introductory Physics For Physics Majors
description: Covers electromagnetism, geometric and wave optics, and modern physics. Credit is awarded for one of the following PHYS 041C, PHYS 002C, PHYS 02HC, or PHYS 040HC.
prerequisites_text: MATH 009C with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently or MATH 09HC with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently or MATH 005C with a grade of C- or better, may be taken concurrently; PHYS 002B with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 02HB with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 040C with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 040HC with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 041B with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Applied Data Science: A Multi-Disciplinary Approach
description: Introduces students from different disciplines (physical, biological, engineering, finance, economy, humanities) to data science techniques and applications. Provides background knowledge in data science and prepares for a career in this field. Provides basic knowledge to continue on to more advanced topics in data science and apply it to practical problems.

subject: PHYS
title: Lower-Division Research
description: Special research projects in physics performed under the supervision of a member of the staff. This course may not be used to satisfy the undergraduate unit requirements in the major. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Astrophysics and Stellar Astronomy
description: Covers stellar interiors, radiations, and evolution; the origin of the elements; particle and electromagnetic radiation; pulsars, quasars, and other unusual objects; and galactic structure and cosmology.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B, MATH 046, or equivalents; one of the following: PHYS 040D with a grade of C- or better, PHYS 041C with a grade of C- or better, PHYS 002C with a grade of B- or better

subject: PHYS
title: Galaxies and Extragalactic Astronomy
description: Topics include the structure of the Milky Way, the observed properties of galaxies, active galactic nuclei and supermassive black holes, the intergalactic medium, the theory of galaxy formation and evolution, galaxy clusters, and the large scale structure of our universe.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 111 with a grade of C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Mathematical Methods of Physics
description: This course covers advanced mathematical for upper division and graduate physics courses. Topics include dimensional analysis, infinite dimensional vector spaces, integral transforms, complex analysis, and the use of Green’s functions to solve inhomogeneous differential equations. This course is strongly recommended for students with a focus on theoretical physics.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B with a grade of C- or better, MATH 046 with a grade of C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: Classical Mechanics
description: Explores vector calculus, single-particle motion, oscillations, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian dynamics, central-forces motion, and celestial mechanics.
prerequisites_text: MATH 009C, MATH 010A (may be taken concurrently); one of the following: PHYS 002A or PHYS 02HA with a grade of B- or better, PHYS 040A or PHYS 040HA with a grade of C- or better, PHYS 041A with a grade of C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: Classical Mechanics
description: Topics include dynamics of a system of particles, motion in non-inertial reference systems, dynamics of rigid bodies, coupled oscillations, and special theory of relativity.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010A, MATH 010B (may be taken concurrently), PHYS 130A

subject: PHYS
title: Thermal Physics
description: Covers thermodynamics and an introduction to statistical mechanics. Topics include states of a model system; entropy and temperature; the Boltzmann distribution and Helmholtz free energy; thermal radiation and the Planck distribution; chemical potential; the ideal gas; Fermi and Bose gasses; and heat and work.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B; MATH 046 (may be taken concurrently); PHYS 130B

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Statistical Physics
description: Covers advanced topics in statistical mechanics, ensembles, and classical and quantum statistical mechanics. Explores the connection between statistical mechanics and thermodynamics.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 132 and PHYS 156B

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetism
description: Topics include vector calculus; Coulomb’s law and the electric field; Gauss’ law; scalar potential; conductors in electrostatic fields; electrostatic energy; electric multipoles; boundary conditions; electrostatics in the presence of matter; and special methods in electrostatics.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B; MATH 046; one of the following: PHYS 002B or PHYS 02HB with B- or better, PHYS 040C or PHYS 040HC with a C- or better, PHYS 041B with a C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetism
description: Topics include electric currents and circuits, Ampere’s law, the magnetic field, the integral form of Ampere’s law, the vector potential, Faraday’s law of induction, magnetic energy, magnetic multipoles, magnetism in the presence of matter, Maxwell’s equations, and plane waves.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 135A

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetic Waves
description: Covers Maxwell’s equations; propagation of electromagnetic waves in wave guides, coaxial lines, and optical fibers; reflection, refraction, and diffraction of waves; dispersion of waves in gases and plasmas; interference and coherence and their role in holography; electromagnetic radiation from charged particles, antennas, masers, and lasers; and relativistic electrodynamics.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 135B

subject: PHYS
title: Electronics For Scientists
description: Introduces basic analog and digital circuit designs that emphasize practical applications. Includes properties of diodes and transistors; operational amplifiers for use as amplifiers, oscillators, and function generators; properties and use of logic gates, counters, and timers; data storage and synchronization; multiplexer and decoder applications; microprocessor functions; and computer interfacing.
prerequisites_text: One of the following: PHYS 002B or PHYS 02HB with B- or better, PHYS 040C or PHYS 040HC with a C- or better, PHYS 041B with a C- or better, or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Techniques of Observational Astronomy
description: Covers modern techniques of observational astronomy including digital optical imaging, photometry, spectroscopy, radio observations, error propagation and statistical inference. Lab practicum includes calibrating digital images and spectra, computer programming for data analysis, quantifying uncertainties in astronomical measurements, and written communication of scientific results.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 002C with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 02HC with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 040E with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 041C with a grade of C or better; restricted to major(s) Physics; or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Physics Laboratory
description: A capstone experience consisting of experiments chosen from areas in contemporary physics. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units. Credit is awarded to a maximum of 10 units for either or both PHYS 142L and/or PHYS 142W.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 002C with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 02HC with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 040E with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 41C with a grade of C- or better; restricted to class level standing of senior; restricted to major(s) Physics; or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Physics Laboratory
description: A capstone experience consisting of experiments chosen from areas in contemporary physics. Includes writing instruction with an emphasis on technical communication. Fulfills the third-quarter writing requirement for students who earn a grade of “C” or better for courses that the Academic Senate designates, and that the student’s college permits, as alternatives to WRIT 030. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 10 units. Credit is awarded to a maximum of 10 units for either or both PHYS 142L or PHYS 142W.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 040S; PHYS 002C with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 02HC with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 040E with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 041C with a grade of C- or better; WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better; restricted to class level standing of senior; and consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Biophysics
description: Covers physical modeling of the structure of proteins; protein folding; structure of nucleic acids; electrostatic potential of DNA; dynamics of biomolecules; structure of a biological cell; osmotic pressures of cells; non-equilibrium thermodynamics; and biochemical reactions.
prerequisites_text: CHEM 001C or CHEM 01HC; MATH 010B; MATH 046; one of the following: PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC with B- or better, PHYS 041C with a C- or better, PHYS 040E with a C- or better

subject: PHYS
title: Biophysics
description: Covers conformation of biopolymers, intermolecular forces, dynamics of biopolymers, Brownian motion, biopolymers as polyelectrolytes, electrolytic solutions, and the Debye-Huckel theory.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 145A; BCH 100 or BCH 110B or BCH 110HB; or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Biophysics
description: Examines stochastic thermodynamics; the Fluctuation Theorems and the Jarzynski relation; protein and RNA denaturation; tests of the Jarzynski relation; chemical forces and self-assembly; enzymes and molecular machines; survey of molecular devices found in cells; and kinetics of real enzymes and machines.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 145B or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Condensed Matter Physics
description: Covers properties of systems composed of many atoms arranged in a periodic lattice. Topics include crystal structure, symmetry, and diffraction; crystal cohesion; lattice dynamics; thermal properties; metallic properties and the Fermi surface; band theory of metals and semiconductors; and collective excitations.
prerequisites_text: One of the following: PHYS 002B with B- or better, PHYS 040E with a C- or better, PHYS 041C with a C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Condensed Matter Physics
description: Covers properties of systems composed of many atoms arranged in a periodic lattice. Topics include superconductivity; magnetism; non-crystalline solids; defects in solids; surface and interface physics; and alloys.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 150A

subject: PHYS
title: Topics in Modern Condensed Matter Research
description: Consent of instructor is required for students repeating the course. Introduces cutting-edge physics research being conducted in laboratories and institutes around the world. Focuses on a single research area (e.g., nanoscale physics, biological physics) that may change each quarter. Includes experimental methods and theoretical concepts. Course is repeatable as content changes to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: One of the following: PHYS 002B or BCH 110HB with a grade of “B-” or better, PHYS 040E with a C- or better, PHYS 041C with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: PHYS
title: Exploring Many-Body Quantum Physics With Mathematica
description: An introduction to numerics and visualization using Mathematica. Topics include random numbers and stochastic processes; time-dependent and stationary equations in matrix form; single-particle tight-binding model; single-spin dynamics; pure and mixed states; spin echo; the direct product of matrices; many-body quantum mechanics; and quantum spin chains.
prerequisites_text: MATH 046; one of the following: PHYS 002C with a B- or better, PHYS 040E with a C- or better, PHYS 041C with a C- or better; or consent of instructor. MATH 031 is recommended

subject: PHYS
title: Exploring Many-Body Quantum Physics With Mathematica
description: Covers the symmetry of many-body wavefunction, including bosons and fermions; secondary quantization; harmonic oscillators; ladder operators, eigenvalues, and eigenfunctions; interacting many-body systems; mean field approximation; and density matrix of a subsystem and decoherence.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 152A or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Topics include wave-particle duality, the Schrodinger equation, superposition, the uncertainty principle, and one-dimensional harmonic oscillator.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B, MATH 046, PHYS 130B; one of the following: PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC with a grade of “B-” or better, PHYS 040E with a grade of “C-” or better, PHYS 041C with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Topics include the hydrogen atom, angular momentum and spin representations, many-electron systems, the Pauli exclusion principle, and perturbation theory.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 156A

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Applications in quantum mechanics. Includes perturbation theory and other approximations, scattering, and an introduction to advanced topics such as relativistic quantum mechanics.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 156B

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Quantum Computation
description: Topics include the basic concepts of quantum mechanics; entanglement; Bell’s inequalities; quantum circuits; Deutsch’s and Shor’s algorithms; and quantum error correction.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 002C with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 02HC with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 040C with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 041C with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Atomic Physics and Spectroscopy
description: Covers the role of atomic physics and spectroscopy in the development of quantum mechanics; Bohrs old quantum theory; Heisenbergs matrix mechanics; Schrodingers wave mechanics; Dirac equation; the g-factor; Zeeman effect and the Darwin term; Spin-orbit coupling and Thomas precession; Dirac hydrogen atom; Fine structure; Hyperfine structure; Lamb shift.
prerequisites_text: CHEM 113 or PHYS 156A with a C- or better, PHYS 135A with a C- or better, or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Nuclear Physics
description: Addresses the basic nuclear properties, as well as the nuclear building blocks and structure. Explores radioactivity, nuclear interactions, the strong force, the confinement and chiral phase transitions, the quantum chromodynamics (QCD) vacuum, and matter at extreme temperatures and densities.
prerequisites_text: One of the following: PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC with a grade of “B-” or better, PHYS 040E with a grade of “C-” or better, PHYS 041C with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: PHYS
title: Introduction to Particle Physics
description: Explores the classification of particles in terms of the Standard Model. Includes methods and techniques for particle acceleration and detection; conservation laws and symmetries; the basic interactions of particles (electromagnetic, strong, weak); and electroweak unification.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 156A

subject: PHYS
title: Cosmology
description: Discusses current topics in astrophysics and cosmology from the perspective of elementary particle physics. Topics include the development and structure of the early universe, dark matter and dark energy, cosmic radiation, and particle physics in the stars.
prerequisites_text: PHYS 156A

subject: PHYS
title: Energy and the Environment
description: Explores physical insights into primary energy uses in society such as electricity, transportation, and heating. Explains how that energy is obtained and transformed (e.g., fossil fuels, nuclear, hydropower, heat engines). Also addresses renewable energy (photovoltaics, wind, batteries, fuel cells) in the context of climate change and sustainability.
prerequisites_text: MATH 010B with a grade of C- or better, PHYS 040C with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 041C with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Computational Methods For Physical Sciences
description: Covers computer applications for solving problems in physical sciences. Addresses symbolic manipulation languages such as Mathematica, mathematical operations, plotting, and symbolic and numerical techniques in calculus. Includes numerical methods such as histogramming, the Monte-Carlo method for modeling experiments, statistical analysis, curve fitting, and numerical algorithms.
prerequisites_text: CS 009A or CS 010A or CS 010B; PHYS 002C with a grade of B- or better or PHYS 02HC with a grade of B or better or PHYS 040E with a grade of C- or better or PHYS 041C with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Special Studies
description: May not be used to satisfy major requirements unless taken as a replacement for a course not being offered during the student’s remaining tenure. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 9 units; a maximum of 5 units may be used to substitute for PHYS 142L.
prerequisites_text: consent of department chair Individual study to meet special curricular needs

subject: PHYS
title: Special Studies at Los Alamos National Laboratory
description: Individual study to meet special curricular needs. Course is repeatable to a maximum to 16 units.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UCR/LANL Educational Internship Program; consent of advisor and department chair

subject: PHYS
title: Senior Thesis
description: A thesis written on research conducted under the supervision of a faculty member. May be undertaken as a one-, two-, three-, or four-quarter course (PHYS 195A, PHYS 195B, PHYS 195C, PHYS 195D). Total credit awarded for PHYS 195A plus PHYS 195B plus PHYS 195C plus PHYS 195D may not exceed 8 units; a maximum of 4 units may be used to satisfy the unit requirement for the major, and a maximum of 5 units of any combination of PHYS 195A, PHYS 195B, PHYS 195C, and PHYS 195D may be used to substitute for PHYS 142L. Graded In Progress (IP) until the last quarter is completed, at which time a final grade is assigned; a Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grade is awarded unless the course is taken to substitute for PHYS 142L.

subject: PHYS
title: Senior Thesis
description: A thesis written on research conducted under the supervision of a faculty member. May be undertaken as a one-, two-, three-, or four-quarter course (PHYS 195A, PHYS 195B, PHYS 195C, PHYS 195D). Total credit awarded for PHYS 195A plus PHYS 195B plus PHYS 195C plus PHYS 195D may not exceed 8 units; a maximum of 4 units may be used to satisfy the unit requirement for the major, and a maximum of 5 units of any combination of PHYS 195A, PHYS 195B, PHYS 195C, and PHYS 195D may be used to substitute for PHYS 142L. Graded In Progress (IP) until the last quarter is completed, at which time a final grade is assigned; a Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grade is awarded unless the course is taken to substitute for PHYS 142L.
prerequisites_text: senior standing; consent of instructor; PHYS 195A

subject: PHYS
title: Senior Thesis
description: A thesis written on research conducted under the supervision of a faculty member. May be undertaken as a one-, two-, three-, or four-quarter course (PHYS 195A, PHYS 195B, PHYS 195C, PHYS 195D). Graded In Progress (IP) until the last quarter is completed, at which time a final grade is assigned; a Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grade is awarded unless the course is taken to substitute for PHYS 142L
prerequisites_text: senior standing; consent of instructor; PHYS 195B

subject: PHYS

description: A thesis written on research conducted under the supervision of a faculty member. Graded In Progress (IP) until the last quarter is completed, at which time a final grade is assigned; a Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grade is awarded unless the course is taken to substitute for PHYS 142L.
prerequisites_text: senior standing; consent of instructor; PHYS 195C

subject: PHYS
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: Special research projects in physics performed under the supervision of a member of the staff. This course may not be used to satisfy the undergraduate unit requirement in the major. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor

subject: PHYS
title: Individual Internship in Physics
description: Provides experience as a practicing scientist in a government or industrial laboratory. Includes joint supervision by an off-campus sponsor and a Physics faculty member. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units; a maximum of 4 units may be used to satisfy major requirements, and a maximum of 5 units may be used to substitute for PHYS 142L.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of department chair

subject: PLPA
title: Microbes and Society: A Window Into the Microbial World Around US
description: An introduction to the remarkable diversity and biology of microorganisms. Emphasizes the areas microorganisms impact human affairs, including food production, agriculture, medicine, and history. Includes cheese-, yogurt-, wine-, beer- and bread-making; the Irish potato famine; tulipomania; antibiotics; mushrooms and mushroom lore; food preservation; microbial toxins and food poisoning; and vaccines and useful viruses.

subject: PLPA
title: Introduction to Plant Pathology
description: An introduction to the study of plant diseases. Topics include diseases and disease-causing agents, host-pathogen interaction during disease development, and strategies for disease management. Includes optional, separate laboratory. Cross-listed with BIOL 120, and MCBL 120. Credit is awarded for one of the following PLPA 120, BIOL 120, MCBL 120, or PLPA 210.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; BCH 100 or BCH 100H or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; STAT 010

subject: PLPA
title: Introduction to Plant Pathology Laboratory
description: Covers fundamentals in the use of laboratory instruments and techniques for the detection, isolation, and identification of representative infectious agents that cause disease in plants. Cross-listed with BIOL 120L, and MCBL 120L. Credit is awarded for one of the following PLPA 120L, BIOL 120L, MCBL 120L, or PLPA 210.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC; PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; BIOL 120, may be taken concurrently or MCBL 120, may be taken concurrently or PLPA 120, may be taken concurrently; STAT 010, may be taken concurrently; BIOL 121/MCBL 121 and BIOL 124/MCBL 124 recommended; or consent of instructor

subject: PLPA
title: Introduction to Comparative Virology
description: Considers viruses as infectious agents of bacteria, plants, and animals (vertebrates and invertebrates). Compares the major groups of viruses with respect to their biological and biochemical properties, molecular and genetic characteristics, and modes of replication. Cross-listed with BIOL 123, and MCBL 123.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; BCH 100, may be taken concurrently or BCH 100H, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110A, may be taken concurrently or BCH 110HA, may be taken concurrently; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; STAT 010; or consent of instructor

subject: PLPA
title: Pesticide Science
description: An introduction to the chemistry, modes of action, and use of insecticides, rodenticides, herbicides, and biopesticides from discovery to environmental interactions. Includes genetics of pesticide resistance development, resistance management, government regulation, probit analysis, dilution and calculations of treatment rates, and sustainable pest management. Cross-listed with ENTM 125, and ENTX 125.
prerequisites_text: CHEM 008B, BIOL 005C or CHEM 08HB; CHEM 08LB or CHEM 08HLB

subject: PLPA
title: Introduction to Mycology
description: Introduction to the morphology, taxonomy, genetics, physiology, ecology, and economic importance of the major groups of the fungi. Cross-listed with BIOL 134.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005C; MATH 007B or MATH 009B or MATH 09HB; PHYS 002C or PHYS 02HC; PHYS 02LC or PHYS 02HLC; BCH 100 or BCH 110A or BCH 110HA; STAT 004, or equivalent; or consent of instructor

subject: PLPA
title: Introduction to Mycology Laboratory
description: Introduces fundamentals in the use of laboratory instruments and techniques for the isolation, cultivation, and identification of representatives of the major taxa of fungi. Cross-listed with BIOL134L.
prerequisites_text: BIOL 005A, BIOL 005B, BIOL 005C, or equivalents; concurrent enrollment in BIOL 134/PLPA 134; or consent of instructor

prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: PORT
title: Intensive Brazilian Portuguese For Speakers of Spanish
description: An introduction to Brazilian Portuguese for students knowing Spanish. Emphasizes comparing and contrasting grammatical constructions. Provides examples from Brazilian literature.
prerequisites_text: SPN 101A or SPN 109A or equivalent

subject: PORT
title: Intensive Brazilian Portuguese For Speakers of Spanish
description: Continuation of PORT 101A. Covers advanced language through conversation, composition, and readings.
prerequisites_text: PORT 101A or equivalent

subject: PORT
title: Intensive Brazilian Portuguese For Speakers of Spanish
description: Completes the study of structures of oral and written Portuguese, builds vocabulary, and hones the skills necessary to read Brazilian literature, discuss its content and importance, and write short essays explaining its nature.
prerequisites_text: PORT 101B or equivalent

subject: PORT
title: (E-Z) Survey in Brazilian Fiction
description: Reading and analysis of selected works of major Brazilian prose writers. Topics may vary each time course is offered. E. Jorge Amado And Machado De Assis; F. Graciliano Ramos, Rego, Queiroz, Azevedo, Amado; G. Verissimo, Amado. Course To Be Taught In The Original Language.
prerequisites_text: PORT 101B

subject: POSC
title: Political Ideologies
description: An introductory study of the ideologies of the modern era. Explores selected thinkers and texts representative of liberalism, conservatism, socialism, fascism, nationalism, nonviolence, and feminism, as well as various non-Western ideologies. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 005, POSC 005H, or POSC 005W.

subject: POSC
title: Honors Political Ideologies
description: Honors course corresponding to POSC 005 and POSC 005W. An introductory study of the ideologies of the modern era. Explores selected thinkers and texts representative of liberalism, conservatism, socialism, fascism, nationalism, nonviolence, and feminism, as well as various non-Western ideologies. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Credit is awarded for only one of POSC 005, POSC 005H, or POSC 005W.
prerequisites_text: admission to University Honors or consent of instructor

prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 040G; WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better, WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better; or consent of instructor

subject: POSC
title: Introduction to Political Theory
description: An introductory exploration of political theory from the ancient world to the present. Covers either Western theorists (from Aristotle to Rawls) or non-Western theorists (from Confucius to Gandhi). Topics include citizenship, community, political change, and human flourishing. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 007 or POSC 007W.

title: American Politics
description: An introduction to the principles and practices of government. Focuses on the policy process and selected political issues in the United States. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 010, POSC 010H, or POSC 010W.

description: A systematic survey of research methodologies in psychology. Laboratory assignments include evaluating and testing psychological theories; assessing methodologies and research designs; designing and implementing research; collecting data and analyzing statistics; writing research reports; and discussing ethical issues in science.
prerequisites_text: ENGL 001B with a grade of C or better; PSYC 001 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 002 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better; MATH 004 with a grade of C- or better or MATH 005A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 006A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 006B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 007A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 007B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 009A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HA with a grade of B or better or MATH 009B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HB with a grade of B or better or MATH 009C with a grade of C- or better or MATH 09HC with a grade of B or better or MATH 010A with a grade of C- or better or MATH 010B with a grade of C- or better or MATH 022 with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent; a score on the Math Advisory Exam sufficient for placement into MATH 005A or MATH 022 or higher; consent of instructor is required for students repeating the course

subject: PSYC
title: Skepticism and Pseudoscience in Psychology
description: Studies topics at the borderland of psychology (extra-sensory perception, repressed memory, pseudoscientific beliefs, parapsychology, psychic phenomena, faith healing, and mass hysteria). Explores skepticism, cynicism, and “gullibility,” and the rhetoric of extraordinary claims. Stresses the development of scientific literacy, critical thinking skills, hypothesis testing, and understanding psychology as an empirical science.
prerequisites_text: WRIT 010 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 010S with a grade of C or better or WRIT 009 with a grade of C or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Topics in Psychology
description: Explores a topic of general interest in psychology. Debate and dialog are the distinguishing features of this course. Topics are announced in the Schedule of Classes. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 16 units.

subject: PSYC
title: Introduction to Art and Psychology
description: Explores the intersection of art and psychology. Examines how artists use techniques to manipulate visual perception and elicit emotional responses. Includes how psychological theories can illuminate the understanding of artistic expression. Cross-listed with AHS 006.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of freshman, or sophomore; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Research For Lower-Division Students
description: An introduction to research in psychology. Emphasizes aspects of library and laboratory research within the content of ongoing faculty research programs Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 6 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of freshman, or sophomore; and consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Research Laboratory For Lower-Division Students
description: An introduction to research in psychology. Emphasizes aspects of library and laboratory research within the content of ongoing faculty research programs. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 6 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of freshman, or sophomore; and consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Advanced Research Methods
description: Advanced theory and practice of planning, conducting, reporting, and evaluating research in the social and behavioral sciences. Students conduct original research that, if desired, can lead to (and become part of) a senior honors thesis or other senior-level research project. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012, each with a grade of “B-” or better; or equivalents; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: The Brain and Behavior
description: Explores the principles of neuroanatomy and neurophysiology and their relationship to brain function. Topics include sensory and perceptual processes, biological aspects of learning and memory, motivation, emotion, language, and abnormal behavior.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001 with a grade of “C-” or better, or equivalents, or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Neural Mechanisms of Animal Behavior
description: Studies how the nervous systems of vertebrates and invertebrates contribute to and control their behavior. Focuses on aspects of sensory physiology with a brief orientation to the structure and function of nervous systems. Emphasizes a top-down approach to neurobiology, with specific behaviors providing guidelines for an examination of neural mechanisms.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 with a grade of “C-” or better or PSYC 110 with a grade of “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Pandemic Biopsychology: From Virus to Vaccine
description: Explores pandemics through analyses of historical events, scientific research investigating viruses related to global outbreaks, human immune response to infection, and how different vaccines (adenovirus, mRNA) are created and function in human systems. Also examines how pandemics impact people’s sense of security, mental health, and personal well-being.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001 with a grade of C- or better, PSYC 002 with a grade of C- or better, PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better, PSYC 012 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Drugs and Behavior
description: Describes both legal and illegal drugs. Analyzes drug-nervous system interactions and how the use of various drugs (particularly drugs of abuse) affects behavior and psychological well-being.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 with a grade of “C-” or better or PSYC 110 with a grade of “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Cognitive Neuroscience of Memory and Consciousness
description: Surveys the neural basis of mental processes, focusing on memory and consciousness and their behavioral manifestations. Emphasizes current research literature.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 with a grade of “C-” or better or PSYC 110 with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: PSYC
title: Cellular Neuroscience: Membrane and Synaptic Phenomena
description: An examination of cellular and molecular mechanisms of nervous system function using concepts drawn from the study of vertebrates and invertebrates with emphasis on mammalian systems. Cross-listed with CBNS 120.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Neuroscience Laboratory
description: Laboratory experiments using electrophysiological, chemical, and anatomical research methods fundamental to understanding neurons and neural systems. Cross-listed with CBNS 120L.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 120, may be taken concurrently or PSYC 120, may be taken concurrently; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Developmental Neuroscience
description: A study of the development of nervous systems. Examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms of neural development and the determinants of cell birth and death, axonal pathfinding, neuronal connections, and development of neural systems underlying behavior. Cross-listed with CBNS 121.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Human Neuroimaging
description: An introduction to magnetic resonance imaging in psychological research with an emphasis on the merits and limitations of structural and functional neuroimaging in humans.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 110 or CBNS 106 or consent of instructor. PSYC 122 can be taken without PSYC 122L

subject: PSYC
title: Human Neuroimaging Laboratory
description: Laboratory exercises in the design, acquisition, and analysis of structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging data.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 122, may be taken concurrently, PSYC 110 or CBNS 106; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Computational Neurophysiology Laboratory: Simulating Neuronal Membrane Properties
description: Introduces computer modeling techniques to enhance understanding of neuronal membrane physiology. Selected topics include biophysical models of single neurons including passive properties and action potential firing, channels regulating neuronal firing properties, synaptic interactions, and simple circuits. Cross-listed with CBNS 130L.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106; CBNS 120, may be taken concurrently or PSYC 120, may be taken concurrently; and consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Systems Neuroscience
description: A study of the structure and function of motor and sensory systems in vertebrate and invertebrate nervous systems. Cross-listed with CBNS 124.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Neuropharmacology
description: Examines synaptic neurotransmitter systems, mechanisms, and pharmacological agents and effects, which are fundamental to neural information processing. Cross-listed with CBNS 125.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 120/PSYC 120

subject: PSYC
title: Neuroscience of Learning and Memory
description: Covers mechanisms of learning and memory across levels of analysis including genetic, neuronal, systems, and theory. Topics include the multiple memory systems, memory consolidation, working memory, emotional memory, recognition memory, spatial memory, and human amnesia. Cross-listed with CBNS 126.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 or PSYC 110; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Behavioral Control Systems
description: An analysis of neural mechanisms that underlie behavior, concentrating on motor control. Topics range from command systems, to central pattern generators, to cortical control of voluntary movement and brain-machine interfaces (neuroprosthetics). Cross-listed with CBNS 127.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 120/PSYC 120; CBNS 124/ PSYC 124 strongly recommended

subject: PSYC
title: Language and the Brain
description: Interdisciplinary introduction to the study of language and the brain. Includes brain evolution for language, neural bases for language production and language comprehension, aphasiology and language disorders, and additional special topics. Cross-listed with LING 162.
prerequisites_text: LING 020 or PSYC 110 or PSYC 135 or CBNS 106; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Human Neuropsychology
description: Surveys how high-level psychological functions (e.g., perception, memory, language) are organized in the human brain. Covers behavioral and cognitive impairments due to disorders such as brain injury, stroke, Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, and dementias including Alzheimer’s disease. Emphasizes how such disorders inform our understanding of cognitive functions.
prerequisites_text: CBNS 106 with a grade of C- or better or PSYC 001 with a grade of C- or better, PSYC 002 with a grade of C- or better, PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better, PSYC 012 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Fundamentals of Learning and Conditioning
description: A survey course that includes both historical and current models of human learning, conditioning, and memory. Provides a good foundation for research or future study in learning and memory by covering fundamental theories established by Pavlov and Skinner while incorporating new theories of human behavioral control.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012 with grades of “C-” or better; or equivalents; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Computational and Mathematical Models in Cognitive Science
description: Introduces students to the technical and theoretical issues involved in using models to understand behavior. Involves analysis of model predictions and simulation of behavioral data. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units if taken with different instructors.
prerequisites_text: a grade of “C-” or better in PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012 or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Perception
description: An analysis of the role played by sensory mechanisms, experiences, expectations, and needs in recognizing objects in the environment.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012 with grades of “C-” or better; or equivalents; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Human Factors
description: Provides an overview of the human capabilities and limitations considered in the design of person-machine systems. Evaluates factors critical to performance in person-machine systems, including attention, decision making, motor performance, and memory.
prerequisites_text: a grade of “C-” or better in one of the following courses or consent of instructor: PSYC 132 or PSYC 134

subject: PSYC
title: Cognitive Processes
description: Addresses empirical and theoretical research in several subareas within contemporary cognitive psychology. Subareas include attention, mental representation, information organization and retrieval from memory, psycholinguistics, problem solving, decision making, thinking, and artificial intelligence and computer simulation of cognitive processes.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 002 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 012 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Psycholinguistics
description: Introduction to psycholinguistics emphasizing the psychological implications of linguistic theory, including the effect of syntactic structure on the comprehension, production, and retention of speech; the course of language acquisition; and models of the adult language user.
prerequisites_text: a grade of “C-” or better in the following courses or consent of instructor: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012

subject: PSYC
title: Topics in Cognitive Neuroscience
description: Intensive study of selected topics in cognitive neuroscience. Stresses the methodology and interpretation of current research topics. Course is repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: a grade of “C-” or better in one of the following courses or consent of instructor: CBNS 106, PSYC 110, PSYC 129, PSYC 132, PSYC 134, PSYC 135

subject: PSYC
title: Topics in Cognitive Psychology
description: Intensive study in cognitive psychology. Stresses literature, methodology, and experimental design and analysis. Course is repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: a grade of “C-” or better in the following courses or consent of instructor: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012; PSYC 132 or PSYC 134 or PSYC 135

subject: PSYC
title: Social Psychology
description: The relationship between the individual and the group, including such topics as conformity and deviance, attraction and prejudice, altruism and aggression, and the social nature of attitudes.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012 with grades of “C-” or better; or equivalents; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Industrial/Organizational Psychology
description: Introduction to the field of industrial/organizational psychology covering fundamental theory and research in personnel and organizations. Topics include employee selection and training, performance appraisal, motivation, organizational dynamics, leadership, and job satisfaction.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 002

subject: PSYC
title: Topics in Social Psychology
description: Intensive study of selected topics in social psychology such as race relations, attitude formation and change, biases of social science researchers, and the application of psychological principles in community organization. Emphasis is on the study of these areas in natural settings. Specific course content varies. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: a grade of “C-” or better in the following courses or consent of instructor: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012, PSYC 140

subject: PSYC
title: The Science of Well-Being
description: Covers current theory and research in positive psychology and the scientific study of optimal human functioning. Topics include the causes and benefits of happiness; how happiness can be measured and increased; positive emotions; flow; and human strengths and virtues including optimism, love, altruism, forgiveness, and gratitude.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001 and PSYC 002

subject: PSYC
title: Personality
description: A survey of the principal theories of personality with attention to the experimental methods and findings on which they are based.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012 with grades of “C-” or better; or equivalents; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Psychopathology
description: An introduction to the research and theories regarding the major types of abnormal behavior. Includes the neuroses, schizophrenia, psychosomatic disorders, sexual disorders, drug and stress induced states, and organic disorders.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 002 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 012 with a grade of C- or better; or equivalents; or consent of instructor

subject: PSYC
title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
description: Introduction to the field of clinical psychology. Emphasizes the application and evaluation of techniques of individual and group counseling and therapy. Also addresses the application and evaluation of psychological tests in the assessment of psychological problems.
prerequisites_text: a grade of “C-” or better in the following courses or consent of instructor: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012, PSYC 151

subject: PSYC
title: Personality Assessment
description: Covers the assessment of personality through self-report tests, projective tests, and systematic observations. Also entails descriptions of the psychometrics of testing as it applies to the problems in studying personality.
prerequisites_text: a grade of “C-” or better in the following courses or consent of instructor: PSYC 001, PSYC 002, PSYC 011, PSYC 012, PSYC 150

subject: PSYC
title: Life Span Development
description: Introduces the biological, social, and cognitive processes that influence development from the prenatal period through late adulthood. Topics include development in physical, motor, perceptual, cognitive, emotional, and social areas. Includes discussion of issues related to intellectual functioning, personality, social roles and relationships, coping and adjustment, and aging.
prerequisites_text: PSYC 001 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 002 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better; PSYC 012 with a grade of C- or better

subject: PSYC
title: Socioemotional and Personality Development
