Also examines movement and advocacy outcomes, challenges, and opportunities for promoting health equity and environmental justice. Credit is awarded for one of the following SEHE 106S or SEHE 106.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Environmental Health and Activism in Southern California
description: Interdisciplinary cross-examination of environmental challenges, social inequities, human health consequences, and environmental justice activisms focusing on Southern California. Investigates the historical contribution of regional industrial developments and racial stratification to poor environmental health. Examines the spatial distribution of environmental and health burdens using California’s mapping and indexing tools.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Ethnography: Collaborative/ Activist Interdisciplinary Research
description: Explores the ethnographic methodologies that are the interdisciplinary tools researchers use to describe and document everyday lived lives. Engages through various practicum and independent research utilizing literary sources. Includes composition of a research proposal and video presentation of independent findings. Cross-listed with GBST 115.
prerequisites_text: GBST 001; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Climate Anxiety and Mental Health
description: Introduces emotional responses to climate change. Identifies the relationships between emotions and mental health outcomes. Explores the roles of race, gender, age, and social marginalization.
prerequisites_text: SEHE 001; Any introductory level environmental studies course; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Gender and Science
description: Focuses on the intersections of Western constructions of gender and scientific knowledge since the sixteenth century. Considers the cultural and political roles of the scientist in terms of gender; the structuring of objectivity and objects of study; the status of scientific knowledge; and the emergence of feminist science studies. Cross-listed with GSST 161. Credit is awarded for one of the following GSST 161, SEHE 123, GSST 161S, or SEHE 123S.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Gender and Science
description: Focuses on the intersections of Western constructions of gender and scientific knowledge since the sixteenth century. Considers the cultural and political roles of the scientist in terms of gender; the structuring of objectivity and objects of study; the status of scientific knowledge; and the emergence of feminist science studies. Cross-listed with GSST 161S. Credit is awarded for one of the following GSST 161S, SEHE 123S, GSST 161, or SEHE 123.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Global Environmental Politics
description: Introduces the study and practice of global environmental politics. Explores major developments in the evolution of international environmental law and policy. Covers ozone depletion, acid rain, marine pollution and whaling, tropical deforestation, overpopulation, and the impact of environmental degradation. Cross-listed with POSC 127. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 127, SEHE 127, POSC 127S, or SEHE 127S.
prerequisites_text: POSC 020 or POSC 020H

subject: SEHE
title: Global Environmental Politics
description: Introduces the study and practice of global environmental politics. Explores the major developments in the evolution of international environmental law and policy. Covers ozone depletion, acid rain, marine pollution and whaling, tropical deforestation, overpopulation, and the impact of environmental degradation. Cross-listed with POSC 127S. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 127S, SEHE 127S, POSC 127, or SEHE 127.
prerequisites_text: POSC 020 or POSC 020H

subject: SEHE
title: Food Justice
description: Explores relations of power, love, desire, hunger, and taste through food and food systems. Considers how food is found, grown, made, bought, sold, shared, and consumed. Covers food apartheid and carceral food systems; metabolic disease; nutrition and nourishment; the right to food; and movements to decolonize food systems.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Environmental Planning & Management
description: Introduces environmental policy and regulation and environmental analysis of issues. Includes conservation, air quality, water quality and access, waste management, disaster planning, risk assessment, and environmental justice.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Global Climate Politics & Policy
description: Explores global climate policies in relation to the Global Climate Politics Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). Addresses the critique of neoliberal climate policies, the politics of climate justice, and low carbon challenges and opportunities.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Community Resilience to Climate Change
description: Introduction to the theory and practices of climate resilience in rural and urban settings around the globe. Examines strategies for assessing climate resilience in different communities and building socially just action plans.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Mindfulness, Climate Action, and Resilience
description: Develops personal and social skills to respond to the climate crisis and interrelated global crises the (polycrisis). Reviews climate science and introduces the polycrisis concept. Develops mindfulness and other contemplative practices. Explores strategies for effective climate communication and action to navigate and build a meaningful future. Cross-listed with GBST 133.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Environmental War Crimes
description: Explores when environmental destruction is considered to be a crime of war. Examines how people work to expose hazards, threats, and hidden burdens associated with environmental legacies of war. Addresses how communities pursue ecological recovery in connection with projects that are established to facilitate peacebuilding, reparations, and transformative justice. Credit is awarded for one of the following SEHE 135 or SEHE 135S.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Environmental Political Thought
description: Addresses various philosophical aspects of the human relationship to the environment from social, political, and economic perspectives. Includes debates related to issues such as how should human beings interact with their environment, as well as the relationship of environmental practice to liberalism, democracy, and capitalism. Cross-listed with POSC 106. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 106, SEHE 136, POSC 106S, or SEHE 136S.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Environmental Justice and Human Rights
description: Examines how notions of justice and human rights have been brought to bear on environmental and sustainability debates. Also examines the theoretical and historical basis of the environmental justice and human rights movements. Topics include local concerns (including “food deserts”) and air pollution, as well as global problems. Cross-listed with POSC 137. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 137, SEHE 137, POSC 137S, or SEHE 137S.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Environmental Justice and Human Rights

subject: SEHE
title: Net Zero Climate, Technology, and Society
description: Examines Net-Zero approaches to climate change from interdisciplinary social science perspectives. Considers carbon management technologies such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and artificial photosynthesis as scientific and social products that embody the promises and ironies of technical solutions to climate change.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Environment, Sustainability, and Society
description: Examines the relationship of human society to the natural environment from a multi disciplinary approach. Considers ways in which values, paradigms, policies, technologies, and their interactions have determined humans’ current unsustainable relationship with the earth. Explores challenges inherent in moving society toward a more environmentally sustainable future. Cross-listed with POSC 139. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 139, SEHE 139, POSC 139S, or SEHE 139S.
prerequisites_text: POSC 017 or POSC 020 or POSC 020H or SOC 020; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Environment, Sustainability, and Society

Explores challenges inherent in moving society toward a more environmentally sustainable future. Cross-listed with POSC 139S. prerequisites_text: POSC 017 or POSC 020 or POSC 020H or SOC 020; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Gender and Climate Change
description: Examines the global social impacts of climate change that are magnified based on existing inequalities. Focuses on the disparity between men and women in their vulnerability and ability to cope with the global phenomenon. Investigates both women as “victims” of global warming and their positive roles in climate change mitigation. Cross-listed with GSST 173.
prerequisites_text: GSST 001 or GSST 001H or GSST 001S; GSST 020 or GSST 020H or GSST 020S or GSST 021

subject: SEHE
title: Feminisms and Environmentalisms
description: Explores women’s and feminist involvement in environmental movements. Examines how gender shapes our relationships with and approaches to environmental problems in the United States and globally. Investigates intersections between feminist concerns (health, reproduction, mothering, gender equity, and social justice) and environmental issues (conservation, pollution and global warming, and sustainability). Cross-listed with GSST 181.
prerequisites_text: GSST 001 or GSST 001H or GSST 001S; GSST 020 or GSST 020H or GSST 020S or GSST 021

subject: SEHE
title: Modern U.S. Consumer Culture
description: Examines the history of mass consumer culture in the United States. Includes the shift from mass production to mass consumption; the grown in advertising and marketing; relationships of race and gender to the market; impacts on built and natural environment; rise of logistics; and waste. Cross-listed with HISA 119. Credit is awarded for one of the following HISA 119, SEHE 144, HISA 119S, or SEHE 144S.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Modern U.S. Consumer Culture
description: Examines the history of mass consumer culture in the United States. Includes the shift from mass production to mass consumption; the grown in advertising and marketing; relationships of race and gender to the market; impacts on built and natural environment; rise of logistics; and waste. Cross-listed with HISA 119S. Credit is awarded for one of the following HISA 119S, SEHE 144S, HISA 119, or SEHE 144.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Intersectionality, Ecology, and Community Design
description: Introduces theoretical underpinnings of ecological utopias and ecotopias. Examines practical aspects of designing these intentional communities focused on sustainability. Includes discussion and critique of proposed ecotopias, analysis of egalitarian economic systems, inclusive and participatory political institutions, and social mores adopted by existing ecovillages and other sustainable intentional communities. Cross-listed with GSST 145.
prerequisites_text: GSST 021

subject: SEHE
title: Intersectionality, Ecology, and Design Science
description: Introduces regenerative design. Emphasizes stability and resiliency of natural systems and intersectional praxis of environmental justice in agricultural and social design. Recognizes sustainable food, water, and shelter requires understanding structures of power that shape and maintain discrimination. Includes agroecology; climate; health; permaculture; intentional communities; social activism; and sustainability. Cross-listed with GSST 148.
prerequisites_text: GSST 145, may be taken concurrently

subject: SEHE
title: Typhoons and Other Disasters
description: Explores how typhoons and other climatological events inform literatures around the Atlantic, the Indian Ocean, and the Pacific. Addresses themes of coloniality, climate change, diaspora, disaster capitalism, and the Anthropocene. Cross-listed with CPLT 184, and SEAS 154.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, senior, or masters; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Special Topics in Environmental Studies
description: Explores specific topics in Environmental Studies. Course content varies and is announced as the course is offered. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Introduction to Epidemiology in Global and Community Health
description: Introduces methods and applications of epidemiology with emphasis on community and global health. Covers concepts including measures of morbidity and mortality, sources of data, study designs, measures of effect, screening, and practical applications. Addresses chronic and infectious disease epidemiology, public health surveillance systems, and procedures involved in investigating an outbreak.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Reproductive Justice
description: Introduces reproductive justice concepts of intersectionality, systemic oppression, the triple pillar approach, and human rights. Analyzes inequality and power in shaping the reproductive contexts of people’s lives, behaviors, and outcomes. Cross-listed with GSST 164.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: SEHE
title: Giving Birth
description: Examines maternal care in the U.S. and worldwide. Analyzes childbirth as a social practice and a cultural construction. Topics include maternal mortality and morbidity, childbirth in different cultures, medicalization of childbirth, alternative and natural birth movements, media representations of childbirth, birth stories, and attitudes toward cesarean section.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Globalizing Roe: the Past, Present, and Future of Abortion Worldwide
description: Surveys the modern history of abortion policy and provision from legal, medical, religious, and public health perspectives. Centers the lived experiences of different individuals in their need to access abortion from a global lens.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Interpersonal Relationship Violence
description: Addresses causes, identification, and prevention of and responses to interpersonal relationship violence, such as family violence and partner violence. Examines theories and research findings for practical field application. Promotes better understanding of this common social problem and prepares for careers involving contact with victims and/or perpetrators of relationship violence. Cross-listed with SOC 144.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better; SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Aging in America
description: Explores special topics in sociology. Segment H may be offered online or in-person. H. Aging In America; M. Geographic Inform Sysms & Mapping In Soc & Other Social Sciences: principles, Techniques, & Research; P. Poverty And Welfare; W. Social Mobility. Cross-listed with SEHE 170 (E-Z), and SOC 183 (E-Z).

subject: SEHE
title: Public Health: Then and Now
description: Surveys the modern history of societal attempts to protect the health of human populations. Focuses on the lived experiences of individuals and cultures in the development of public health globally.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Disease and Society
description: Covers a world history of disease and how it relates to cultural shocks, environmental change, and survival. Evaluates the complex and reciprocal relationship between illness and society, and the historical dynamics around power, race, gender, and class which define disease and shape life chances, medicine and health. Cross-listed with HIST 107.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Eugenics, Disability and Social Justice
description: Examines the intersections of race, disability, and the history and legacy of eugenics. Explores how theories of hereditary fitness shaped categories and experiences of disability, citizenship, reproduction, and race.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Transforming Toxic Jobs: Health and Work in the United States
description: Examines research on health and work including occupational health; how work and employment impact health outcomes and health care; work experiences of health care providers; and the role of policies and organized efforts by workers, their allies, and clients to improve health and well-being at work and in the community. Cross-listed with LABR 175.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Race, Gender, and Health: Diasporic Perspectives
description: Surveys ways in which historical legacies of slavery and racialization affect the health of racialized peoples from a diasporic perspective. Focuses on (but not limited to) the African diaspora in the Americas. Offered online only.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Politics of Global Health
description: Explores the intersection of politics and global health focusing on how political decisions, international relations, and power dynamics shape health outcomes globally. Topics include health governance, policy-making processes, human rights, the role of international organizations, and the impact of political and economic systems on health equity. Cross-listed with POSC 179. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 179, SEHE 179, POSC 179S, or SEHE 179S.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Politics of Global Health
description: Explores the intersection of politics and global health focusing on how political decisions, international relations, and power dynamics shape health outcomes globally. Topics include health governance, policy-making processes, human rights, the role of international organizations, and the impact of political and economic systems on health equity. Cross-listed with POSC 179S. Credit is awarded for one of the following POSC 179S, SEHE 179S, POSC 179, or SEHE 179.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Anthropology of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)
description: A cross-cultural examination of the global Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) epidemic from an anthropological perspective. Cross-listed with ANTH 144I.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Drugs and Culture
description: A cross-cultural examination of drug use and its relation to race, class, gender, morality, laws, and health policy. Cross-listed with ANTH 144K.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Anthropology of Global Health
description: Examines the overlaps, debates, and potential of medical anthropology to address contemporary issues in global health. Focuses on how the historical development, theoretical frameworks, methodological approaches, and ethical debates within medical anthropology can contribute to a just and inclusive version of global health. Cross-listed with ANTH 144N.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Special Topics in Global and Community Health
description: Explores specific topics in Global and Community Health. Topics are announced in the Schedule of Classes. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Special Studies
description: Individual study directed by a faculty member to meet special curricular needs. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 15 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; and consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: SEHE Seminar 1 or
description: Features researchers, community organizers, and professionals in environmental justice and health equity. Provides opportunities to build relationships, network, participate in the SEHE community, and engage in experiential education. Student-organized and faculty-supervised. Topics include Latinx and the environment, climate and health, and SEHE research in progress. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Capstone in Society, Environment & Health Equity
description: Completion of a capstone project that synthesizes and integrates the knowledge and skills obtained throughout the program. Develops skills in the formulation of research questions on topics in Society, Environment, and Health Equity, the use of primary or secondary data, and theory. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: SEHE 101; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: Provides letter grade for written term paper or oral presentation; otherwise, provides only Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grade. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; and consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Group Internship in Labor Studies and Society, Environment, and Health Equity
description: Examines strategies for organizing and advocating for environmental justice and health equity within working class communities generally and within the Inland Empire. Provides hands-on professional experiences with community organizations related to environment and/or health justice. Critically reflects on internship experiences through course readings, in-class discussions, writing assignments, and oral presentations. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units. Cross-listed with LABR 198G.
prerequisites_text: LABR 001 or SEHE 001 or SEHE 002 or SEHE 002S; restricted to major(s) Environmental Studies, Global and Community Health, Labor Studies; completion of internship activities for 3 hours per week before enrollment; and consent of instructor

subject: SEHE
title: Individual Internship in Society, Environment, and Health Equity
description: An individual internship in a community or professional organization in matters relating to environmental studies and/or global and community health to gain professional experience and skills. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; and consent of instructor

subject: SFCS
title: Introduction to Speculative Fiction and Cultures of Science
description: Investigates the relationship among science, technology, medicine, and the genre of science fiction. Emphasizes exchanges between technology and popular culture. Covers fiction by H.G. Wells, Kim Stanley Robinson, and Nancy Kress and critical readings by Steven Shafer, Donna Haraway, and Bruno Latour.

subject: SFCS
title: Reclaiming the Dark: Black Life Is Speculative Fiction
description: Explores alternative states of being, doing, and imagining in, around, and through Black life and culture. Covers writers, artists, and activists such as Octavia Butler, Toni Morrison, Cedric Robinson, the Combahee River Collective, N. K. Jemisin, Adrienne Maree Brown, Kevin Quashie, Nnedi Okorafor, and Ursula K. Le Guin. Cross-listed with BLKS 123.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SFCS
title: Senior Seminar in Speculative Fiction and Cultures of Science
description: Develops skills in the formulation and investigation of research questions in science fiction and technoculture studies. Synthesizes and integrates knowledge and skills obtained in the minor. Includes a major research project and presentations by guest speakers. Speculative Fiction and Cultures of Science Designated Emphasis
prerequisites_text: SFCS 001; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Sociology
description: Covers the basic concepts and theories relating to the study of humans as participants in group life, analysis of culture, social institutions, personality development, and processes of social interaction. Credit is only awarded for one of SOC 001 or SOC 001H.

subject: SOC
title: Honors Introduction to Sociology
description: Honors course corresponding to SOC 001. An in-depth look at concepts and theories relating to the study of humans as participants in group life, analysis of culture, social institutions, personality development, and processes of social interaction. Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC) grading is not available. Credit is awarded for only one of SOC 001 or SOC 001H.
prerequisites_text: admission to University Honors or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: (E-Z) Sociological Foundations
description: Selected topics which promote critical thinking skills essential for success in upper-division sociology courses. For hours and prerequisites, see segment descriptions.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Global Change and Inequality
description: Introduces basic concepts and perspectives in the macro-comparative study of social change and inequality at the global level. Explores causes and consequences of globalization in the arenas of economy, polity, and culture. Emphasizes their impacts upon various forms of inequality worldwide. Credit is awarded for one of the following SOC 002G or SOC 002GS.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Intro Global Chg & Inequality
description: Introduces basic concepts and perspectives in the macro-comparative study of social change and inequality at the global level. Explores causes and consequences of globalization in the arenas of economy, polity, and culture. Emphasizes their impacts upon various forms of inequality worldwide. Credit is awarded for one of the following SOC 002GS or SOC 002G.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Inequality in American Society
description: Examines inequality in modern American society and how gender, race, ethnicity, and social class maintain inequality.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Criminology
description: Analyzes the nature and patterning of criminality focusing on theoretical and methodological issues encountered in research. Examines explanations and crime control policies regarding linkages among social conflicts and inequalities, criminal laws and enforcement practices, and social deviance.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: Racial and Ethnic Issues in American Society
description: Introduces issues and topics associated with racial and ethnic populations in U.S. society. Focuses on social processes that stratify American society by ethnicity and race.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: Social Problems
description: The application of major sociological theories, concepts, and perspectives to the study of social problems in contemporary society. Utilizes an analytical approach.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: Methods of Sociological Inquiry
description: Applies the fundamentals of science to social research. Investigates problems of research design, sampling, measurement of social phenomena, conduct of field studies, and interpretation of qualitative and quantitative social data.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better

subject: SOC
title: Statistical Analysis
description: Covers logical and procedural aspects of the application of statistical methods for data reduction and hypothesis testing in sociology. Includes distributions, tabulations, central tendency, variability, independence, contrasts, correlation and regression, and nonparametrics.
prerequisites_text: SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: American Society
description: Examines the culture and structure of American society. Topics include beliefs, key institutions, community patterns, and systems of inequality.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to the Sociology of Gender
description: Introduces gender as a system of inequality that organizes social life and shapes the distribution of resources, power, and privilege in ways that benefit men over women, including the social construction of gender in everyday life and the gendering of organizations and institutions such as the workplace.

subject: SOC
title: Identity and Society
description: Studies the nature of the self, one’s identities, and their role in social behavior. Examines the processes of self-verification, self-esteem, self-efficacy, and authenticity using social psychological theories. Introduces research methods that allow the study of self and identity processes.

subject: SOC
title: Couples and Families
description: Examines the major trends in marriage, families, and intimate relationships. Focuses on how inequality and diversity affect loving and family relations. Discusses the dynamics of gender inequality among families and couples and how family life is shaped by race and ethnicity, social class, divorce, and sexuality.

subject: SOC
title: Global Political Economy
description: Examines economic and political outcomes and assumes these are mutually constitutive. Focuses on macro-level phenomena and takes the global political economy (as it varies structurally and historically) as its unit of analysis. Applies the scientific method and draws broadly from qualitative and quantitative approaches. Credit is awarded for one of the following SOC 035 or SOC 035S.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better or ECON 101 with a grade of C- or better or PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better or STAT 004 with a grade of C- or better or STAT 008 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Global Political Economy
description: Examines economic and political outcomes and assumes these are mutually constitutive. Focuses on macro-level phenomena and takes the global political economy (as it varies structurally and historically) as its unit of analysis. Applies the scientific method and draws broadly from qualitative and quantitative approaches. Credit is awarded for one of the following SOC 035S or SOC 035.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better or ECON 101 with a grade of C- or better or PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better or STAT 004 with a grade of C- or better or STAT 008 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Multivariate Analysis
description: Involves computer analysis of social and behavioral data using statistical inference, multiple-regression, simulation, and multivariate nonparametric techniques.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: World Inequality
description: Covers the inequalities that manifest between and within countries. Focuses on economic disparities along with inequalities relating to gender dynamics, political representation, and health outcomes. Also explores other dimensions including poverty and inter-generational mobility. Offers a comparative examination of major world regions.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of the Labor Movement
description: Introduces sociological literature related to the labor movement. Provides a comparative and historical overview of research on unions, workers’ centers, and other organizational forms and collective actions through which working-class people have sought to improve their working and living conditions. Credit is awarded for one of the following SOC 112 or SOC 112S.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of the Labor Movement
description: Introduces sociological literature related to the labor movement. Provides a comparative and historical overview of research on unions, workers’ centers, and other organizational forms and collective actions through which working-class people have sought to improve their working and living conditions. Credit is awarded for one of the following SOC 112S or SOC 112.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: Society and Mental Health
description: Covers the social causes and patterns of mental health and disorder in the United States. Examines scientific research on the social determinants of mental health and disorder, inequalities of mental health, and access to mental health care and US mental health care policies.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Social Change
description: A study of patterns of social change, resistance to change, and change-producing processes and agencies.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Sports, Competition, and Society
description: Introduction to the sociology of sports. Surveys competitive sports groups with respect to the functions they perform, the allocation of roles, the use of rewards and punishments, risks and harms that athletes face, and deviant behavior. Offers a historical overview and examines factors that produce elite performance.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Sociological Determinants of Health
description: Introduces the role that social factors play in shaping the occurrence and distribution of disease and death in populations with an emphasis on socioeconomic status, racism, social relationships and social stress. A particular emphasis is placed on sociological origins of health inequalities. Cross-listed with PBPL 127.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Chicano Sociology
description: Analysis of the Mexican experience in U.S. society. Explores the history as a minority; mass immigration in the twentieth century; relationships with American institutions; present socioeconomic status; variations in social status from region to region; political emergence and variations in values; and social relations and integration with non-Mexicans. Cross-listed with ETST 128. Credit is awarded for one of the following SOC 128, ETST 128, ETST 128S, or SOC 128S.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Chicano Sociology
description: Analysis of the Mexican experience in U.S. society. Explores the history as a minority; mass immigration in the twentieth century; relationships with American institutions; present socioeconomic status; variations in social status from region to region; political emergence and variations in values; and social relations and integration with non-Mexicans. Cross-listed with ETST 128S. Credit is awarded for only one of ETST 128/SOC 128 or ETST 128S/SOC 128S.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Race and Ethnic Relations
description: A study of underrepresented racial and ethnic groups. Involves a comparative analysis of the dynamics and consequences of discrimination of racial and ethnic groups in the United States.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: (E-Z) Selected Ethnic Groups
description: In-depth studies of particular ethnic groups in the United States. Treats a specific ethnic group for an entire quarter
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: SOC
title: Inequality and Social Class
description: Covers the analysis of theory and research concerning sources of inequality in the distribution of scarce rewards in societies. Addresses the influence of aspects of social class and processes involving the hierarchical allocation of social groups to positions.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Population
description: Introduction to the study of human populations including theories, concepts, and measures. Explores the social causes and consequences of population trends. Emphasizes population problems including population growth, fertility, migration, and mortality.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Mass Media and Popular Culture
description: A comparative analysis of the television, radio, record, cinema, and journalism industries as social institutions and a discussion of contemporary developments in mass communications theory. A study of the relationship between the social processes of modern society and the content of popular culture. Cross-listed with MCS 139.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: The Sociology of Women
description: Analyzes the role women have played in society emphasizing modern American society. Considers some of the social determinants of women’s positions and the efforts being made to bring about change. Cross-listed with GSST 143.
prerequisites_text: GSST 001 or GSST 001H or GSST 001S or SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of the Family
description: A comparative and historical treatment of the family. Explores major theoretical frameworks developed for conceptualizing the family as a social system within the context of the relation between social structure and family group processes.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Urban Sociology
description: A comparative examination of metropolitan and other urban communities with emphasis on processes of urbanization. Cross-listed with URST 143.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Interpersonal Relationship Violence
description: Addresses causes, identification, and prevention of and responses to interpersonal relationship violence, such as family violence and partner violence. Examines theories and research findings for practical field application. Promotes better understanding of this common social problem and prepares for careers involving contact with victims and/or perpetrators of relationship violence. Cross-listed with SEHE 168.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better; SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Law and Subordination
description: A comparative and historical analysis of subordinated communities and law emphasizing integrating theoretical understanding of racial, class, and gender subordination. Includes field experience working directly with groups that have traditionally lacked equal access to the legal and judicial system. Cross-listed with ETST 145.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing in Ethnic Studies or Sociology; ETST 128/SOC 128 or ETST 128S/SOC128

subject: SOC
title: Gender in Global Perspective
description: Examines gender using global and comparative perspectives. Explores how gender is constructed in different societies. Proves the relationship between gender and globalization. Considers resistance to global processes that create and reinforce gender inequalities.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H or SOC 028

subject: SOC
title: Corrections
description: Involves a review, analysis, and criticism of the major techniques of resocialization of adult and juvenile offenders. Surveys the history, application, and theory of probation, parole, incarceration, and delinquency prevention programs. Discusses the methods involved in evaluating the effectiveness of correctional programs. May provide opportunities for field work.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Organized Crime
description: A review of the operations, structures, history, and theories of syndicated crime in the United States. Emphasizes the implications of organized crime on the development of criminological theory, the operation of formal organizations, and American ethnic relations.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: The Sociology of Economic Organizations
description: Examines how the scope and nature of formal and informal organizations are shaped by sociological processes external to them, such as the influence of governments, institutions, networks, and resources. Illustrates the processes with examples from contemporary United States and from other periods and cultures.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Formal Organizations
description: Examines the structures of formal organizations, the forces that shape them, and the impact they have on their participants, their environments, and one another. Surveys the major classical and contemporary theories of human behavior in organizations.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: SOC
title: (E-Z) Topics in the Sociology of Gender
description: Intensively studies selected topics in the sociology of gender. Course is repeatable to a maximum of units.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H; SOC 028

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Law
description: Introduction to social scientific perspectives and research on the nature, sources, dimensions, and impact of law.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better; SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to major(s) Anthropology/Law & Society, Economics/Law and Society, History/ Law and Society, Law & Society, Philosophy/ Law and Society, Political Sci/Law and Society, Psychology/Law and Society, Sociology, Sociology/Administrative Stds, Sociology/Law and Society

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Education
description: A comparative analysis of educational institutions in complex societies and their relation to a society’s political and economic structure. Examines the school as a societal subsystem consisting of teacher, student, and administrator roles with its own evolving subculture.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Immigration and Society
description: Analyzes the origins of immigration and its nature, patterns, and trends in the twentieth century in Western societies, with special emphasis on the United States. Topics include theories of immigration, causes of immigration, sources of immigrants, immigration laws, reactions to immigrants, and the effects of immigration on the host society.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H

subject: SOC
title: Medical Sociology
description: Introduces key concepts and theories in medical sociology and their application to a variety of health issues. Exemplar topics include social construction of health and illness, medicalization, stigma and labeling, patient-provider interaction, sociology of medical professionals, social determinants of health, and political economy of health. Cross-listed with PBPL 167.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Development of Sociological Theory
description: Covers the emergence of sociology as a systematic discipline. Provides a critical analysis of sociological theory from the nineteenth and early and mid-twentieth centuries.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Modern Sociological Theory
description: An analysis and critical evaluation of sociological theory from 1920 to the present. Explores the growth of current sociological theories and recent trends in conceptual formulations.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Aging and the Life Course
description: Examines aging from a sociological, life-course perspective, emphasizing how social institutions, family roles, and the timing of life events shape inequality and well-being across societies. Explores key debates on caregiving, health, retirement, and population aging in the United States and other countries.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Social Psychology: Sociological Orientation
description: A study of the sociological contributions to theory and research in social psychology. Focuses on the relationship between culture and group life to human behavior and personality.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Socialization and Personality
description: Analyzes socialization from various theoretical perspectives emphasizing the impact of patterns of child rearing on personality development. Provides a historical and cross-cultural treatment focusing on the relation among family structure, social structure, and socialization processes.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Social Roles and Interaction
description: Covers the nature of face-to-face contact between persons in everyday life. Examines the relationship among the social self, social roles, and communication in the day-to-day activities of people in informal groups, closed establishments, and public contacts.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better; SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better, SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better

subject: SOC
title: The Sociology of Work in Organizations
description: Emphasizes the roles of individuals in organizations. Topics include the effects of jobs on workers, long-term trends in the nature of work, and differences in work among major segments of the labor force. Cross-listed with BUS 176.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: (E-Z) Topics in Social Psychology: Sociological Orientation
description: Intensively studies selected topics in social psychology, such as the individual and social change, attribution theory, experimentation in social psychology, exchange and consistency theories in social psychology, and applied social psychology. E. Social Psychology Of Gender; G. Theories Of Interpersonal Behavior.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H; SOC 030

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Emotions
description: Surveys theory and research on emotions. Focuses on sociological and social psychological theories. Also covers evolutionary, biological, and cognitive theories. Studies a range of emotions such as shame and embarrassment; guilt, empathy, and sympathy; jealousy and envy; and anger.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better; SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better; SOC 173 or SOC 174 or SOC 175

subject: SOC
title: Social Movements and Collective Action
description: Examines the emergence and outcomes of collective action and social movements. Considers the conditions under which social movements develop and why they succeed or fail. Utilizes sociological theories to understand collective action and social movements. Includes analysis of the U.S. civil rights movement, feminist movement, and LGBIT movement.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better; SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better; SOC 168 or SOC 169

subject: SOC
title: Deviance and Control
description: Introduction to sociological analysis of deviance as defined by informal and formal processes of social control in varying cultural, legal, and political contexts.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better; SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: World-Systems and Globalization
description: Provides systematic comparisons of societies and world-systems emphasizing changes in the logic of social development. Credit is awarded for one of the following SOC 181 or SOC 181S.
prerequisites_text: SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better, SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or ECON 101 with a grade of C- or better or PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better or STAT 004 with a grade of C- or better or STAT 008 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: World -Systems and Globalization
description: Systematic comparisons of societies and world-systems with emphasis on changes in the logic of social development. Credit is awarded for one of the following SOC 181S or SOC 181.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better, SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better or ECON 101 with a grade of C- or better or PSYC 011 with a grade of C- or better or STAT 004 with a grade of C- or better or STAT 008 with a grade of C- or better; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Urban Problems
description: An interdisciplinary examination of selected urban problems such as civil disorders, transportation, housing, welfare, and planning. Cross-listed with PBPL 182, and URST 182. Credit is awarded for one of the following PBPL 182, SOC 182, URST 182, or PBPL 178.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: SOC
title: (E-Z) Special Topics in Sociology
description: Explores special topics in sociology. Segment H may be offered online or in-person. H. Aging In America; M. Geographic Inform Sysms & Mapping In Soc & Other Social Sciences:principles, Techniques, & Research; P. Poverty And Welfare; W. Social Mobility. Cross-listed with SEHE 170 (E-Z).
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Environmental Sociology
description: A sociological approach to the study of mainstream environmentalism. Addresses societal implications of environmental reform; the nature of distributive impacts (costs and benefits); environmental conflict resolution; land-use decision making; and the placement of noxious facilities in minority, working class, and poor communities.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better, SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better, SOC 005 with a grade of C- or better

subject: SOC
title: Capstone Seminar in Sociology
description: Examines selected topics in Sociology through readings, oral presentations, research and writing, and active participation in seminar discussions. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; restricted to major(s) Sociology; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Globalization and Development
description: Examines the trend, nature, and processes of multidimensional globalization. Explores broad implications of globalization in transforming the world in various aspects. Investigates development issues and how to build a better world.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 with a grade of C- or better or SOC 001H with a grade of C- or better; SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Special Studies
description: Individual study, directed by a faculty member, to meet special curricular needs. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 15 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; consent of instructor and Department Chair

subject: SOC
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: Directed original research. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable.

subject: SOC
title: Individual Internship in Sociology
description: Individual internship in community agencies to observe community processes. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: SOC 004 with a grade of C- or better; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; and consent of instructor

subject: SOC
title: Senior Honors Research
description: Required seminar for all participants in the department’s senior honors program. Must be taken in conjunction with SOC 195, and for a total of three quarters. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: senior standing in Sociology

subject: SPN
title: Elementary Spanish
description: An introduction to the sound system and grammar of Spanish, with attention to the development of the four skills: understanding, speaking, reading, and writing. Classes conducted in Spanish insofar as possible. Audio-lingual and computer-based learning materials are available in the language laboratory.

subject: SPN
title: Elementary Spanish
description: An introduction to the sound system and grammar of Spanish, with attention to the development of the four skills: understanding, speaking, reading, and writing. Classes conducted in Spanish insofar as possible. Audio-lingual and computer-based learning materials are available in the language laboratory.
prerequisites_text: SPN 001 with a grade of “C-” or better or equivalent

subject: SPN
title: Elementary Spanish
description: An introduction to the sound system and grammar of Spanish, with attention to the development of the four skills: understanding, speaking, reading, and writing. Classes conducted in Spanish insofar as possible. Audio-lingual and computer-based learning materials are available in the language laboratory.
prerequisites_text: SPN 002 with a grade of “C-” or better or equivalent

subject: SPN
title: Intermediate Spanish
description: A comprehensive review of the basic grammatical structures of Spanish, vocabulary building, development of conversation and composition skills, and readings of literary and social interest. Classes conducted in Spanish.
prerequisites_text: SPN 003 with a grade of “C-” or better or equivalent

subject: SPN
title: Intermediate Spanish
description: A comprehensive review of the basic grammatical structures of Spanish, vocabulary building, development of conversation and composition skills, and readings of literary and social interest. Classes conducted in Spanish.
prerequisites_text: SPN 004 or equivalent

subject: SPN
title: Intermediate Spanish
description: A comprehensive review of the basic grammatical structures of Spanish, vocabulary building, development of conversation and composition skills, and readings of literary and social interest. Classes conducted in Spanish.
prerequisites_text: SPN 005 or equivalent

subject: SPN
title: Myths and Cultures of Latin America, the Caribbean, and Spain: Transatlantic Currents
description: Examines cultural themes from a transatlantic perspective, through study of literature, film, and visual arts. Topics include chronicles of the conquest, cultures of the baroque, religious traditions and conflicts, the incorporation of popular culture into the literary tradition, contemporary writers, and cinema. Course is conducted in English.

subject: SPN
title: Introduction to Global National Or Regional Media and Cultures
description: Provides a historical overview of a variety of media and cultures specific to a national or regional context. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 10 units. Cross-listed with MCS 046.

subject: SPN
title: Special Studies
description: To be taken with the consent of the Chair of the Department as a means of meeting special curricular problems. Course is repeatable.

subject: SPN
title: Advanced Oral and Written Composition
description: Designed for nonnative speakers to practice speaking and writing in Spanish and to review basic grammar. Emphasis is on composition, editing, and conversation practice. Class is conducted in Spanish. Native speakers without knowledge of college-level grammar should take SPN 109A. Credit is awarded for only one of SPN 101A or SPN 109A.
prerequisites_text: SPN 006

subject: SPN
title: Advanced Oral and Written Composition
description: Designed for nonnative speakers to practice speaking and writing in Spanish and to review basic grammar. Emphasis is on composition, editing, and conversation practice. Class is conducted in Spanish. Native speakers without knowledge of college-level grammar should take SPN 109B. Credit is awarded for only one of SPN 101B or SPN 109B.
prerequisites_text: SPN 101A

subject: SPN
title: Introduction to Spanish Culture
description: Introduction to Spanish culture and civilization from the Roman times to the present. Readings cover history, art, architecture, literatures, and other aspects of culture and civilization. Provides background for courses on the literature of Spain. Course is taught in Spanish.
prerequisites_text: SPN 101B or SPN 109B or equivalent

subject: SPN
title: Introduction to Latin American Culture
description: Introduction to Latin American culture and civilization from pre-Columbian times to the present. Emphasis is on the period from postcolonial independence to the present. Readings cover history, art, architecture, literatures, and other aspects of culture and civilization. Provides background for courses on the literature of Latin America. Course is taught in Spanish.
prerequisites_text: SPN 101B or SPN 109B or equivalent

subject: SPN
title: Spanish Culture and Civilization in Spain
description: Provides intensive study of Spain within its European and New-World contexts. Emphasizes expansion and retraction, as well as the roles of religion and authority. Course taught in Spain in Spanish. Offered in summer only.
prerequisites_text: SPN 101B or SPN 109B; consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: An Introduction to the Study of Spanish and Comparative Linguistics
description: An introduction to the study of Spanish and comparative linguistics. Cross-listed with LNST 104.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: SPN
title: The Phonology of the Spanish Language
description: Provides a descriptive and normative analysis of the phonological system of the Spanish language. Focuses on the phonetic characteristics of contemporary Peninsular and Hispano-American Spanish. Cross-listed with LNST 106.
prerequisites_text: LING 020; SPN 101A, SPN 101B or SPN 109A, SPN 109B; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: Structure of the Spanish Language
description: An introduction to descriptive and applied techniques in the morphosyntax of the Spanish language as found in Spain and Spanish America.
prerequisites_text: SPN 105 with a grade of C- or better or LNST 106 with a grade of C- or better

subject: SPN
title: Spanish in the United States
description: A sociolinguistic study of the Spanish language in the United States. Cross-listed with LNST 107.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: Spanish For the Native Speaker
description: Designed for the native speaker with little or no experience with Spanish grammar and composition. Emphasis is on basic grammar, written accents, orthography, and composition. The class is conducted in Spanish. Credit is awarded for only one of SPN 101A or SPN 109A.
prerequisites_text: a sufficiently high test score on the Spanish placement examination, as determined by the Hispanic Studies faculty

subject: SPN
title: Spanish For the Native Speaker
description: Designed for the native speaker with little or no experience with Spanish grammar and composition. Emphasis is on basic grammar, written accents, orthography, and composition. The class is conducted in Spanish. Credit is awarded for only one of SPN 101B or SPN 109B.
prerequisites_text: SPN 109A

subject: SPN
title: Introduction to Literary Criticism and Analysis
description: An introduction to the methods and techniques of literary analysis. Practice in textual explication, with regular writing assignments.
prerequisites_text: SPN 101A, SPN 101B or SPN 109A, SPN 109B; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: (E-Z) Hispanic Literature in Translation
description: Reading and discussion of works of major Spanish and Spanish American writers. Topic will vary from quarter to quarter. F. Latin American Literature And Film; M. Masterpieces In Spanish American Modernism; Q. <i> Don Quijote; R. Theatre Of Spanish Golden Age; T. Latin American Theatre In Translation; W. Women In Latin American Literature. No Knowledge Of Spanish Required. May Be Counted Toward The Spanish Major With Consent Of Instructor.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: SPN
title: Major Topics in Hispanic Literature
description: Reading and analysis of short texts of authors from Spain, Latin America, and the United States.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Major Topics in Hispanic Literature: Spain
description: Reading and analysis of major texts of authors from Spain.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Major Topics in Hispanic Literature: Latin America
description: Reading and analysis of major texts of authors from Latin America. Cross-listed with LNST 120.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Introduction to Hispanic Cultural Studies
description: Explores the relation between high and popular culture, mass media and subcultures, stories and history, narrative and memory, representation and gender, and technology and the notion of “alterity.”
prerequisites_text: SPN 110.An introduction to cultural studies in Latin America and Spain

subject: SPN
title: Transatlantic Cultural Studies
description: Examines issues such as the legacies of the conquest of America and the slave trade, the nation-building process, theories of mestizaje and transculturation, and transatlantic exile.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110.Offers a transatlantic cultural studies perspective that explores the shared histories of Spain, the Caribbean, and Latin America

subject: SPN
title: (E-Z) Mexican Literary and Cultural Studies
description: Introduces a cultural studies approach to Mexican texts and theorists. Covers issues of nation-building, urbanization, modernization, mestizo imaginaries, representations of violence, gender and nation, indigenismo, race and ethnicity, and borders and migration. Involves reading and discussions of cultural criticism, film, visual culture, and literary texts.
prerequisites_text: vary segment to segment; see individual segments for prerequisite information; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: Mexican Modernities
description: Introduction to the construction of Mexico as a modern nation in popular, mass, and literary cultures from the 19th to mid-20th century. Focuses on the phenomenon of cultural nationalism through the critical discussion of multiple modernities in competition. Analyzes literature, film, and visual culture.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: Global Mexico
description: Continues the study of Mexican cultural development. Focuses on Mexican cultural politics and dynamics from post-1960s up to current times. Analyzes literature, film, and visual culture. Topics may include state violence, neoliberal culture, globalization, indigenous cultural production, migration, border narratives, women’s literature, Nuevo Cine Mexicano, and Mexploitation.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: Nation of Women
description: Introduces the intervention of women as cultural producers throughout Mexican history (17th to the 21st century). Focuses on convergences and divergences between high and low/ popular and mass culture through a gender studies approach. Analyzes literature, film, visual culture, and music.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: (E-Z) Topics in Latin American Film and Media
description: Intensive formal, historical, and theoretical analysis of a theme or issue in Latin American film and media. Cross-listed with LNST 125 (E-Z), and MCS 125 (E-Z).
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: SPN
title: Soccer as Popular Culture in the Global Hispanophone
description: Explores soccer?s cultural, political, and economic roles in society with an emphasis on gender, race, class, national identity, and global and local dynamics, through different cultural theories. Examines literature, film, videogames and other media from Spanish-speaking regions of Europe, Africa, and the Americas.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: Digital Dialectology
description: Contemporary approach to the study of dialects. Examines the uses and projections of a natural language within a digital realm for both digital or analogical materials. Also studies the different interactions between two or more languages or dialects in the digital production of an individual and how those affect communities.
prerequisites_text: SPN 101A, SPN 101B or SPN 109A, SPN 109B; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: (E-Z) Renaissance and Baroque Literatures
description: A concentrated study of a genre, movement, author, or outstanding work of Spanish literature of the sixteenth or seventeenth century. E. Renaissance And Baroque Literature; H. La Celestina; J. Golden Age Of Poetry; P. La Novela Picaresca; T. Spanish Theatre Of The Golden Age.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Cervantes
description: An overview of Cervantes’ texts within their time and place; discussion of his importance in the development of the novel; and close reading of Don Quixote.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Continuities of the Spanish Golden Age in Modern Latin America
description: Introduces the relationship of key golden age and Spanish colonial texts to modern Latin American narrative and essay. Explores questions of literary genealogy as well as issues of cultural identity and the reclamation of history.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Topics in US Latine Theatre and Social Change
description: Examines the formation of LatinÈ, Afro-LatinÈ, Boricua, Hispanic, and Chicanx identities in the United States through theatre?s historical and contemporary influence. Analyzes dramatic texts, scholarship, and performance practices. Explores how U.S. theatre engages questions of race, migration, politics, language, and cultural expression across diverse LatinÈ communities. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: The Generation of 1898
description: A study of the major writers constituting the generation emerging from the national conflict produced in Spain as a consequence of the defeat in the Spanish American War. Readings and discussion of essays, fiction, and poetry of writers such as Unamuno, Baroja, Valle-Incln, Antonio Machado, Azorn, and Benavente.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: (E-Z) Studies in Twentieth-Century Spanish Literature
description: A concentrated study of a genre, period, author, or outstanding work of twentieth-century Spanish literature. E. Spanish Poetry; N. Contemporary Novel In Spain; T. Contemporary Theatre In Spain.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Spanish and Latin American Cultural Studies: Violence and Representation
description: Introduces students to a cultural studies approach to Latin American and Spanish texts and theorists. Covers the Southern Cone dictatorships, post-Franco Spain, and emerging urban imaginaries. Involves readings and discussions of cultural criticism, films, urban chronicles, and literary texts.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: (E-Z) Studies in Nineteenth-and Twentieth-Century Latin American Literature
description: A concentrated study of a genre, movement, author, or outstanding work of Latin American literature. E. Short Story; F. Censorship, Self-censorship, Anti-censorship; L. Nineteenth-century Latin American Novel; M. Twentieth-century Latin American Novel; N. Mexican Novel; P. Poetry; R. Voyages Through Latin America: A Cultural And Literary Vision; T. Spanish American Theatre.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Reel to Real: Latin American Film and Social Change
description: Introduces Latin American film as it articulates with contemporary history and current events. Cross-listed with MCS 171.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: The Testimonio and Cultural History
description: Explores the relation between the testimonial genre and the emergence of Latin American cultural studies, subaltern studies, and postcolonial studies. Involves readings and discussions of a representative sample of testimonial literature and criticism.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Human and Nonhuman: Decolonial and Audiovisual Perspectives On Life On A Diminished Planet
description: A study of decolonial and audiovisual approaches to conceiving the human/ nonhuman from Latin American perspectives. Examines issues of extractivism, environmental justice, the debate on living well, the relation between human and nonhuman, and how films illustrate these issues.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: SPN
title: Gender, Media, and Latin America
description: Explores the way Latin Americans have thought of and represented gender across a variety of media including essays, film, novel, short story, and performance. Compares the possibilities and limitations of these media for representing gender in the Latin American context. Cross-listed with MCS 179, LNST 109, and GSST 179.
prerequisites_text: MCS 020 or upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: Survey of Spanish Literature, Middle Ages-1699
description: Survey of literary movements and trends and major writers of medieval and Golden Age Spanish literature. Covers writers such as Cervantes, Lope de Vega, Tirso de Molina, Quevedo, and Gngora.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Survey of Spanish Literature, 1700-Present
description: Survey of literary movements and trends and major writers of eighteenth-, nineteenth-, and twentieth-century Spanish literature. Readings in fiction, poetry, drama, and essay. Covers writers such as Moratin, Becquer, Galdos, Larra, Azorin, and Garcia Lorca.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Survey of Spanish American Literature, Discovery to Modernismo
description: Survey of literary movements and trends and major Spanish American writers from the colonial period to Modernismo. Readings are in fiction, poetry, drama, and essay. Covers writers such as Sor Juana Ines de la Cruz, Echeverria, Sarmiento, and Marti.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Survey of Spanish American Literature, Modernismo to the Present
description: Survey of literary movements and trends and major Spanish American writers from Modernismo to the present. Readings are in fiction, poetry, drama, and essay. Covers writers such as Dario, Azuela, Vallejo, Huidobro, Garcia Marquez, Fuentes, Paz, Buenaventura, and Elena Poniatowska.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Imagining the Nation: Film and Media in Latin America
description: Studies the role of media and film in creating a national imaginary in Latin America. Focuses on one region or nation--such as the Andes, the Caribbean, Mexico, Argentina, or Chile--and relates the local history to the global context. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units. Cross-listed with LNST 105.
prerequisites_text: MCS 020; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: Latin American Science Fiction
description: Focuses on intersections between literature and scientific discourse. Considers how popular notions of science inform the production and reading of the literary text. Topics may include the function of power in scientific discourse, the politics of alternative universes, and science and gender. Course is repeatable as content changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Interdisciplinary Studies: the Hispanic World
description: Includes reading, research, and discussion on particular problems related to Spain and Latin America that lend themselves to interdisciplinary analysis. Course is repeatable as topics change to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110

subject: SPN
title: Special Studies
description: Individual study, directed by a faculty member, to meet special curricular needs. Course is repeatable.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110; consent of Department Chair

subject: SPN
title: Tutorial Activities
description: Under faculty supervision, students conduct discussion sections of elementary Spanish courses. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 6 units.
prerequisites_text: SPN 110; senior standing; consent of Department Chair

subject: SPN
title: Senior Seminar in the Literatures and Cultures of the Hispanic World
description: Introduction to research methods and documentation necessary for completion of a long final project. Specific topics vary depending on the instructor. Intended for Spanish majors. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of senior; or consent of instructor

subject: SPN
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: Directed original research. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: SPN 101A, SPN 101B or SPN 109A, SPN 109B; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; and consent of instructor

subject: STAT
title: Elements of Data Science
description: Explores basic concepts, algorithms, and techniques of data science with simulation and data visualization. Topics include summarizing and visualizing data using R or Python, causality, randomness, decision making in the presence of uncertainty, prediction, and classification. Credit is awarded for one of the following STAT 004, SEHE 005, or STAT 005. Credit is not awarded for STAT 004 if it has already been awarded for STAT 008, STAT 010, or STAT 011.

subject: STAT
title: Statistics, Health, and Society
description: An introduction to statistics using social, health, and environmental applications. Topics include descriptive statistics; simple linear regression and correlation; probability; discrete and continuous distributions; confidence intervals; hypothesis testing; and one-way analysis of variance. Cross-listed with SEHE 005. Credit is awarded for one of the following SEHE 005, STAT 005, or STAT 004. Credit is not awarded for STAT 005 or SEHE 005 if already awarded to STAT 008, STAT 010, or STAT 011

subject: STAT
title: Statistics For Business
description: An introduction to statistics using business applications. Topics include descriptive statistics; probability; discrete and continuous distributions; Bayes’ theorem; random variables; estimation and confidence intervals; hypothesis testing; and simple linear regression. Recommended for Business majors. Credit is awarded for one of the following STAT 008 or STAT 010.
prerequisites_text: MATH 004 or MATH 005A or MATH 006B or MATH 005B, may be taken concurrently or MATH 007A, may be taken concurrently or MATH 009A, may be taken concurrently or MATH 09HA, may be taken concurrently or MATH 022, may be taken concurrently; or equivalent

subject: STAT
title: Introduction to Statistics
description: A general introduction to descriptive and inferential statistics. Topics include histograms; descriptive statistics; probability; normal and binomial distributions; sampling distributions; hypothesis testing; and confidence intervals. Recommended for non-Business majors. Credit is awarded for one of the following STAT 010 or STAT 008.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005A or MATH 006B or MATH 005B, may be taken concurrently or MATH 007A, may be taken concurrently or MATH 009A, may be taken concurrently or MATH 09HA, may be taken concurrently

subject: STAT
title: Introduction to Statistical Modeling
description: Topics include linear regression, correlation, analysis of variance, and simple experimental designs.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 with a grade of C- or better or STAT 010 with a grade of C- or better

subject: STAT
title: Decision Analysis and Management Science
description: A survey of deterministic and probabilistic models for decision making.
