Topics include linear programming and extensions, networks, dynamic programming, decision trees, queuing models, and simulation. Explores the application of these models in decision making. Cross-listed with BUS 104.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010; or equivalents; or consent of instructor

subject: STAT
title: Introduction to Statistical Computing With R
description: An introduction to the R programing language. Topics include data management, basic statistical analysis and graphics, use of functions and packages, simple programming, and reproducible work.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010; or equivalent

subject: STAT
title: Data Science Ethics
description: Covers ethics specifically related to data science. Topics include data privacy; data curation and storage; discrimination and bias arising in the machine learning process; statistical topics such as generalization, causality, curse of dimensionality, and sampling bias; data communication; and strategies for conceptualizing, measuring, and mitigating problems in data-driven decision-making. Cross-listed with CS 108. Credit is awarded for one of the following CS 108, STAT 108, CS 212, or STAT 212.
prerequisites_text: CS 105 or STAT 107 or CS 171; or consent of instructor

subject: STAT
title: Biostatistical Methods in Life Sciences
description: Provides undergraduate majors or those interested in life sciences with statistical tools for analyzing different types of data frequently encountered in life sciences. Emphasizes applications of methodology including contingency table analysis, linear regression and ANOVA, maximum likelihood method and the estimation-maximization algorithm, logistic regression, Poisson regression, and survival analysis.
prerequisites_text: STAT 011 or STAT 107; or equivalent

subject: STAT
title: Introduction to Quality Improvements
description: Explores Deming’s 14 points for management, graphical methods, fishbone diagram, Pareto analysis, control charts for attributes and variables, cusum and moving average charts, and process-capability. Also covers economic design, acceptance sampling, Taguchi method, parameter design, tolerance design, reliability, hazard rate, censoring, and accelerated life testing. Cross-listed with BUS 127.
prerequisites_text: STAT 008 or STAT 010; or ECON 101

subject: STAT
title: Sampling Surveys
description: Covers simple random sampling, stratified sampling, cluster sampling, and ratio and regression estimates. Also explores random response, capture-recapture, and jack-knife techniques.
prerequisites_text: STAT 011 or STAT 107; or equivalent

subject: STAT
title: Nonparametric Techniques
description: Covers randomization tests, rank tests, methods of association, and distribution-free tests.
prerequisites_text: STAT 011 or STAT 107; or equivalent

subject: STAT
title: Statistical Forecasting Techniques
description: Topics include exponential smoothing, simple and multiple regression analysis, time series, trend analysis, and seasonal analysis.
prerequisites_text: STAT 156A or STAT 160A

subject: STAT
title: Spatial Statistics
description: An introduction to spatial statistics. Topics include spatial homogeneity, heterogeneity, autocorrelation, sampling, interpolation techniques, spatial centrality, dispersion metrics, hot-spot analysis, and spatial regression.
prerequisites_text: STAT 107; or consent of instructor

subject: STAT
title: Probability and Statistics For Science and Engineering
description: Covers sample spaces and probability; random variables and probability distributions; elements of statistical inference; and testing and estimation. Also addresses selected topics in multivariate distributions and introduces stochastic processes. Credit is not awarded for STAT 155 if it has already been awarded for STAT 156A or STAT 160A.
prerequisites_text: MATH 009C, may be taken concurrently or MATH 09HC, may be taken concurrently or MATH 005C, may be taken concurrently

subject: STAT
title: Mathematical Statistics With Applications For Data Science I
description: Introduction to frequentist probability concepts, random variables, and their distributions. Discusses key theorems and inequalities in probability theory. Introduces frequentist methods of point and interval estimation. Credit is awarded for one of the following STAT 156A or STAT 160A.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C or MATH 009C, may be taken concurrently or MATH 09HC, may be taken concurrently

subject: STAT
title: Mathematical Statistics With Applications For Data Science 2
description: Topics include illustrative applications of Frequentist theory to linear regression; logistic regression and ANOVA; introduction to Bayes’ rule, Bayesian probability concepts, and credible intervals; analysis of contingency tables; applications of sequential statistics; and methods for observational studies and missing data. Credit is awarded for one of the following STAT 156B or STAT 160B.
prerequisites_text: STAT 156A with a grade of C- or better

subject: STAT
title: Statistical Computing With Sas
description: Covers statistical computing with SAS. Topics include syntax and programming logic; data management; basic statistical analysis; statistical graphics; regression; and macros.
prerequisites_text: STAT 010 with a grade of C- or better; CS 009A with a grade of C- or better or CS 010A with a grade of C- or better or STAT 107 with a grade of C- or better; or equivalent

subject: STAT
title: Elements of Probability and Statistical Theory
description: Topics include statistical regularity, probability spaces, fundamental theorems in discrete probability, Bayes’ theorem, random variables, densities and distribution functions, and continuous distributions. Credit is awarded for one of the following STAT 160A or STAT 156A.
prerequisites_text: MATH 005C or MATH 009C, may be taken concurrently or MATH 09HC, may be taken concurrently

subject: STAT
title: Elements of Probability and Statistical Theory
description: Topics include transformations of random variables and central limit theorem, distributions of sample statistics, statistical inference, and estimation. Credit is awarded for one of the following STAT 160B or STAT 156B.
prerequisites_text: STAT 160A with a grade of C- or better

subject: STAT
title: Elements of Probability and Statistical Theory
description: Topics include hypothesis testing, chi-square tests, and nonparametric methods.
prerequisites_text: STAT 160B with a grade of “C-” or better

subject: STAT
title: Introduction to Probability Models
description: Covers compound distributions, branching processes, and random walk. Explores continuous time models such as Poisson process and queuing models. Examines the Markov property and introduces Markov chains. Also covers simple time series models.
prerequisites_text: STAT 156B with a grade of C- or better or STAT 160B with a grade of C- or better

subject: STAT
title: Introduction to Data Science
description: Introduction to data science using the R programming language. Topics include big data management, visualization and analytical skills, unsupervised and supervised statistical learning methods, and real-world data science application examples.
prerequisites_text: STAT 107 with a grade of C- or better; CS 009A with a grade of C- or better or CS 010A with a grade of C- or better

subject: STAT
title: Design of Experiments
description: Topics include principles of design; completely randomized designs; and one-way analysis of variance. Covers complete block designs and two-way analysis of variance; multiple comparisons; and complete factorial experiments. Explores fixed, random, and mixed models; split-plot designs; nested designs; analysis of covariance; sample size determination; and power analysis.
prerequisites_text: STAT 107; STAT 156B or STAT 160B; or equivalent

subject: STAT
title: Regression Analysis
description: Topics include simple and multiple linear regression, scatter-plots, and point and interval estimation. Addresses prediction, testing, calibration, interpretation, and practical applications of multiple regression. Explores simple, partial, and multiple correlation; variable selection methods; diagnostic procedures; and regression for longitudinal data.
prerequisites_text: STAT 107; STAT 156B or STAT 160B; or equivalent

subject: STAT
title: General Statistical Models
description: Covers generalized linear models and least squares, analysis of covariance, nonlinear regression, and nonlinear least squares. Explores regression methods for discrete data including loglinear models, logistic regression, and discriminant analysis. Also addresses regression methods for life data, the Cox survival model, the Kaplan-Meier estimation, and the Mantel-Haenszel test.
prerequisites_text: STAT 170

subject: STAT
title: Statistical Consulting
description: Introduces the statistical consulting process. Promotes consulting skills including developing effective communication skills, applying statistical methodology to client projects, and learning how to manage time and resources in a consulting environment. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: STAT 169; STAT 170; STAT 171; restricted to class level standing of senior

subject: STAT
title: Research For Undergraduates
description: An introduction to research in Statistics. Requires a research project completed under the supervision of a Statistics faculty member or a group of faculty members. Students who submit a term paper receive a letter grade; other students receive a Satisfactory (S) No Credit (NC) grade. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; and consent of instructor

subject: STAT
title: Individual Internship in Statistics
description: An internship to provide statistical field experience in governmental, industrial, or research units. Projects must be approved by the Statistics Department and the head of the unit in which the internship is to be carried out. Requires a written report. Total credit toward graduation may not exceed 12 units. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; and consent of instructor

subject: STAT
title: Senior Honors Research
description: Senior standing with major concentration in statistics and with consent of instructor. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 10 units.
prerequisites_text: senior standing with major concentration in statistics and with consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to Acting
description: Through exercises, lectures, videos, and on-site visits, explores the work of actors and their collaborations with other artists in historical and contemporary settings. Recommended for nonmajors.
prerequisites_text: none Introduction to acting in theatre, film, television, and performance art

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to Latinx Cultural Production On Stage and Screen
description: An introduction to Latino theatre and film from 1965 to the present. Examines the major works of playwrights and important films and videos.

subject: TFDP
title: Shakespeare in Performance
description: A study of contemporary Shakespearean production on stage and film. Considers the problems of adapting the text, creating visual elements, speaking the language, and performing the characters. Explores a wide range of performance styles.

subject: TFDP
title: A Study of Technical Production Practices,equipment and Architecture For Film and Digital Media
description: A study of technical production practices, equipment, and architecture for Film and Digital Media. Explores the application of production practices and principles of film and media production.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of freshman, or sophomore; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: A Study of Technical Production Practices,equipment and Architecture For Theatre and Live Action
description: A study of technical production practices, equipment, and architecture for theatre and live action. Explores the application of production practices and principles of stagecraft in relation to scenic, costume, lighting, sound, and projection design.

subject: TFDP
title: Costume Construction
description: A theoretical and practical study of theatrical costume production. Topics include draping and flat pattern development, fabric, fitting, and sewing techniques. Costume projects are required. Sewing skills helpful but not essential.

subject: TFDP
title: Makeup For Theatre, Film, and Television
description: A study of the theory and practice of makeup for theatre, film, and television. Includes demonstrations by industry professionals.

subject: TFDP
title: Public Speaking
description: Covers the principles and practice of effective speech composition and delivery. Provides the communicative skills essential in professional careers and community life. Credit is awarded for one of the following TFDP 050 or TFDP 050S.

subject: TFDP
title: Public Speaking
description: Covers the principles and practice of effective speech composition and delivery. Provides the communicative skills essential in professional careers and community life. Credit is awarded for one of the following TFDP 050S or TFDP 050.

subject: TFDP
title: Screenwriting: How Movies Work
description: An Introduction to writing for stage and screen. Addresses structure, character, dialogue, theme, and story. Cross-listed with CRWT 066, and MCS 066.

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to Playwriting and Screenwriting
description: An introduction to writing for stage and screen. Addresses structure, character, dialogue, theme, and story.
prerequisites_text: CRWT 066/ MCS 066/TFDP 066 with a grade of “C-” or better or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to the Theatre Department
description: An introduction to the faculty and areas of study offered by the Department of Theatre. Promotes a better understanding of undergraduate opportunities, graduate training, and careers in the entertainment industry. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).

subject: TFDP
title: Play Analysis
description: In-depth analysis of selected plays. Explores structure, character, and imagery.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to Design
description: A comprehensive introduction to design for theatre, film, and television. Topics include design principles and practice of set, costume, and lighting. Includes the history of design and conceptual approaches and research.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 024; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to Dramaturgy
description: Introduction to theatre dramaturgy, script analysis and advising for production. Topics include analyzing a dramatic text, researching production histories, preparing research materials for a production, season planning, lobby display, and working with new work.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 100; upper-division standing

subject: TFDP
title: Acting: the Process
description: A comprehensive introduction to the process of acting. Topics include imagination, communication, and the psychophysical development of the actor’s instrument. Explores basic approaches to the acting process through monologues and introductory scene study.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 099 or MCS 001; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Acting: Fundamentals
description: A study of the acting fundamentals and the actor’s basic tool kit. Topics include text analysis, actions and activities, problems and objectives, and audition technique. Explores basic approaches to characterization through audition practice, monologues, and scene study using methods such as Stanislavsky’s “system,” the American Method, and Meisner Technique.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 109 with a grade of D or better; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Acting: Techniques
description: An examination of acting techniques from various global practitioners. Topics include advanced psychophysical work, advanced text analysis, the architecture of the stage space, and the actor-audience relationship in dynamic storytelling. Explores analysis and performance of scenes from a range of world dramas.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 110A; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Advanced Acting: Shakespeare and the Power of Language
description: Advanced scene study in classic theatre to develop the actor’s skills with heightened language. Emphasizes works by Shakespeare. Topics include performance styles, working on text and voice, and the power of images.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 110B; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Advanced Acting: Acting With Facts and Playing With the Truth
description: Advanced scene study in world theatre of the realistic mode to expand the actor’s emotional repertoire, character range, and worldview. Includes in text and subtext, performance styles in fact-based and verbatim dramas, and the nature of truth in acting. Explores realism from Anton Chekhov to Anna Deavere Smith.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 110B; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Advanced Acting: Acting For the Camera
description: A practical exploration of acting for camera. Topics include technicalities of performing for screen, adaptation of interpretative acting tools to performance from stage to screen, and auditioning for camera. Explores analysis of film/television scripts, recorded performance to camera, and analysis of iconic screen performances.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 110B; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Advanced Acting: the Business of Acting
description: Examines professional strategies of the working actor. Topics include analysis of the casting process, portfolio creation (headshot, resume, reel), audition techniques, and business strategies and protocols.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 111A or TFDP 111B or TFDP 111C; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: (E-Z)
description: Study in voice, vocal performance techniques, and theories for actors.

subject: TFDP
title: Dramatic Interpretation
description: Vocal presentation of text. Includes the use of various literary forms emphasizing rhythm, tonality, diction, imagery, focus, and phrasing as implements to convey the text, character, actions, and intentions.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Voice and Diction
description: The study of vocal production for actors. Focuses on breathing, relaxation, articulation, communication, and projection, enabling the actor to fill a theatre with clear, understandable speech. Also examines the International Phonetic Alphabet to assist in pronunciation.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: (E-Z) Movement For Actors and Performers
description: A study of movement techniques and theories for actors and performers. F. Stage Combat; M. Mime; N. Nonverbal Theatre.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: TFDP
title: Acting For Writers
description: Examines the theory and practice of acting to enable writers to better understand how language reflects character, as well as how actors turn the written word into spoken language. Includes text work and improvisation. Credit is awarded for one of the following TFDP 114 or CWPA 214.
prerequisites_text: CRWT 164C or TFDP 164C or TFDP 166C; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Hip Hop Theatre
description: Provides tools to create new work by using elements of hip hop culture such as Graffiti Art, Emceein’ (rappin’), DeeJayin’ and Breakdancin’ as primary means of storytelling on stage. Explores theoretical aspects of hip hop culture and a working knowledge of playwriting, acting, directing, and design.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Directing For the Screen
description: An introduction to the study of film directing from the perspective of film analysis and filmmaking practice. Explores the job of the director in the realms directors control: narrative form, mise-en-scene, cinematography, sound, and editing.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 144; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Literature and History of the Theatre: the Classical Period Through the Italian Renaissance
description: Examines the literature and history of the theatre from the classical period through the Italian Renaissance. Focuses on analysis of representative plays, theatrical architecture, and production modes.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Literature and History of the Theatre: the Elizabethan Period Through the Nineteenth-Century
description: Examines the literature and history of the theatre from the Elizabethan period through the nineteenth century. Focuses on analysis of representative plays, theatrical architecture, and production modes.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Dramaturgy: World of the Play
description: A study of a significant play in the context of the social, intellectual, and artistic movements of its time. Offered simultaneously with the Theatre Department’s production of the play. May also consider related works and writings. Course is repeatable as content changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Theatre For Social Change
description: Examines theatre for social change as created by grassroots theatrical organizations. Focuses on how community-based theatre groups develop works and how theatre in public or private spaces redefines traditional theatre practices.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Asian/American Theatre: Disorienting the Stage
description: An introduction to the histories, theories and texts of Asian/American theatre. Explores themes such as Orientalism, imperialism, and immigration.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: American Theatre, 1900- 1945
description: Examination of the major American playwrights, theatrical figures, and movements from 1900 through World War II.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: American Theatre, 1945-Present
description: Examination of the major American playwrights, theatrical figures, and movements from World War II to the present.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: (E-Z) History of the Theatre
description: A study of the plays, playhouses, and players of the following theatrical eras: E. Classical Theatre; F. Medieval Theatre; G. Renaissance Theatre; I. Romantic Theatre; J. Realistic Theatre; K. Contemporary Theatre; M. American Theatre; N. Neo-classic Theatre; P. American Theatre And Drama Of The Great Depression; S. American Musical Theatre; T. Asian Theatre; X. Experimental Theatre In America. Course is repeatable.

subject: TFDP
title: History of Dress
description: A study of the psychological, sociological, and economic history of fashion and dress from 4000 B.C. to A.D. 1700.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: History of Dress
description: A study of the psychological, sociological, and economic history of fashion and dress from A.D. 1700 to the present.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Theories of the Modern Theatre
description: Examines the major theories underlying twentieth-century theatre practice. Special attention is paid to the ideas of important theatre artists such as Konstantin Stanislavsky, E. Gordon Craig, Antonin Artaud, and Bertolt Brecht.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Seminar On the Life and Work of Tomas Rivera
description: Introduction to the life and work of Tomas Rivera, UCR Chancellor (1979-1984) and foundational Chicana/o author. Explores the breadth of Rivera’s writing (novel, poems, short stories, speeches) and his contributions through administrative leadership in higher education as well as personal papers in the UCR Tomas Rivera Archives in Special Collections.
prerequisites_text: consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: History of the Modern Theatre: Nineteenth-Century - Present
description: Introduces the main developments in modern theatre from a global perspective. Explores major historical developments in theatre as a response to globalization, colonization, feminism, and other cultural developments. Course is repeatable as content changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing

subject: TFDP
title: Producing Short Episodic Content A
description: Introduces techniques involved in producing a pilot for a short episodic content series in video. Reviews the entire production cycle for a pilot including casting and location scouting, working with actors, shooting, and editing.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 144 or TFDP 153B or TFDP 156A or TFDP 156B; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Producing Short Episodic Content B
description: Covers techniques and skills needed for producing episodes of a short episodic content series in video. Reviews the entire production cycle for two episodes including producing, directing, photographing, and editing.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 144 or TFDP 153B or TFDP 156A or TFDP 156B; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Sound Design For Theatre, Film, and Television
description: Introduces sound design for theatre, film, and television productions. Covers topics such as critical listening, psycho acoustics, computer editing, sound recording and processing, and copyright laws pertaining to sampling.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 101; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Lighting Design For Theatre, Film, and Television
description: A study of design, technical production practices, and equipment for lighting in theatre, film, and television. Explores the application of production practices and principles of designing light for entertainment. Develops skills associated with the creation and execution of a lighting design.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 101; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Scene Design For Theatre, Film, and Television
description: An introduction to basic skills and techniques for theatre design and to issues of contemporary design for theatre, film, and television. Topics include sketching, rendering, drafting, and model making.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 101; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Costume Design For Theatre, Film, and Television
description: A study of theory, principles, and practice of costume design for theatre, film, and television.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 101; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: History of Theatre Design
description: Explores the development of scenic, costume, lighting, and sound design in theatre. Examines different styles of theatrical aesthetics throughout history focusing on Western culture.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Art Direction For Film and Television
description: An introduction to the design principles and methods professional art directors use in the entertainment industry. Projects related to feature film and television design explore current methods of presentation and composition for the film and television camera.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 101 or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: The Art of Film
description: An introduction to the analysis of cinema. Topics include film forms, genres, and Mise-en-Scene. Examines how creative choices by filmmakers affect what viewers experience and how they respond. Develops the skills of watching and listening closely that are necessary to become informed filmmakers.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 155; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Scene Painting
description: Explores and applies techniques and materials used to create the various elements of scene design. Includes methods of set preparation, coating, mixing, palette preparation, spraying, transfer, texturing, finishing, and wall papering.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 024; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Directing Actors For the Screen
description: Develops skills needed to direct actors for the screen. Topics include communication, breaking down screenplays, identifying characters’ objectives and arcs, and blocking actors for the camera. Studies giving directions using action verbs, facts, imagination, and physical activities. Students will learn by directing and acting in scenes.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 155; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Computer Aided Design For Theatre, Film, and Television
description: Explores the established computer-aided design (CAD) applications in the design industry including 3DS Studio Max, Adobe Photoshop, and Vectorworks.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 101 or TFDP 024

subject: TFDP
title: Stage Management
description: Explores the role and function of the stage manager in theatrical production. Provides basic skills to work in the field of stage management emphasizing organization, documentation, and dissemination of information.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 099

subject: TFDP
title: Directing
description: Introduces directing for theater and film. Includes analyzing texts, preparing a rehearsal schedule, communicating with actors and designers, blocking scenes, utilizing space and lighting, and introducing concepts for directing projects. Also proposes various theories of directing.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 099; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Directing
description: An examination of the rehearsal process focusing on combining the elements of text, acting, and design.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 150A or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Transition to the Film Industry
description: Involves creating a plan for transition into professional life after college. Determines short- and long-term career and academic goals and develops strategies to achieve them. Explores diverse avenues to enter the film industry.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 155; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Advanced Public Speaking
description: An intense practice-based laboratory in communication, rhetoric, and delivery. Designed to strengthen practical and professional skills in conducting research, crafting presentations for diverse interdisciplinary audiences, and dynamic delivery. Includes visual rhetoric, online presentations, argument, debate, and preparation for the written materials and impromptu speech necessary to thrive in job interviews.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 050 or TFDP 050S; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to Cinematography
description: Introduces basic operations and skills of cameras, lighting, and lenses. Emphasizes aesthetics of cinematography including image control through lighting, exposure, and film equipment.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 024; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Advanced Cinematography
description: Addresses visual perception through practice with a variety of lenses, light fixtures, cameras, and formats. Focuses on cinematic thought in both documentary and dramatic work. Includes practical film exercises designed to develop more creative and personal expression.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 153A; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to Filmmaking
description: Introduces filmmaking including the basic elements of film sets, functions and terminology of various roles on a film set, and mechanics of the film industry.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 024; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to Digital Film Production
description: Introduces the skills needed for making a narrative film. Includes examining and utilizing scripts, cameras, lighting, sound, and editing. Also includes filmmaking projects.
prerequisites_text: CRWT 066 or MCS 066 or TFDP 066: TFDP 024; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Digital Film Production
description: Examines the techniques of narrative filmmaking and directing for the camera. Emphasizes the working relationship with actors.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 153A with a grade of C- or better or TFDP 155; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Digital Film Production
description: Examines the techniques of production and postproduction for narrative filmmaking. Emphasizes sound and editing processes.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 155 or TFDP 156A

subject: TFDP
title: Introduction to Film Editing
description: Examines the art and craft of editing the narrative film. Includes hands-on work in editing a montage, a short documentary, and a narrative fiction scene.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 153A or TFDP 154 or TFDP 155; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Storytelling of Witness: Introduction to Documentary Theatre and Film
description: Introduces vocabulary, themes, genres, and methods of documentary storytelling in theater and film. Explores the evolution of documentary storytelling focusing on signature works by noted playwrights and filmmakers. Addresses craft, voice, and legacy of documentary storytelling from strictly recorded (verite, interview) to creatively devised narratives (post-event recreation, hybrid forms).
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Documentary Production
description: Creation of independent, low-budget documentaries through hands-on experience in pre-production, production, and post-production. Presents works in progress and finished pieces throughout the quarter. Considers peer feedback.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 153A or TFDP 154 or TFDP 155; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: The Filmmaker’s Life
description: An overview of the various jobs (and their requirements) connected to the process of creating products for film and television entities.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: African American Drama
description: Examines the major African American plays and playwrights from the 1800s to the present.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Writing the Half-Hour Television Comedy
description: Introduction to the style, form, content, and creation of a half-hour television comedy series.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 166A or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Writing the Short Film
description: Addresses the mechanical and creative components of crafting a screenplay for a short film.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 066 or CRWT 066 or MCS 066, TFDP 153A or TFDP 154; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Beginning Playwriting
description: Seminar in the practice of playwriting centering on the construction of a plot. Cross-listed with CRWT 164A.
prerequisites_text: CRWT 056 or TFDP 100 or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Intermediate Playwriting
description: Seminar in the practice of playwriting. Revisions of works in progress emphasizing character development and techniques for writing dialogue. Cross-listed with CRWT 164B.
prerequisites_text: CRWT 164A/TFDP 164A

subject: TFDP
title: Advanced Playwriting
description: Seminar in the practice of playwriting. Includes playwrights’ participation in staged readings of their work. With consent of instructor, course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units. Cross-listed with CRWT 164C.
prerequisites_text: CRWT 164B/TFDP 164B

subject: TFDP
title: Creating the Webseries
description: An introduction to the demands and processes of creating and writing a web series. Designed to produce a full season of fifteen to twenty five-minute episodes. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 166B; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Screenwriting: Introduction
description: An introduction to the process and craft of screenwriting. Includes developing and presenting an idea for a screenplay created over the breadth of this three-part series TFDP 166A, TFDP 166B, TFDP 166C. TFDP 166A includes creation of an outline for the entire screenplay and the writing of the first act.
prerequisites_text: CRWT 066 or MCS 066 or TFDP 066, TFDP 020; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Screenwriting: Outline to First Draft
description: An introduction to the process and craft of screenwriting. Continues to develop the idea of the screenplay began in TFDP 166A. Utilizes the previously created outline and first act to write Act 2 and Act 3 and produce a complete rough draft.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 166A; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Screenwriting: Rewrites and Writing For Television
description: An introduction to the process and craft of screenwriting. Includes a page one rewrite of the screenplay developed in TFDP 166A and TFDP 166B. Teaches the rewriting process utilizing notes provided in TFDP 166A and TFDP 166B and instructor input to further develop the original screenplay. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 166B; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Writing For Television: Creating the One-Hour Series Drama
description: Introduces the craft of writing for television focusing on production of original work. Includes writing a one-hour pilot, creating series guidelines, and formulating work leading to a 13-episode series. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 12 units.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Rewriting the Script
description: Covers rewriting a full-length script (screenplay or play). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units. Credit is awarded for only one of CWPA 269 or TFDP 169.
prerequisites_text: CRWT 164C/TFDP 164C or TFDP 166C; consent of instructor is required for students repeating the course

subject: TFDP
title: Performance in Production
description: Students act in full productions. Students are cast in roles and throughout the rehearsal period are taught by the director how to perform their assigned roles in a professional manner. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 32 units.
prerequisites_text: permission by department

subject: TFDP
title: Technical Production
description: Provides training to serve in various capacities on theatre or film production crews. Includes work in assigned crew positions on departmental productions during pre-production, rehearsals, performances, and post-production. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 32 units.
prerequisites_text: permission by department

subject: TFDP
title: Design in Production
description: Provides training to be a designer on theatre or film productions. Includes work with a mentor designer on departmental productions throughout pre-production, production, and post-production. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 32 units.
prerequisites_text: permission by department

subject: TFDP
title: Management and Directing in Production
description: Provides training to become stage managers, production managers, and directors on theatre and film productions. Includes attending production meetings, rehearsals, and performances of departmental productions. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 32 units.
prerequisites_text: permission by department

subject: TFDP
title: Writing and Dramaturgy in Production
description: Provides training to write scripts or serve as a dramaturge on theatre and film productions. Includes working with a mentor on departmental productions during the pre-production process and attending some rehearsals and performances. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 32 units.
prerequisites_text: permission by department

subject: TFDP
title: Fabrication in Production
description: Teaches fabrication while working in the scene shop, costume shop, or the lighting/sound shop during the build process of theatre or film productions. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 32 units.
prerequisites_text: permission by department

subject: TFDP
title: Performing Arts of Asia
description: A survey of music, dance, theatre, and ritual in four major geocultural regions of Asia: Central, East, South and Southeast. No Western music training is required. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units. Cross-listed with ANTH 128, AST 128, and DNCE 128.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Staging the Middle East
description: Examines the ways in which theatre, performance, and film engage with and critique the representations of peoples and cultures of the Middle East. Includes films and plays from the region as well as the work of Americans representing the Middle East. Credit is awarded for only one of TFDP 177 or TFDP 177S.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Staging the Middle East
description: Examines the ways in which theatre, performance, and film engage with and critique the representations of peoples and cultures of the Middle East. Includes films and plays from the region as well as the work of Americans representing the Middle East. Credit is awarded for only one of TFDP 177 or TFDP 177S.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: (E-Z) Theatre Practicum
description: An investigation of theatrical production theories and practices. E. Contemporary Mexican Theatre; F. Musical Comedy; M. Arts Management; Q. Plays In Progress; R. New Plays; S. Improvisation.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: TFDP
title: Arts, Management, and Community
description: An introduction to business and arts management including the study of film and television production, stage management, and music production. Offers hands-on experience for practicing management skills working in partnership with local organizations and artists of Riverside and the Inland Empire. Cross-listed with MUS 185. Credit is awarded for only one of MUS 185/TFDP 185 or MUS 185S/TFDP 185S.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Arts, Management, and Community
description: An introduction to business and arts management including the study of film and television production, stage management, and music production. Offers hands-on experience for practicing management skills working in partnership with local organizations and artists of Riverside and the Inland Empire. Cross-listed with MUS 185S. Credit is awarded for only one of MUS 185/ TFDP 185 or MUS 185S/TFDP 185S.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, and Mixed Reality Design and Production
description: Topics include historical examples of immersive technologies, VR/AR/MR projects, the social impact of VR/ AR/MR concepts and projects, and the broader impact on society.
prerequisites_text: TFDP 020, TFDP 066; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: TFDP
title: Special Studies
description: Independent study and research by qualified undergraduate students under supervision of a faculty member. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 20 units.
prerequisites_text: consent of the chair of the department

subject: TFDP
title: (E-Z) Seminar in Theatre
description: Covers various topics on a rotating basis. Includes playwriting, acting, directing, scenic design, theatre history, and dramatic literature. E. Hamlet: Who Is Hamlet And Why Should You Care?; M. American Frontier In American Drama; N. Theatre Of Eugene O' S. Script To Production; T. Women In Theatre: Theory And Performance.

subject: TFDP
title: Senior Thesis
description: Open by invitation only Presentation of a significant piece of creative work with faculty supervision. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: senior standing; consent of Department Chair

subject: TFDP
title: Individual Internship in Theatre
description: An internship in a theatre, television, or film production company. Includes work with directors or designers in one or more areas of professional production such as acting, design, costumes, lighting, and sound. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units.

subject: TFDP
title: Senior Research
description: Research in the practice and/or theory of the theatre. Open to seniors by invitation only. University Honors
prerequisites_text: consent of chair of the department

subject: UCDC
title: Special Topics in Political Science
description: Addresses topics in Political Science from the perspective of politics in Washington, D.C. Topics vary each term and may be viewed at https://www.ucdc.edu. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

description: Addresses topics in business and economics from the perspective of Washington, D.C. Topics vary each term, and may be viewed at https:// www.ucdc.edu. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.

description: Addresses topics in media and communications from the perspective of Washington, D.C. Topics vary each term and may be viewed at https://www.ucdc.edu. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.

title: Special Topics in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics
description: Addresses topics in the natural sciences, technology, engineering, and mathematics from the perspective of Washington, D.C. Topics vary each term and may be viewed at https:// www.ucdc.edu. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Washington Special Topics
description: Addresses topics relevant to Washington, D.C. from an interdisciplinary or non-disciplinary perspective. Topics vary each term and may be viewed at https://www.ucdc.edu. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar For General Research
description: Complements the internship experience of participants in the UCDC program by connecting their internship experience to a focused research project. Guides students through the process of conducting focused and detailed research. For more course information, visit https://www. ucdc.edu. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar On Congress
description: Explores how Congress works including representation of constituents, congressional elections, internal rules, the role of parties, executive branch relations, and policymaking. Complements the experiences of UCDC Capitol Hill interns. Provides guidance through the process of conducting focused and detailed research. For more course information, visit https://www. ucdc.edu. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar On the Presidency and Executive Branch
description: Examines American presidential leadership and the evolving role of the presidency in American culture. Introduces major thematic debates that define presidential politics. Complements experiences of UCDC interns in the Executive Branch. Provides guidance through the process of conducting focused and detailed research. For more course information, visit https://www. ucdc.edu. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar in Environmental Policy
description: Covers theoretical perspectives and methodological approaches used in determining the environmental sustainability of various public policies. Complements interns whose experiences relate to the environment by connecting and guiding through a focused and detailed research project. For more course information, visit https://www.ucdc.edu. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar in International Policy
description: Investigates the complex policy community (governmental, non-governmental, and intergovernmental actors) that engages in forging international policy. Complements students whose internships relate to foreign policy by connecting their internship experience to a focused and detailed research project. For more course information, visit https://www. ucdc.edu. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar On the Washington Media
description: Explores the rapidly changing relationship between the news media, political communication, and governing. Complements interns whose experiences relate to the media by connecting to a focused and detailed research project. For more course information, visit https://www. ucdc.edu. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar On the Arts in Washington
description: Addresses how the arts function in American institutions and society as well as how to improve on this constantly shifting interface. Complements interns with experiences in the arts by connecting to a focused and detailed research project. For more course information, visit https://www.ucdc.edu. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar in Health Policy
description: Honors course corresponding to UCDC 191H. Examines the shape of the U.S. healthcare system and the trail of public health care policies. Complements interns who experiences relate to health care by connecting to a focused and detailed research project. For more course information, visit https://www.ucdc.edu.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar On the United States Supreme Court
description: Introduces the Supreme Court of the United States as a legal, political, and cultural institution. Complements interns whose experiences relate to law and the courts by connecting to a focused and detailed research project. For more course information, visit https://www.ucdc. edu. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Seminar in Washington, D.C.
description: Examines aspects of the Washington, D.C., area including cultural, political, and governmental institutions as well as the sciences, arts, and media. Includes guided independent work drawing on the unique aspects of Washington, D.C. For more course information, visit https://www.ucdc. edu. Satisfactory(S) or No Credit(N/C) is not available.
prerequisites_text: admission to the UC Washington Center (UCDC) Academic Internship Program; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UCDC
title: Experiential Learning in Washington Dc
description: An examination of the multifaceted nature of Washington, DC by exploring the city’s history, politics, and identity. Examines the perspectives of residents, political actors, visitors, and the global community. Promotes application of concepts covered in course materials to assigned internship sites. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units. Cell Biology and Neuroscience
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; acceptance into the UCDC program

subject: UGRC
title: R’Course Proposal Development
description: Focuses on the development of R’Course proposals with pedagogical strategy and quality course design. Topics include the principles of democratic pedagogy and active learning. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 2 units.
prerequisites_text: excludes graduate students; permission by department

subject: UGRC
title: Democratic Pedagogy
description: Focuses on the development and practice of teaching skills in preparation for R’Course facilitation. Topics include course delivery, assessment, and lesson design with attention to the principles of democratic pedagogy and active learning. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: UGRC 001A with a grade of S or better; excludes graduate students; requires an approved R’Course proposal

subject: UGRC
title: Teaching Rcourses
description: Provides strategic support for R’Course facilitators with a focus on incorporating effective teaching strategies in course deployment. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 6 units.
prerequisites_text: UGRC 001B with a grade of S or better; excludes graduate students; must be teaching an approved R’Course; and consent of instructor

subject: UGRC
title: R’courses : Variable Topics
description: Student-initiated courses designed by undergraduates and taken by other UCR undergraduates. Covers original course topics that are unique from other departmental course offerings. Topics vary each quarter. Includes working closely with a faculty mentor and R’Course staff to develop and refine course offerings. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 8 units.
prerequisites_text: excludes graduate students

subject: UGRD
title: Foundations For Academic Advancement and Career Preparedness
description: Introduces career preparedness and provides practical strategies for career exploration and principles for networking-workforce success. Explores effective forms of written and professional communication.

subject: UGRD
title: Foundations For Effective Oral Communication
description: Introduces practical oral communication and public speaking skills that are necessary for networking, workforce success, and creating a professional profile.

subject: UGRD
title: R Excellence: How Bold Hearts and Brilliant Minds Are Made
description: Offers an opportunity to appreciate the range of academic experiences provided at UCR. Includes presentations from faculty to provide opportunity to reflect on lessons learned.

subject: UGRD
title: Contemporary Topics in Information and Society
description: Explores the impacts of information systems and legal and ethical issues surrounding information within a disciplinary or professional context. Introduces the principles of information literacy and provides preparation to find, evaluate, and integrate information in coursework, professional settings, and their lives. Course is repeatable as content or topic changes to a maximum of 4 units.

subject: UGRD
title: Military Science: Introduction to the Army
description: Introduces the Army Leadership Requirements Model and the Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC) program. Teaches basic soldier skills to survive in a field environment. Promotes development as Army leaders.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of freshman; and consent of instructor

subject: UGRD
title: Exploring Pathways to Graduate and Professional School
description: Focuses on long-term strategies and skills required to be successful in academic and professional pathways. Topics include writing application materials, a plan of action for applying for graduate and professional schools, and opportunities for collaboration to create sustainable career goals.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UGRD
title: Advanced Communication Skills For Academic and Personal Success
description: Focuses on advanced oral communication skills, specifically the ability to craft and present compelling and competitive personal oral narratives for graduate school, research opportunities, or industry positions.
prerequisites_text: none; restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: UGRD
title: Transfer Success Program Transfer Transition & Succes
description: Offers incoming transfer students an opportunity to gain the necessary skills for a seamless transition into the campus community. Presentations by guest speakers and hands-on experience with campus resources aid students in becoming familiar with campus resources and achieving academic and personal success. Offered in Summer only.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, or junior

subject: UGRD
title: Group Internship
description: On-or off-campus internship work in an industry, community organization, school district, or non-profit. Conducted under the joint direction of an on- or off-campus supervisor and a Division of Undergraduate Education faculty member. Course is repeatable to a maximum of 16 units. University Writing Program
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior

subject: URST
title: Popular Musics of the World
description: Introduction to issues surrounding popular and urban musics of the world focusing on three major geocultural areas: Africa, Asia, and the Americas. Emphasizes the relationship between mass-mediated music and issues of cultural hegemony, resistance, and subversion. Analyzes the cultural impact of media technology on music performance and reception. Cross-listed with ETST 014, and MUS 014.

subject: URST
title: Introduction to the Built Environment: Suburbia
description: Introduces the history of suburbia from the Industrial Revolution to the present. Includes the rise of suburbs in England; classic suburbs in the United States; the spread of suburbs and mass transportation; the role of race and gender in suburbia; suburban sprawl in Southern California; and sustainability and suburban development. Cross-listed with MCS 025.

subject: URST
title: The Politics of Public Space
description: Introduces theories and history of public space in modern cities. Topics include public space during the Industrial Revolution; modern planning and urban renewal; political uses of public space including demonstrations and occupations; privatization and policing of public spaces; and changing concepts of public and private space in contemporary society. Cross-listed with MCS 069.

subject: URST
title: Urban Sociology
description: A comparative examination of metropolitan and other urban communities with emphasis on processes of urbanization. Cross-listed with SOC 143.
prerequisites_text: SOC 001 or SOC 001H; or consent of instructor

subject: URST
title: Urban Economics
description: Applies basic microeconomic principles to the spatial concentration of economic activity, the operation of the urban land, housing, transportation, and labor markets, the role of government in the urban economy, and urban economic problems, including pollution, crime, and homelessness. Cross-listed with ECON 146.
prerequisites_text: ECON 102 or ECON 104A

subject: URST
title: Race, Space, and Identity
description: Examines the intersection of race, space, and identity in modern and contemporary culture. Explores the critical and constitutive importance of race in the built environment. Topics include the racialization of space; colonialism and colonial cities; expositions and world’s fairs; segregation; race and the canon; decolonization; and urban renewal. Cross-listed with MCS 159.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: URST
title: The Modern City
description: Examines the modern metropolis from the Industrial Revolution to the present. Explores the history and theory of modern urbanism through case studies of metropolitan areas with a rich urban culture, architecture, and morphologic features. Investigates approaches to the problems of the large urban agglomeration in the context of social Cross-listed with AHS 178.
prerequisites_text: Restricted to class level standing of sophomore, junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: URST
title: Urban Problems
description: An interdisciplinary examination of selected urban problems such as civil disorders, transportation, housing, welfare, and planning. Cross-listed with PBPL 182, and SOC 182. Credit is awarded for one of the following PBPL 182, SOC 182, URST 182, or PBPL 178.
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: URST
title: Modern Architecture
description: Explores modern architecture and its sources from 1800 to the present. Cross-listed with AHS 184.
prerequisites_text: sophomore, junior, or senior standing; or consent of instructor

subject: VNM
title: Elementary Vietnamese
description: 4 hours. An introduction to the sound system and grammar of Vietnamese. Focuses on the development of the four skills: comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing. Classes are conducted in Vietnamese as often as possible. Credit is awarded for only one of the following sequences: VNM 001, VNM 002, and VNM 003; VNM 020A and VNM 020B.
prerequisites_text: student must take the Vietnamese placement examination

subject: VNM
title: Elementary Vietnamese
description: Focuses on the development of the four skills: comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing. Classes are conducted in Vietnamese as often as possible. Credit is awarded for only one of the following sequences: VNM 001, VNM 002, and VNM 003; VNM 020A and VNM 020B.
prerequisites_text: VNM 001 with a grade of “C-” or better or equivalent or a sufficiently high test score on the Vietnamese placement examination as determined by the department faculty An introduction to the sound system and grammar of Vietnamese

subject: VNM
title: Elementary Vietnamese
