prerequisites_text: VNM 002 with a grade of “C-” or better or equivalent or a sufficiently high test score on the Vietnamese placement examination as determined by the department faculty An introduction to the sound system and grammar of Vietnamese

subject: VNM
title: Intermediate Vietnamese
description: Emphasizes further development of vocabulary, reading, writing, comprehension, and speaking skills. Provides foundation for recognizing, formulating, and articulating complex ideas.

subject: VNM
title: Intermediate Vietnamese
description: Provides foundation for recognizing, formulating, and articulating complex ideas.

subject: VNM
title: Beginning Vietnamese For Advanced Heritage Learners
description: Focuses on developing language skills and improving existing reading and writing skills. Credit is awarded for only one of the following sequences: VNM 001, VNM 002, and VNM 003; VNM 020A and VNM 020B.
prerequisites_text: Student must take the Vietnamese placement examination Structured for the heritage student at the beginning level who has advanced comprehension and some speaking skills

subject: VNM
title: Beginning Vietnamese For Advanced Heritage Learners
description: Builds upon course work covered in VNM 020A. Includes integrating situational lessons with vocabulary, sentence patterns, grammar, and socio-linguistics used in daily life. Credit is awarded for only one of the following sequences: VNM 001, VNM 002, and VNM 003; VNM 020A and VNM 020B.
prerequisites_text: VNM 020A with a grade of “C-” or better or equivalent or a sufficiently high test score on the Vietnamese placement examination as determined by the department faculty

subject: VNM
title: Introduction to Vietnamese and Diasporic Film Culture
description: Explores the revival of film production in Vietnam following the Vietnam War. Focuses on the means of production, state control, and international distribution. Engages in critical viewing strategies and analytical visual critique. Readings are in translation; classes conducted in English. Cross-listed with AST 064, and SEAS 064.

subject: VNM
title: Advanced Vietnamese
description: Designed to develop fluency in Vietnamese to the level of intellectual conversation. Emphasis is on reading and writing of Vietnamese literature and criticism, visual culture, and discussion of current issues of Vietnamese society.
prerequisites_text: VNM 005 or equivalent or a sufficiently high test score on the Vietnamese placement examination as determined by the department faculty or consent of instructor

subject: VNM
title: Vietnamese Literary History
description: A historical analysis of Vietnamese literature from its oral tradition to contemporary fiction. Follows the formation of the nation-state and the subsequent struggles with the Chinese, French, Japanese, and Americans. No knowledge of Vietnamese required. Readings are in translation or bilingual editions. Classes are conducted in English. Cross-listed with AST 162, HIST 187, and SEAS 162.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing

subject: VNM
title: Vietnamese American Culture
description: A study of the pervasive aspects of Vietnamese American culture. Includes shared histories, acculturation patterns, class diversity, identity struggles, community-building literary and cultural production, youth issues, and cultural survival. Also introduces foundational literature, visual culture, and scholarship in the field. Cross-listed with AST 164, and SEAS 164.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: VNM
title: (E-Z) Themes in Vietnamese Literature
description: An exploration of Vietnamese literature in translation as seen through the lens of a particular theme or issue. Focuses on the implications of gender and sexuality on nation formation. All materials are read or viewed in English. E. Women And War. Cross-listed with AST 165 (E-Z), GSST 165 (E-Z), and SEAS 165 (E-Z).
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior

subject: VNM
title: Vietnam and the Philippines
description: An introduction to the comparative national histories of Vietnam and the Philippines by way of great literary works in various genres including poetry, short fiction, and novels. All materials are read in English. Cross-listed with CPLT 166, AST 166, and SEAS 166.
prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor

subject: VNM
title: The Vietnam Wars
description: An introduction to Vietnamese history in the twentieth century. Covers the three Indochina wars (1945-1986) from different Vietnamese perspectives. Topics include experiences during French colonial rule; the anticolonial movements; periods of French and American military involvement up to 1975; the postwar society; and the post-doi moi society. Cross-listed with AST 160, HIST 184, and SEAS 184. Computer Engineering
prerequisites_text: restricted to class level standing of junior, or senior; or consent of instructor

subject: WRIT
title: Foundations of Academic Discourse
description: Introductory course designed for multilingual, first-generation, or other students needing intensive, multi-quarter support in academic discourse foundations in writing, reading, listening, and speaking. Focuses on reading comprehension; oral communication; sentence clarity; and academic composition, editing, and revising skills. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 001L; placement determined by the UCR Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: Foundations of Academic Discourse Laboratory
description: Reinforces foundational understanding and applications of English grammar and idiomatic expression, critical reading, and listening practice. Sets a foundation of improvement in reading comprehension, oral communication, and sentence clarity. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 2 units.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 001; placement into WRIT 001 by the University Writing Program’s Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: Fundamentals of Academic Discourse
description: Course designed for multilingual, first-generation, or other students needing support in academic discourse fundamentals. Focuses on increasing communicative competence in composing a variety of texts with special attention to the writing process, academic grammar, critical reading, and verbal skills. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 003L; WRIT 001 with a grade of S or better; special permission required to take WRIT 003 if students don’t receive an S in WRIT 001 after two attempts; or placement determined by the UCR Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: Fundamentals of Academic Discourse Laboratory
description: Reinforces fundamental understanding and applications of English grammar and idiomatic expression, critical reading, and listening practice. Sets a foundation of improvement in reading comprehension, oral communication, and sentence clarity. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 2 units.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 003; WRIT 001 with a grade of S or better; or placement into WRIT 003 by the University Writing Program’s Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: Frameworks of Academic Discourse
description: Designed for multilingual, first-generation, or other students needing focused additional support honing academic communication skills. Advances student academic discourse skills through the combined frameworks of aural, oral, and written communications; process-based composition strategies; advanced reading comprehension strategies for a variety of subjects; and rhetorical grammar. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC).
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 005L; WRIT 003 with a grade of S or better; special permission required to take WRIT 005 if students don’t receive an S in WRIT 003 after two attempts; OR Placement determined by the UCR Writing Placement Process (WPP) OR UWP Director approval

subject: WRIT
title: Frameworks of Academic Discourse Laboratory
description: Reinforces principles and applications of English grammar and idiomatic expression, critical reading, and rhetorical practice. Advances student academic discourse skills through process-based composition strategies, reading comprehension strategies for a variety of subjects, and rhetorical grammar. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 3 units.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 005; WRIT 003 with a grade of S or better; or placement into WRIT 005 by the University Writing Program’s Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: English Writing For Academic Inquiry and Exchange of Ideas
description: Helps develop reading and writing proficiency in a rigorous, process-oriented approach. Introduces writing conventions of academic communities. Provides the opportunity to write response-oriented essays and refine the mechanics of their writing. Grade of ‘C’ or better satisfies the UC ELWR.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 007L; WRIT 005 with a grade of S or better; special permission required to take WRIT 007 if students don’t receive an S in WRIT 005 before the final academic quarter in the UC Entry-Level Writing Requirement time limit or UWP Director approval; placement determined by the UCR Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: English Writing For Academic Inquiry and Exchange of Ideas Laboratory
description: Focuses on mastery of principles and applications of academic language and idiomatic expression as well as critical reading. For students who do not need, or have advanced beyond, second-language instruction. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 3 units.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 007; WRIT 005 with a grade of S or better; or placement into WRIT 007 by the University Writing Program’s Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: English Writing For Ideas in Conflict
description: Examines academic argument in significant written texts with a consideration of spoken texts. Includes reading with attention to tone, rhetoric, and evidence; writing effective and persuasive essays; writing and delivering speeches; and delivering multimodal presentations. Passing students satisfy UC ELWR and are eligible for WRIT 010 or WRIT 010S.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 008L; must be invited by the Director of the UWP based on the UCR Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: English Writing For Ideas in Conflict Laboratory
description: Focuses on mastery of principles and applications of academic language, rhetoric, and intensive critical reading with attention to tone, rhetoric, and evidence. Includes writing effective and persuasive essays, writing and delivering speeches, and delivering multimodal presentations. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 3 units.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 008; placement into WRIT 008 by the University Writing Program’s Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: Academic Writing: Intensive
description: Introduces strategies of personal writing by fostering awareness of writing and reading, encouraging the consideration of audience and conventions of genre in smaller class environments with an embedded tutor. Considers responses to different rhetorical situations. Passing students satisfy UC ELWR and are eligible for WRIT 020 or WRIT 020S. Credit is awarded for one of the following WRIT 009, WRIT 010, or WRIT 010S.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 009L; must be invited by the Director of the UWP based on the UCR Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: Academic Writing: Intensive Laboratory
description: Focuses on mastery of principles and applications of academic language and idiomatic expression, as well as critical reading, narrative structures, and initial argumentation fundamentals, for students who do not need, or have advanced beyond, second-language instruction. Graded Satisfactory (S) or No Credit (NC). Course is repeatable to a maximum of 3 units.
prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in WRIT 009; must be invited by the Director of the UWP to WRIT 009 based on the UCR Writing Placement Process (WPP)

subject: WRIT
title: Academic Writing
description: Introduces strategies of personal writing to foster awareness as a writer and reader. Encourages consideration of audience and genre conventions, responses to different rhetorical situations, and incorporation of various forms of research when engaging with academic writing that employs individual voice and style. Credit is awarded for one of the following WRIT 010, WRIT 009, or WRIT 010S.
prerequisites_text: WRIT 007 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 008 with a grade of C or better; fulfillment of the University of California Entry-Level Writing Requirement

subject: WRIT
title: Academic Writing
description: Introduces strategies of personal writing to foster awareness as a writer and reader. Encourages consideration of audience and genre conventions, responses to different rhetorical situations, and incorporation of various forms of research when engaging with academic writing that employs individual voice and style. Credit is awarded for one of the following WRIT 010S, WRIT 009, or WRIT 010.
prerequisites_text: WRIT 007 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 008 with a grade of C or better; fulfillment of the University of California Entry-Level Writing Requirement

subject: WRIT
title: Persuasive Writing
description: Emphasizes the transition from personal to public writing as students learn to apply the essential tenets of the rhetorical tradition of persuasion to various genres and develop arguments by identifying an issue, articulating a stance in relation to that issue, and defending that stance with appropriate evidence. Credit is awarded for one of the following WRIT 020 or WRIT 020S.
prerequisites_text: WRIT 010 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 010S with a grade of C or better or WRIT 009 with a grade of C or better

subject: WRIT
title: Persuasive Writing
description: Emphasizes the transition from personal to public writing as students learn to apply the essential tenets of the rhetorical tradition of persuasion to various genres and develop arguments by identifying an issue, articulating a stance in relation to that issue, and defending that stance with appropriate evidence. Lecture with sections. Credit is awarded for one of the following WRIT 020S or WRIT 020.
prerequisites_text: WRIT 010 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 010S with a grade of C or better or WRIT 009 with a grade of C or better

subject: WRIT
title: Analytical Writing
description: Addresses the function of writing in a range of contemporary situations from a critical and theoretical perspective. Includes analyzing and responding to a wide variety of texts to understand theoretical and critical models and to apply those models to texts to articulate an interpretative understanding. Credit is awarded for one of the following WRIT 030 or WRIT 030S.
prerequisites_text: WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better

subject: WRIT
title: Analytical Writing
description: Addresses the function of writing in a range of contemporary situations from a critical and theoretical perspective. Includes analyzing and responding to a wide variety of texts to understand theoretical and critical models and applying those models to texts to articulate an interpretative understanding. Credit is awarded for one of the following WRIT 030S or WRIT 030.
prerequisites_text: WRIT 020 with a grade of C or better or WRIT 020S with a grade of C or better

subject: WRIT
title: Oral Communication
description: An introduction to public speaking in genres and for occasions appropriate in the academy and in public forums. Covers classroom and seminar presentations, conference presentations including poster talks and speeches appropriate for public assemblies, debate, and special occasions. Offered in Summer only.
